sentence: Postquam pāx nūntiāta est, pater noster ex castrīs ad vīllam rediit.
translation: Once peace had been announced, our father came home from camp to the farm.

sentence: Lēgātī hostium in cūriam ingressī sunt et pācem ā senātū petīvērunt.
translation: The enemy's envoys walked into the senate house and sued the senate for peace.

sentence: Avia mea saepe dīcit sē numquam per tōtam vītam in pāce vīxisse.
translation: My grandmother often says that she has never lived in peace her whole life long.

sentence: Hodiē in hortō nōn labōrāmus; imber enim tōtam noctem sine fīne cecidit.
translation: We are not working in the garden today, for the rain came down all night without stopping.

sentence: Magister discipulōs hodiē dīmīsit; ipse enim ad forum properāre dēbēbat.
translation: The teacher let the pupils go early today, since he himself had to hurry down to the forum.

sentence: Nōlī illī mercātōrī crēdere; multōs enim in forō iam fefellit.
translation: Don't trust that merchant — he has already cheated plenty of people in the forum.

sentence: Māter pānem in mēnsā posuit et nōs statim ad cēnam vocāvit.
translation: Mother set the bread down on the table and called us straight in to dinner.

sentence: Mercātor in forō ōlīvās et vīnum vēndit, sed pretium nimis auget.
translation: The trader in the forum sells olives and wine, but he pushes the price up too far.

sentence: Fessus et īrātus domum rediī, quod nēmō mihi in forō pecūniam reddidit.
translation: I came home tired and angry, because nobody in the forum paid me back.

sentence: Avia in culīnā sedēbat et fabās in ollam lentē coniciēbat.
translation: Grandmother was sitting in the kitchen, slowly dropping beans into the pot.

sentence: Mīlitēs in castrīs pernoctāvērunt et prīmā lūce in aciem prōcessērunt.
translation: The soldiers spent the night in camp and marched out into battle line at first light.

sentence: In hāc urbe nēmō mihi cōnfīdit, itaque in patriam redīre cupiō.
translation: In this city nobody trusts me, so I long to go back to my own country.

sentence: Iānuam claudere nōn possum, quod cardō vetus rōbīgine corruptus est.
translation: I cannot shut the door, because the old hinge has been eaten away by rust.

sentence: Dominus servō nōn crēdidit, quamquam ille tōtam noctem in tabernā labōrāverat.
translation: The master did not believe the slave, although the man had worked the whole night in the shop.

sentence: Nōn timeō mortem, sed amīcōs meōs sine mē relinquere nōlō.
translation: I am not afraid of death, but I do not want to leave my friends behind without me.

sentence: Hortus noster parvus est, sed in eō pirus vetustissima adhūc frūctum fert.
translation: Our garden is small, but a very old pear tree in it still bears fruit.

sentence: Via ad forum hodiē plēna est, quia mercātōrēs nova vīna vēndunt.
translation: The road to the forum is packed today, because the traders are selling the new wines.

sentence: Difficile est amīcum monēre, quod cōnsilium nostrum audīre iam nōn vult.
translation: It is hard to warn a friend, because he no longer wants to hear our advice.

sentence: Pōma dē arbore cecidērunt, et avia ea in corbem colligēbat.
translation: The apples fell down from the tree, and grandmother was gathering them into a basket.

sentence: Senātōrēs in cūriā dē bellō Gallicō tōtum diem ācriter disputāvērunt.
translation: In the senate house the senators argued fiercely about the Gallic war all day long.

sentence: Nōlī dē mē male loquī, cum ipse eadem vitia domī tuae alās.
translation: Do not speak ill of me, when you nurse the very same faults in your own house.

sentence: Puer quī cotīdiē aquam ē puteō haurit iam manūs callōsās habet.
translation: The boy who draws water from the well every day already has calloused hands.

sentence: Mīlitēs quī prīmī mūrum ascendērunt corōnam ā duce accēpērunt.
translation: The soldiers who were first up the wall received a crown from the general.

sentence: Nēmō est quī tam grave onus sōlus ferre possit sine querellā.
translation: There is nobody who could carry so heavy a burden alone without complaining.

sentence: Tōtā nocte vigilāvī et nunc tam fessus sum ut vix stem.
translation: I lay awake all night, and now I am so tired that I can hardly stand.

sentence: Ego faber sum, nōn scrība; litterās tuās aliī legere dēbent.
translation: I am a craftsman, not a clerk; other people will have to read your letters.

sentence: Longē ā patriā sum, sed epistulae tuae mē cotīdiē cōnsōlantur.
translation: I am far from home, but your letters comfort me every day.

sentence: Ego ligna in silvā caedam; tū interim ignem in culīnā cūrā.
translation: I will cut firewood in the forest; you, meanwhile, look after the fire in the kitchen.

sentence: Quid tū in hāc tabernā quaeris, cum omnēs iam dormīre dēbeant?
translation: What are you after in this tavern, when everyone ought to be asleep by now?

sentence: Cēterī mē dēseruērunt, sed tū sōlus mēcum in perīculō mānsistī.
translation: Everyone else abandoned me, but you alone stayed with me in the danger.

sentence: Māne ad fontem eō, quod aqua domī nostrae iam dēfēcit.
translation: In the morning I go to the spring, because the water at our house has run out.

sentence: Nūntius ad castra celeriter equitāvit et epistulam ad ducem tulit.
translation: The messenger rode swiftly to the camp and brought the letter to the general.

sentence: Ad sepulcrum patris cotīdiē veniō, quia domī sine eō nihil mē dēlectat.
translation: I come to my father's tomb every day, because without him nothing at home gives me any pleasure.

sentence: Nōs sub tēctō cēnāvimus, dum imber hortum tōtam noctem verberat.
translation: We ate our dinner indoors while the rain lashed the garden the whole night.

sentence: Dominus nōs ante lūcem excitāvit et in agrōs statim mīsit.
translation: The master woke us before daylight and sent us straight out into the fields.

sentence: Nōs quidem pācem cupimus, sed dux noster bellum longius trahit.
translation: We ourselves want peace, but our commander is dragging the war out further.

sentence: Vōs, puerī, hodiē domī manēte, quia māter aegra est.
translation: You boys stay home today — your mother is ill.

sentence: Dominus vōs in agrōs mittet, nisi hodiē vīnum in cellam portāveritis.
translation: The master will send you all out to the fields unless you get the wine into the cellar today.

sentence: Nēmō vōs magis amat quam ego, quamquam saepe verba dūra dīcō.
translation: Nobody loves you more than I do, even though I often speak harshly to you.

sentence: Cum mātre meā in culīnā pānem faciō, dum pater in agrō labōrat.
translation: I make bread with my mother in the kitchen while my father works out in the field.

sentence: Cum in forum vēnissēmus, iam nūlla merx in tabernīs supererat.
translation: By the time we reached the forum, there was nothing left to buy in the shops.

sentence: Cum patre numquam dē pecūniā loquor, quia semper īrāscitur.
translation: I never talk about money with my father, because he always loses his temper.

sentence: Māter fenestram clausit, ut īnfāns in cubiculō quiētē dormīret.
translation: Mother shut the window so that the baby would sleep quietly in the bedroom.

sentence: Dux mīlitibus imperāvit ut ante lūcem castra in colle pōnerent.
translation: The general ordered the soldiers to pitch camp on the hill before daybreak.

sentence: Puella tam dulciter cantābat ut omnēs in tabernā tacērent et lacrimārent.
translation: The girl sang so sweetly that everyone in the tavern fell silent and wept.

sentence: Sī crās pluet, domī manēbimus et castaneās in focō torrēbimus.
translation: If it rains tomorrow, we'll stay in and roast chestnuts on the hearth.

sentence: Sī hodiē mercātōrī pecūniam nōn solveris, crās ante iūdicem stābis.
translation: If you don't pay the merchant today, tomorrow you'll be standing before a judge.

sentence: Sī plūs temporis habērem, tēcum ad mare libenter īrem.
translation: If I had more time, I'd gladly go down to the sea with you.

sentence: Cūr iterum lucernam ārdentem in cubiculō relīquistī, fīlia mea?
translation: Why have you left the lamp burning in the bedroom again, my girl?

sentence: Cūr tam sērō ad officīnam vēnistī, cum omnēs iam labōrent?
translation: Why have you come to the workshop so late, when everyone else is already at work?

sentence: Cūr mihi nōn crēdis, postquam tot annōs tibi fidēlis fuī?
translation: Why don't you trust me, after I've been loyal to you all these years?

sentence: Māter rogat quandō pater ex agrīs redeat, quia cēna frīgēscit.
translation: Mother is asking when father will be back from the fields, because dinner is going cold.

sentence: Quandō nāvis frūmentum ex Aegyptō in portum nostrum advehet?
translation: When is the ship going to bring the grain from Egypt into our harbour?

sentence: Quandō tandem quiēscēmus, sī cotīdiē ā prīmā lūce labōrāmus?
translation: When will we ever get any rest, if we work from first light every single day?

sentence: Puerī in hortō clāmant, quod pater eīs canem novum ēmit.
translation: The boys are shouting in the garden because their father has bought them a new dog.

sentence: Frūmentum, quod ex Siciliā vēnit, in horreō prope forum condidimus.
translation: The grain that came in from Sicily we stored in the granary near the forum.

sentence: Grātiās tibi agō quod mē in tantō perīculō nōn dēseruistī.
translation: Thank you for not abandoning me when I was in such danger.

sentence: Hic pānis iam dūrus est, sed novum in tabernā emere nōn possum.
translation: This bread has already gone hard, but I can't buy a fresh loaf at the shop.

sentence: Hic faber cotīdiē ante lūcem surgit ut fornācem accendat.
translation: This blacksmith gets up before dawn every day to light his furnace.

sentence: Hic mihi diēs longissimus vīsus est, quod nūntium tuum exspectābam.
translation: This day has felt endless to me, because I was waiting for word from you.

sentence: Senex ille, quī in angulō sedet, avum meum bene nōverat.
translation: That old man sitting over in the corner knew my grandfather well.

sentence: Ille servus ā dominō lībertātem accēpit et nunc tabernam prope portum tenet.
translation: That slave was granted his freedom by his master, and now he keeps a shop near the harbour.

sentence: Ille diēs numquam ex animō meō excidet, quō prīmum Rōmam vīdī.
translation: I will never forget that day, the day I first laid eyes on Rome.

sentence: Is puer, quem herī vīdistī, fīlius vīcīnī nostrī est.
translation: That boy you saw yesterday is our neighbour's son.

sentence: Is mercātor nimis magnum pretium poposcit, itaque nihil ēmimus.
translation: That merchant asked far too high a price, so we bought nothing.

sentence: Is sōlus mihi vērum dīxit, cum cēterī omnēs tacērent.
translation: He alone told me the truth, at a time when everyone else kept quiet.

sentence: Dum tū in ātriō dormīs, ego tōtam cēnam sōlus parō.
translation: While you sleep in the hall, I get the whole dinner ready by myself.

sentence: Crās ego in forō causam dīcam, tū autem in turbā tacēbis.
translation: Tomorrow I'll be the one pleading the case in the forum, while you stand silent in the crowd.

sentence: Omnēs magistrum timent, sed ego eum semper amāvī atque laudāvī.
translation: Everyone else is afraid of the teacher, but I have always loved and praised him.

sentence: Fēmina fessa in culīnā sedet et ancillae imperat ut pānem coquat.
translation: The tired woman sits in the kitchen and orders the maid to bake the bread.

sentence: In forō fēmina pānem emit et cum pistōre dē pretiō contendit.
translation: In the market the woman buys bread and haggles with the baker over the price.

sentence: Fēmina illa, quamquam pauper erat, omnibus vīcīnīs semper benignē subveniēbat.
translation: That woman, poor as she was, always came kindly to the help of all her neighbours.

sentence: Domina māne ancillās vocāvit et eīs clāvēs cellae vīnāriae trādidit.
translation: In the morning the mistress called the maids and handed them the keys to the wine cellar.

sentence: Dum domina in hortō ambulat, servī tōtam vīllam tacitī pūrgant.
translation: While the lady of the house takes her walk in the garden, the slaves clean the whole villa in silence.

sentence: Poēta miser dominae dūrae carmina ante iānuam clausam noctū canit.
translation: The lovesick poet sings his songs at night outside his hard-hearted mistress's locked door.

sentence: Fīlius meus tōtum diem in agrō labōrāvit et fessus domum rediit.
translation: My son worked in the field all day and came home worn out.

sentence: Fīlius senātōris hodiē togam virīlem sūmpsit et in forum dēscendit.
translation: Today the senator's son put on the toga of manhood and went down into the forum.

sentence: Māter dē fīliō suō sollicita est, quī nunc in Galliā mīlitat.
translation: The mother is sick with worry about her son, who is serving in Gaul now.

sentence: Fīlia mea prope focum sedēbat et aviae fābulam longam nārrābat.
translation: My daughter was sitting by the hearth, telling her grandmother a long story.

sentence: Crās fīlia vīcīnī nostrī nūbet iuvenī quem numquam vīdit.
translation: Tomorrow our neighbour's daughter marries a young man she has never even seen.

sentence: Fīliam meam magis quam vītam meam amō, sed saepe mē vexat.
translation: I love my daughter more than my own life, though she often drives me to distraction.

sentence: Quis iānuam tam sērō pulsat, dum tōta domus dormit?
translation: Who is knocking at the door so late, when the whole house is asleep?

sentence: Quis vestrum, ō cīvēs, hunc hominem in cūriā dēfendere audēbit?
translation: Which of you, citizens, will dare to defend this man in the senate house?

sentence: Sī quis tibi dē mē male dīxerit, nōlī statim crēdere.
translation: If anyone speaks ill of me to you, don't be quick to believe it.

sentence: Māter mea, dum pānem in furnō coquit, dē avō suō nārrābat.
translation: While she was baking bread in the oven, my mother would tell stories about her grandfather.

sentence: Māter puerī aegrī medicum per tōtam Subūram anxia quaesīvit.
translation: The sick boy's mother searched the whole Subura for a doctor, frantic with worry.

sentence: Māter mea numquam clāmāvit, sed oculīs sōlīs mē reprehendēbat.
translation: My mother never raised her voice; she could scold me with a look alone.

sentence: Frāter minor meus tōtam noctem in cubiculō meō stertit.
translation: My little brother snores all night long in my bedroom.

sentence: Frāter meus in legiōne septimā decem annōs in Germāniā mīlitāvit.
translation: My brother served ten years with the Seventh Legion in Germany.

sentence: Frātrī meō semper cōnfīdō, quamquam mē dē pecūniā saepe dēcēpit.
translation: I always trust my brother, even though he has often cheated me over money.

sentence: Amīcus meus hodiē ad cēnam vēnit et vīnum optimum attulit.
translation: A friend of mine came to dinner today and brought an excellent wine along.

sentence: In thermīs amīcum veterem cōnspexī, quem vīgintī annōs nōn vīderam.
translation: At the baths I spotted an old friend I hadn't seen for twenty years.

sentence: Vērus amīcus nōn in convīviō sed in perīculō semper appāret.
translation: A true friend shows himself not at the dinner party but in a crisis.

sentence: Hodiē aut ad forum ībimus aut domī tōtum diem manēbimus.
translation: Today we'll either go down to the market or stay at home the whole day.

sentence: Aut mercātōrī pecūniam statim solve aut nāvem in portū āmittēmus.
translation: Either pay the merchant right now, or we lose our ship in the harbour.

sentence: Vir bonus aut vēra dīcit aut omnīnō tacet; medium nihil est.
translation: A good man either tells the truth or says nothing at all; there is no middle way.

sentence: Fenestram claude, nam ventus frīgidus tōtam casam iam implēvit.
translation: Shut the window — the cold wind has already filled the whole house.

sentence: Servum in forum mīsī, nam pater hodiē pānem emere oblītus est.
translation: I sent the slave to the forum, because father forgot to buy bread today.

sentence: Nēminī crēdō in hāc urbe, nam amīcus meus mē herī prōdidit.
translation: I trust nobody in this city, for my own friend betrayed me yesterday.

sentence: Cēna frīget et hospitēs sērō veniunt; focum igitur iterum accendō.
translation: The dinner is going cold and the guests are late, so I am lighting the hearth again.

sentence: Mercātor pretium nimis auxit; aliam igitur tabernam in forō quaerēmus.
translation: The trader has raised his price too far, so we will look for another shop in the forum.

sentence: Nēmō mihi respondit; sōlus igitur in hāc tenebrōsā viā manēre timeō.
translation: Nobody answered me, and so I am afraid to stay alone on this dark street.

sentence: Fīlia mea numerōs iam bene tenet; ergō eī librum maiōrem ēmī.
translation: My daughter has a good grip on numbers now, so I bought her a bigger book.

sentence: Nāvis in portū nōndum appulit; ergō mercēs crās in forō vēndēmus.
translation: The ship has not docked yet, so we will sell the goods in the forum tomorrow.

sentence: Nūllam epistulam mihi mīsistī; ergō tē meī oblītum esse putābam.
translation: You sent me no letter at all, so I assumed you had forgotten me.

sentence: Tōtam noctem tonuit, nec quisquam in casā nostrā dormīre potuit.
translation: It thundered the whole night, and nobody in our house could get any sleep.

sentence: Dominus mercēdem nōn solvit nec servīs satis cibī dedit.
translation: The master did not pay the wages, nor did he give the slaves enough food.

sentence: Frāter meus nec scrībit nec domum revenit, et māter cotīdiē dolet.
translation: My brother neither writes nor comes home, and mother grieves over it every day.

sentence: Cēnam parābō vel ex ovīs vel ex pisce quem hodiē ēmī.
translation: I will make dinner either out of the eggs or out of the fish I bought today.

sentence: Sī pluet, sub porticū vel in tabernā tē exspectābō ad merīdiem.
translation: If it rains, I will wait for you under the colonnade or in the shop at midday.

sentence: Vel hīc manē vel mēcum Rōmam venī; utrumque mihi placet.
translation: Either stay here or come to Rome with me — either one suits me.

sentence: In cellā ūnus pānis mānsit, et quīnque puerī ēsurientēs exspectant.
translation: One loaf is left in the pantry, and five hungry boys are waiting.

sentence: Ūnus ex mīlitibus portam custōdiēbat, cēterī in castrīs dormiēbant.
translation: One of the soldiers was guarding the gate while the rest slept in the camp.

sentence: Ūnum tantum amīcum habeō, sed eī omnia mea sēcrēta crēdō.
translation: I have only one friend, but I trust him with every secret I have.

sentence: Nisi ignem statim accendis, tōta casa hāc nocte frīgēbit.
translation: Unless you light the fire right now, the whole house will be freezing tonight.

sentence: Nēmō in cūriam intrāre poterat nisi senātor aut eius scrība.
translation: Nobody could go into the senate house except a senator or his secretary.

sentence: Nihil mihi relinquētur nisi dolor, sī frāter tuus agrōs vēndiderit.
translation: Nothing will be left to me but grief if your brother sells the fields.

sentence: Trēs ollae in culīnā frāctae sunt, et coquus īrātus discessit.
translation: Three pots got broken in the kitchen, and the cook stormed out in a rage.

sentence: Trēs mercātōrēs ex Aegyptō vēnērunt et vīnum nostrum omne ēmērunt.
translation: Three traders came from Egypt and bought up every last jar of our wine.

sentence: Trēs annōs tē exspectāvī, sed nūllam epistulam umquam mīsistī.
translation: I waited three years for you, and you never once sent a letter.

sentence: Dum māter in culīnā pānem coquit, puerī ova in hortō quaerunt.
translation: While mother is baking bread in the kitchen, the boys are hunting for eggs in the garden.

sentence: Mīlitēs sub arboribus manēbant dum imperātor signum proeliī daret.
translation: The soldiers stayed under the trees until the general should give the signal for battle.

sentence: Dum tū in Graeciā studēbās, ego hīc sōlus patrem aegrum cūrābam.
translation: All the while you were studying in Greece, I was here alone nursing our sick father.

sentence: Nunc tandem domī sedeō, sed herī tōtum diem in agrīs labōrāvī.
translation: Now at last I am sitting at home, but yesterday I worked all day in the fields.

sentence: Ōlim hīc taberna stābat; nunc mūrus sōlus in viā manet.
translation: A shop once stood here; now only a wall is left standing on the street.

sentence: Diū tacuī, sed nunc tibi vērum dīcere tandem cōnstituī.
translation: I kept quiet for a long time, but now I have finally decided to tell you the truth.

sentence: In hortō sedēmus ubi avia mea rosās sēvit.
translation: We sit in the garden where my grandmother planted her roses.

sentence: Ubi tabernam invēnistī in quā vīnum tam vīle vēndunt?
translation: Where did you find a shop that sells wine so cheap?

sentence: Ubi prīmum Rōmam vēnī, tantam turbam numquam anteā vīderam.
translation: The first time I came to Rome, I had never seen such a crowd before.

sentence: Avia mea pānem sīc coquit ut tōta domus bene oleat.
translation: My grandmother bakes bread in such a way that the whole house smells wonderful.

sentence: Nēmō in tabernā sīc respondet dominō, nisi discēdere vult.
translation: Nobody in the shop answers the boss like that, unless he wants to be out of a job.

sentence: Sīc semper agunt superbī, quī nēminem praeter sē amant.
translation: That is how arrogant people always behave — they love no one but themselves.

sentence: Ita vehementer pluēbat ut nēmō ex casā exīre audēret.
translation: It was raining so hard that nobody dared to step out of the cottage.

sentence: Fabrī mūrum ita exstrūxērunt ut per centum annōs stāret.
translation: The builders put up the wall so well that it stood for a hundred years.

sentence: Ita mē terruit ille clāmor ut per tōtam noctem dormīre nōn possem.
translation: That shout frightened me so badly that I could not sleep the whole night.

sentence: Māter mea valdē īrāta est quod fenestram pilā frēgī.
translation: My mother is furious because I broke the window with a ball.

sentence: Dominus noster valdē laudāvit puerum quī equōs tam dīligenter cūrāverat.
translation: Our master praised the boy warmly for looking after the horses so carefully.

sentence: Valdē timeō nē frāter meus iter per montēs hieme suscipiat.
translation: I am very much afraid my brother will set out through the mountains in winter.

sentence: Nōn habeō satis farīnae ut pānem tōtī familiae coquam.
translation: I do not have enough flour to bake bread for the whole household.

sentence: Puer in lūdō satis dīligenter scrīpsit ut magister eum laudāret.
translation: The boy wrote carefully enough at school for the teacher to praise him.

sentence: Satis diū tacuī; nunc omnia quae sēnsī dīcam.
translation: I have held my tongue long enough; now I will say everything I felt.

sentence: Coquus noster bene cēnam parāvit, quamquam paene nihil in culīnā remanēbat.
translation: Our cook put together a good dinner, even though there was almost nothing left in the kitchen.

sentence: Medicus vulnus tam bene cūrāvit ut mīles post mēnsem ambulāret.
translation: The doctor treated the wound so well that the soldier was walking a month later.

sentence: Bene mēcum agitur, quia amīcī meī omnēs incolumēs ex bellō rediērunt.
translation: Things are going well for me, because all my friends came home safe from the war.

sentence: Tam male dormīvī ut māne caput mihi vehementer dolēret.
translation: I slept so badly that in the morning my head was pounding.

sentence: Scrība nōmina male scrīpsit, itaque dominus tōtum librum corrigere coāctus est.
translation: The clerk wrote the names down badly, so the master had to correct the whole ledger.

sentence: Male dē amīcō meō locūtus es; huius reī numquam oblīvīscar.
translation: You spoke badly about my friend, and I will never forget it.

sentence: Soror mea magis canēs quam fēlēs amat, itaque duōs catulōs ēmit.
translation: My sister likes dogs more than cats, so she bought two puppies.

sentence: Cotīdiē magis labōrāmus, sed mercēs nostra numquam crēscit.
translation: Every day we work harder, and yet our wages never go up.

sentence: Quō diūtius in urbe manēbam, eō magis rūs dēsīderābam.
translation: The longer I stayed in the city, the more I missed the countryside.

sentence: Hōc annō minus lignī comparāvimus, itaque tōtā hieme frīgus passī sumus.
translation: This year we laid in less firewood, so we were cold all winter long.

sentence: In officīnā nunc minus labōrāmus, quia magister multōs operāriōs dīmīsit.
translation: We work fewer hours in the workshop now, because the foreman let many of the men go.

sentence: Minus timeō mortem quam dēdecus, quod tōtam familiam meam opprimet.
translation: I fear death less than disgrace, which will crush my entire family.

sentence: Liber meus sub lectō iacēbat, ubi eum canis noster trāxerat.
translation: My book was lying under the bed, where our dog had dragged it.

sentence: Amīcōs meōs in forum dūxī ut novam tabernam nostram vidērent.
translation: I took my friends down to the forum so they could see our new shop.

sentence: Parva domus mea mihi cārior est quam tōta urbs Rōma.
translation: My little house means more to me than the whole city of Rome.

sentence: Avia mea ab hortō rediēns cerasa in gremiō portābat.
translation: My grandmother, coming back from the garden, was carrying cherries in her lap.

sentence: Mīlitēs ab imperātōre iussī sunt pontem ante lūcem incendere.
translation: The soldiers were ordered by the general to burn the bridge before dawn.

sentence: Ab illō diē quō pater discessit, nihil in vīllā manet ut anteā.
translation: Since the day my father left, nothing in the house has been the same.

sentence: Prō cēnā hospes noster fābulās dē Aegyptō nōbīs tōtā nocte nārrābat.
translation: In return for his dinner our guest told us stories about Egypt all night long.

sentence: Ōrātor prō amīcō innocentī apud iūdicēs tōtum diem ācriter dīxit.
translation: The advocate argued fiercely before the judges all day on behalf of his innocent friend.

sentence: Prō patriā mortuōs hodiē in forō magnō silentiō honōrāmus.
translation: Today in the forum we honour in deep silence those who died for their country.

sentence: Pater fīliō nātō nōmen avī suī magnō cum gaudiō imposuit.
translation: When his son was born, the father joyfully gave him his own grandfather's name.

sentence: Mercātor quīdam nōmine Lūcius ad portum hodiē trēs nāvēs mīsit.
translation: A merchant by the name of Lucius sent three ships down to the harbour today.

sentence: Nōminis eius oblīvīscī nōn possum, quamquam iam multī annī praeteriērunt.
translation: I cannot forget her name, even though many years have gone by since then.

sentence: Avus meus tōtam vītam in eōdem agellō prope flūmen ēgit.
translation: My grandfather spent his whole life on the same little plot beside the river.

sentence: Medicus tōtā nocte vigilāvit et puerī aegrī vītam tandem servāvit.
translation: The doctor stayed awake all night and in the end saved the sick boy's life.

sentence: Vīta hominum brevis est, sed labor bonus post nōs manet.
translation: Human life is short, but good work stays behind after we are gone.

sentence: Māter inter ollās et patinās in culīnā clāvem perditam quaerēbat.
translation: Mother was hunting for the lost key among the pots and pans in the kitchen.

sentence: Inter mercātōrēs in forō dē pretiō frūmentī ācris contentiō orta est.
translation: A sharp quarrel broke out among the traders in the forum over the price of grain.

sentence: Inter tot amīcōs sōlum tē vērē fīdum esse sentiō.
translation: Out of so many friends, I feel that you alone are truly loyal.

sentence: Post tempestātem nocturnam aqua per rīmās tēctī in cubiculum stillābat.
translation: After the night's storm, water dripped through the cracks in the roof into the bedroom.

sentence: Post templum vetus taberna parva pānem calidum cotīdiē māne vēndit.
translation: Behind the old temple a little shop sells warm bread every morning.

sentence: Post tot annōs in exsiliō patriam meam vix agnōvī cum revēnī.
translation: After so many years in exile I barely recognised my homeland when I came back.

sentence: Sacerdōs prō animā avī nostrī in ārā parvum sacrificium fēcit.
translation: The priest made a small offering at the altar for our grandfather's soul.

sentence: Philosophus in hortō docēbat animam corpore solūtam ad astra volāre.
translation: In the garden the philosopher taught that the soul, once freed from the body, flies to the stars.

sentence: Mīles vulnerātus in campō iacēns animam inter amīcōs efflāvit.
translation: The wounded soldier, lying out on the field, breathed his last among his friends.

sentence: Ante cēnam semper manūs aquā tepidā in ātriō lavāre solēmus.
translation: Before dinner we always wash our hands with warm water in the hall.

sentence: Ante templum Sāturnī tabellārius nōs ā prīmā lūce exspectābat.
translation: In front of the temple of Saturn the courier had been waiting for us since first light.

sentence: Ante bellum hic pāgus laetus erat, nunc autem omnia silent.
translation: Before the war this village was a cheerful place; now everything is silent.

sentence: Hodiē sine sale coquere dēbuī, quia omnēs tabernae clausae erant.
translation: Today I had to cook without any salt, because all the shops were shut.

sentence: Sine testibus iūdex causam tuam crās audīre nōn poterit.
translation: Without witnesses the judge will not be able to hear your case tomorrow.

sentence: Sine ūllā spē epistulam eius per tōtam hiemem exspectābam.
translation: With no hope left, I went on waiting for her letter the whole winter.

sentence: Fēlēs nostra sub lectō sē cēlat quotiēns tonitrua audit.
translation: Our cat hides under the bed every time she hears thunder.

sentence: Subitō imber cecidit et mercātōrēs omnēs sub porticum cucurrērunt.
translation: Rain came down suddenly and all the traders ran in under the colonnade.

sentence: Sub eādem arbore, ubi puerī lūsimus, nunc senēs sedēmus.
translation: Under the same tree where we played as boys, we now sit as old men.

sentence: Nocte in tablīnō ad lūcernam scrībō, quia diē clāmōribus vexor.
translation: I write at night in the study by lamplight, because in the daytime the shouting wears me down.

sentence: Amīcō Rōmae manentī dē messe scrībō, sed tabellārius nōndum vēnit.
translation: I am writing to a friend who is staying in Rome about the harvest, but the courier still has not turned up.

sentence: Dē puellā versūs scrībō, sed māne cēram īrātus dēleō.
translation: I write verses about the girl, then in the morning I angrily rub the wax smooth again.

sentence: In hortō sedēns Vergilium post cēnam clārā vōce legō.
translation: Sitting in the garden after dinner, I read Vergil aloud.

sentence: Epistulam frātris in forō legō et manūs mihi tremunt.
translation: I read my brother's letter in the forum and my hands start shaking.

sentence: Ex tot candidātīs ūnum legō, quem fidēlissimum esse putō.
translation: Out of so many candidates I pick the one I think is the most loyal.

sentence: Hieme ad focum cum avō sedeō dum fābulās veterēs nārrat.
translation: In winter I sit by the hearth with my grandfather while he tells his old stories.

sentence: Tōtum diem in forō sedeō dum iūdex sententiam dīcit.
translation: I sit in the forum the whole day while the judge delivers his verdict.

sentence: Cēterīs labōrantibus, ego in umbrā ōtiōsus sedeō et pudet mē.
translation: While everyone else is working, I sit idle in the shade, and I am ashamed of it.

sentence: Ante lūcem prō tabernā pistōris stō et pānem exspectō.
translation: Before daybreak I stand outside the baker's shop waiting for bread.

sentence: Inter clientēs in ātriō patrōnī hōrās multās stō.
translation: I stand for hours among the clients in my patron's entrance hall.

sentence: Quamquam omnēs mē reprehendunt, prō patre meō firmus stō.
translation: Although everyone criticises me, I stand firmly on my father's side.

sentence: Ubi māter clāvēs cēlet bene sciō, sed tacēre mālō.
translation: I know perfectly well where mother hides the keys, but I would rather say nothing.

sentence: Nāvem regere bene sciō, quod inter nautās puer crēvī.
translation: I know how to steer a ship, because I grew up among sailors as a boy.

sentence: Sciō tē mihi semper fidēlem fuisse, ideō nēminī crēdō.
translation: I know that you have always been loyal to me, and that is why I trust no one else.

sentence: Fēlēs super trabem sedet et fūmum ex culīnā vītat.
translation: The cat perches up on the beam and keeps clear of the smoke from the kitchen.

sentence: Vēlum super theātrum tenditur nē spectātōrēs sōle vexentur.
translation: An awning is stretched over the theatre so that the audience is not tormented by the sun.

sentence: Aquila super aciem volat, et mīlitēs deōs adesse crēdunt.
translation: An eagle flies over the battle line, and the soldiers believe the gods are with them.

sentence: Dormīre volō, sed vīcīnī tōtā nocte in viā clāmant.
translation: I want to sleep, but the neighbours shout out in the street all night long.

sentence: Volō fīlium meum Rōmae rhētoricam discere, quamquam pecūnia deest.
translation: I want my son to study rhetoric at Rome, even though the money is not there.

sentence: Nihil magis volō quam cum uxōre in agrō quiētē vīvere.
translation: There is nothing I want more than to live quietly with my wife out on the farm.

sentence: Māter herbās contrā febrem coquit et mē bibere cōgit.
translation: Mother boils up herbs against the fever and makes me drink them.

sentence: In cūriā contrā lēgem novam ācriter dīxī, sed victus sum.
translation: In the senate house I spoke fiercely against the new law, but I lost the vote.

sentence: Contrā voluntātem patris uxōrem dūxī, et numquam mē paenituit.
translation: I married against my father's wishes, and I have never once regretted it.

sentence: Quamquam tōtā nocte pluit, ad forum tamen māne prōcessī.
translation: Although it rained the whole night, I still set out for the market at first light.

sentence: Puer litterās tardē discit; dīligentiam tamen magister semper laudat.
translation: The boy is slow at learning his letters; even so, the teacher always praises how hard he tries.

sentence: Omnēs amīcī eum dēseruērunt; ego tamen numquam dēseram.
translation: All his friends have abandoned him; I, however, never will.

sentence: Avia quoque nōbīscum ad mare īre cupit, quamquam aegra est.
translation: Grandmother wants to come down to the sea with us as well, even though she is unwell.

sentence: Pistor quoque pretium pānis auxit, postquam frūmentum cārius factum est.
translation: The baker too has put up the price of bread, now that grain has become dearer.

sentence: Ego quoque, cum iuvenis essem, hōs lūdōs magnopere amābam.
translation: I loved these games enormously myself, back when I was a young man.

sentence: Cum māter pānem coquit, odōrem per tōtam domum vagantem amō.
translation: When my mother bakes bread, I love the smell drifting through the whole house.

sentence: Magister noster sevērus est, sed fābulās quās dē Homērō nārrat valdē amō.
translation: Our teacher is strict, but I really love the stories he tells about Homer.

sentence: Patriam meam amō, quamquam nunc procul ā Rōmā in castrīs hiemō.
translation: I love my country, though right now I am wintering in camp far from Rome.

sentence: Ex fenestrā cubiculī meī tōtum forum et templum Iovis videō.
translation: From my bedroom window I can see the whole forum and the temple of Jupiter.

sentence: Nūllum in tabernā hominem videō; omnēs ad theātrum iam abiērunt.
translation: I don't see a soul in the shop; they have all gone off to the theatre already.

sentence: Nunc dēmum videō mē hominī perfidō nimium crēdidisse.
translation: Only now do I see that I trusted a treacherous man far too much.

sentence: Domī duōs canēs habeō, quī noctū omnēs vīcīnōs lātrātū excitant.
translation: At home I have two dogs that wake all the neighbours at night with their barking.

sentence: Hodiē in cūriā ōrātiōnem dē frūmentō habeō, et manūs mihi tremunt.
translation: Today I am giving a speech about the grain supply in the senate house, and my hands are shaking.

sentence: Tē amīcum habeō, etsī nūper multa aspera inter nōs dicta sunt.
translation: I count you as a friend, even though harsh words passed between us recently.

sentence: Ex paucīs ōvīs et vetere cāseō cēnam faciō, quia nihil aliud in cellā superest.
translation: I am making dinner out of a few eggs and some old cheese, because nothing else is left in the pantry.

sentence: Fossam circum castra cum commīlitōnibus faciō, quamquam sōl ardet.
translation: I am digging a ditch around the camp with my fellow soldiers, even though the sun is blazing.

sentence: Nihil sine tuō cōnsiliō faciō, quia tibi plūs quam mihi crēdō.
translation: I do nothing without your advice, because I trust you more than I trust myself.

sentence: Fīliae meae carmen dē Aenēā omnī nocte ante somnum dīcō.
translation: Every night before she sleeps I recite my daughter a poem about Aeneas.

sentence: In forō causam pauperis dīcō contrā hominem potentem et superbum.
translation: In the forum I am pleading a poor man's case against someone powerful and arrogant.

sentence: Tibi semper vērum dīcō, etiam cum id audīre nōn vīs.
translation: I always tell you the truth, even when you don't want to hear it.

sentence: Māne gallīnīs frūmentum dō, deinde ōva in culīnam ferō.
translation: In the morning I give the hens their grain, then carry the eggs into the kitchen.

sentence: Discipulīs tabellās dō et eōs litterās Graecās scrībere iubeō.
translation: I hand out writing tablets to my pupils and tell them to write Greek letters.

sentence: Tibi hunc ānulum dō, ut meminerīs meī cum in Aegyptō erō.
translation: I am giving you this ring so that you remember me while I am in Egypt.

sentence: Ex agrīs fessus domum veniō, ubi cēna calida mē exspectat.
translation: I come home worn out from the fields, where a hot dinner is waiting for me.

sentence: Ad tē crās prīmā lūce veniō, ut dē pecūniā tandem loquāmur.
translation: I'll come to you tomorrow at first light, so that we can finally talk about the money.

sentence: Ex Hispāniā veniō, ubi decem annōs sine familiā mīlitāvī.
translation: I have come from Spain, where I served ten years as a soldier without my family.

sentence: Nunc ad thermās eō, quod tōtum diem in officīnā sūdāvī.
translation: I'm off to the baths now, because I have been sweating in the workshop all day.

sentence: Ad senātum pedibus eō, quia lectīca mea in viā frācta est.
translation: I am walking to the senate on foot, because my litter broke down in the street.

sentence: Invītus in exsilium eō, sed lēgibus patriae pārēre mālō.
translation: I go into exile against my will, but I would rather obey my country's laws.

sentence: Cum fīlia mea febrī labōrat, medicum statim ad domum vocō.
translation: Whenever my daughter is down with a fever, I call the doctor to the house at once.

sentence: Operāriōs meōs ante lūcem vocō, ut olīvās ante imbrem legant.
translation: I call my workers out before dawn, so that they can pick the olives before the rain.

sentence: Deōs immortālēs testēs vocō: innocēns sum et falsō accūsor.
translation: I call the immortal gods to witness: I am innocent and falsely accused.

sentence: Nocte per parietem vīcīnōs clāmantēs audiō et dormīre nōn possum.
translation: At night I hear the neighbours shouting through the wall and cannot get to sleep.

sentence: Cum in tabernā tōnsōris sedeō, omnēs urbis rūmōrēs audiō.
translation: When I sit in the barber's shop, I hear every rumour in the city.

sentence: Verba tua audiō, sed tibi post tot mendācia crēdere iam nōn possum.
translation: I hear what you say, but after so many lies I can no longer believe you.

sentence: Frāter tuus canem in hortō relīquit, quī omnēs rosās fōdit.
translation: Your brother left the dog loose in the garden, and it dug up every one of the roses.

sentence: In tabernā patris tuī vīnum optimum tōtam noctem bibimus.
translation: We sat drinking the best wine in your father's tavern all night long.

sentence: Verba tua in senātū nōn probāvī, sed propter amīcitiam tacuī.
translation: I did not approve of what you said in the senate, but out of friendship I kept quiet.

sentence: In hortō nostrō avia herbās colit, quās ad cēnam saepe carpimus.
translation: Grandmother grows herbs in our garden, and we often pick them for dinner.

sentence: Lēgātus noster mīlitēs trāns flūmen dūxit, priusquam hostēs pontem incenderent.
translation: Our commander marched the men across the river before the enemy could burn the bridge.

sentence: Domum nostram flammae cōnsūmpsērunt, sed nēmō flēvit: omnēs incolumēs erāmus.
translation: The fire took our house, but nobody cried: every one of us had got out safe.

sentence: Dux vester in castrīs vōs exspectat; venīte ante prīmam vigiliam.
translation: Your commander is waiting for you in camp; be there before the first watch.

sentence: Puerī, librōs vestrōs sub lectō invēnī, pulvere omnīnō plēnōs.
translation: Boys, I found your books under the bed, thick with dust.

sentence: Prō patriā vestrā fortiter pugnāvistis, et poēta carmen dē vōbīs scrīpsit.
translation: You fought bravely for your country, and a poet has written a song about you.

sentence: Aliquis iānuam mediā nocte pulsāvit, sed nēmō forās exīre ausus est.
translation: Someone hammered on the door in the middle of the night, but nobody dared go outside.

sentence: Mercātor aliquid dē pretiō frūmentī susurrāvit, sed verba nōn audīvī.
translation: The trader whispered something about the price of grain, but I couldn't catch the words.

sentence: Epistula ab aliquō sine nōmine missa mē vehementer terret.
translation: A letter sent by somebody who left no name has frightened me badly.

sentence: Nūlla aqua in cisternā mānsit, itaque ad fontem cum urceīs īmus.
translation: There's no water left in the cistern, so we're off to the spring with the jugs.

sentence: Nūllī mīlitī crēdidit imperātor, priusquam explōrātōrēs ex silvā redīrent.
translation: The general trusted no soldier's word until the scouts came back out of the forest.

sentence: Tot annōs labōrāvī, sed nūllam ā dominō grātiam accēpī umquam.
translation: I have worked all these years and never once got a word of thanks from the master.

sentence: Hoc vīnum acidum est; affer mihi aliud dē cellā, quaesō.
translation: This wine has turned sour; fetch me another one from the cellar, would you.

sentence: Aliī mīlitēs vāllum fodiēbant, aliī aquam ē flūmine portābant.
translation: Some of the soldiers were digging the rampart, others were hauling water up from the river.

sentence: Aliō tempore dē hāc rē loquēmur; nunc nimis īrātus sum.
translation: We'll talk about this some other time; right now I'm too angry.

sentence: Alterum calceum sub lectō inveniō, alterum canis in hortum abstulit.
translation: I find one shoe under the bed; the dog has carried the other off into the garden.

sentence: Alter cōnsul in Galliā bellum gerit, dum alter Rōmae comitia habet.
translation: One consul is fighting the war in Gaul, while the other holds the elections at Rome.

sentence: Duōs fīliōs habeō: alter agrum colit, alterīus mōrēs mē vexant.
translation: I have two sons: one of them farms the land, and the other's habits are wearing me out.

sentence: Tōtam noctem īnfāns clāmāvit, itaque māne omnēs dēfessī erāmus.
translation: The baby screamed the entire night, so by morning we were all worn out.

sentence: Tōtus populus in Circō fremuit, cum quadrīgae ultimam mētam circumīrent.
translation: The whole crowd in the Circus roared as the chariots swung round the last turning-post.

sentence: Tōtā aestāte in Sabīnīs mānsimus, et numquam Rōmam dēsīderāvī.
translation: We stayed up in the Sabine hills the whole summer, and I never once missed Rome.

sentence: Māter sōla in culīnā cēnam parat, quod ancillae ad forum iērunt.
translation: Mother is getting dinner ready alone in the kitchen, because the maids have gone off to the market.

sentence: Iūdex sōlī testī crēdidit, quī in forō rem vīderat.
translation: The judge believed only the one witness who had actually seen it happen in the forum.

sentence: Post fūnus sōlā in ātriō sedēbat, et nēmō eam cōnsōlārī poterat.
translation: After the funeral she sat by herself in the atrium, and nobody could console her.

sentence: Eundem pānem ab illō pīstōre semper emō, quia nūllus melior est.
translation: I always buy the same loaf from that baker, because there's none better.

sentence: Īdem magister patrem meum et mē in eōdem lūdō docuit.
translation: The same teacher taught my father and me, in the very same schoolroom.

sentence: Eadem verba ter audīvī, et patientia mea tandem dēfēcit.
translation: I have heard the same words three times now, and my patience has finally given out.

sentence: Avus meus tunc in vīllā habitābat, nunc in angustō cēnāculō dormit.
translation: My grandfather lived out on the farm back then; now he sleeps in a cramped attic flat.

sentence: Tunc in castrīs mīlitābam, et centuriō nōmen meum cotīdiē clāmābat.
translation: I was serving in the camp back then, and the centurion shouted my name every single day.

sentence: Cum pater mortuus est, tunc dēmum intellēxī quantum eum amāvissem.
translation: When my father died, only then did I understand how much I had loved him.

sentence: Māter mea semper plūs cibī parat quam tōta familia cōnsūmere potest.
translation: My mother always cooks more food than the whole family can possibly eat.

sentence: Mercātor ille in forō semper eandem fābulam dē naufragiō suō nārrat.
translation: That trader in the forum always tells the same story about his shipwreck.

sentence: Frāter meus semper prōmittit sē adfutūrum esse, sed numquam ad tempus venit.
translation: My brother always promises he will be there, but he never turns up on time.

sentence: Ancilla nostra numquam ignem exstinguit antequam dominus ā cēnā redit.
translation: Our maid never lets the fire go out before the master gets home from dinner.

sentence: Tōnsor in angulō forī numquam tacet, etiam cum novāculam tenet.
translation: The barber on the corner of the forum never stops talking, not even when he is holding a razor.

sentence: Numquam mē paenitēbit quod tē in illā tempestāte exspectāvī.
translation: I will never regret having waited for you out in that storm.

sentence: Avia mea saepe nōbīs fābulās dē bellō Pūnicō ante ignem nārrābat.
translation: My grandmother often told us stories about the Punic War in front of the fire.

sentence: In tabernā vīnāriā saepe cum nautīs dē pretiīs piscium contendimus.
translation: In the wine shop we often argue with the sailors over the price of fish.

sentence: Noctū saepe vigilō et dē fīliō meō in Hispāniā mīlitante cōgitō.
translation: At night I often lie awake thinking about my son, soldiering in Spain.

sentence: Pluit iterum, et aqua per tēctum in lectum meum cadit.
translation: It is raining again, and water is coming through the roof onto my bed.

sentence: Scrība epistulam iterum scrīpsit, quod ātrāmentum in chartam effūderat.
translation: The scribe wrote the letter out again, because he had spilled ink over the sheet.

sentence: Iterum atque iterum nōmen eius vocāvī, sed nēmō ex silvā respondit.
translation: I called his name again and again, but nobody answered from the woods.

sentence: Hodiē māne pānem ēmī, sed canis noster eum dē mēnsā rapuit.
translation: This morning I bought bread, and then our dog snatched it off the table.

sentence: Hodiē in forō causam meam dīcam; iūdex enim diūtius exspectāre nōn vult.
translation: Today I plead my case in the forum; the judge refuses to wait any longer.

sentence: Hodiē quadrāgintā annōs nātus sum, et adhūc nihil magnī perfēcī.
translation: Today I turn forty, and I still have not achieved anything great.

sentence: Herī tōtum diem in hortō labōrāvī, et nunc dorsum mihi dolet.
translation: Yesterday I worked in the garden all day long, and now my back aches.

sentence: Herī nūntius Brundisiō vēnit et litterās dē frūmentō dominō nostrō trādidit.
translation: A messenger came from Brundisium yesterday and handed our master a letter about the grain.

sentence: Herī in theātrō tam vehementer rīsimus ut vōcem paene āmitterēmus.
translation: At the theatre yesterday we laughed so hard that we nearly lost our voices.

sentence: Crās māne ad macellum ībō, quia nihil praeter ōva domī habēmus.
translation: Tomorrow morning I will go to the market, since we have nothing at home but eggs.

sentence: Crās nāvis nostra oleī plēna Alexandrīam petet, sī ventus secundus fuerit.
translation: Tomorrow our ship, loaded with oil, will make for Alexandria, if the wind stays favourable.

sentence: Crās fīlia mea nūbet, et māter eius iam nūllam lacrimam retinēre potest.
translation: My daughter is getting married tomorrow, and her mother already cannot hold back a single tear.

sentence: Sub scālīs cellam habēmus; ibi avus meus vīnum vetus cēlat.
translation: We have a storeroom under the stairs; that is where my grandfather hides his old wine.

sentence: Cum Athēnās vēnissem, ibi philosophiam duōs annōs studiōsē didicī.
translation: After I had reached Athens, I studied philosophy hard there for two years.

sentence: Sub illā porticū prīmum tē vīdī; ibi etiam nunc tē exspectō.
translation: I first saw you under that colonnade; even now I am still waiting for you there.

sentence: Hīc sedēre solēbat pater meus, et nēmō alius illam sellam occupābat.
translation: My father used to sit here, and nobody else ever took that chair.

sentence: Hīc ōlim templum stābat; nunc fabrī inter lapidēs et pulverem labōrant.
translation: A temple once stood here; now workmen are toiling among the stones and the dust.

sentence: Hīc frāter meus cecidit; ideō quotannīs hunc collem ascendō.
translation: This is where my brother fell; that is why I climb this hill every year.

sentence: Post tantam tempestātem tēctum casae nostrae per tōtum mēnsem refēcimus.
translation: After a storm that fierce, we spent a whole month repairing the roof of our cottage.

sentence: Mercātor tantum pretium poscit quantum tōta vīcīnia solvere nōn potest.
translation: The merchant is asking a price so high that the whole neighbourhood cannot pay it.

sentence: Tantus mē pudor cēpit ut nihil cōram tot testibus dīcere possem.
translation: Such shame seized me that I could not say a word in front of so many witnesses.

sentence: Dīc mihi, quālis sit hospes quem crās ad cēnam vocābimus.
translation: Tell me what sort of guest this is that we are inviting to dinner tomorrow.

sentence: Quālem magistrum hōc annō in lūdō habēs, sevērumne an mītem?
translation: What kind of teacher do you have at school this year, a harsh one or a gentle one?

sentence: Nesciō quālem animum ille habeat, sed verbīs eius nōn crēdō.
translation: I don't know what sort of character he has, but I don't trust his words.

sentence: Quantā pecūniā tibi opus est ad tēctum ante hiemem reficiendum?
translation: How much money do you need to get the roof repaired before winter?

sentence: Nēmō scit quantus exercitus trāns flūmen hāc nocte castra posuerit.
translation: Nobody knows how large an army pitched camp across the river last night.

sentence: Quantō gaudiō mātrem vīdī, cum post trēs annōs domum rediī!
translation: What joy I felt at seeing my mother when I came home after three years!

sentence: Sarcinam tam gravem sōlus ex raedā efferre nōn possum; adiuvā mē.
translation: I can't get this heavy bag out of the carriage on my own; give me a hand.

sentence: Crās ad tabernam venīre possum, sī dominus mē mātūrius dīmīserit.
translation: I can come to the shop tomorrow if the master lets me go a little earlier.

sentence: Verba tua audīre possum, sed tibi post illud mendācium crēdere nōn possum.
translation: I can listen to what you say, but after that lie I cannot trust you.

sentence: Bovēs ante lūcem ad forum agō, dum viae adhūc vacuae sunt.
translation: I drive the oxen to market before daybreak, while the roads are still empty.

sentence: In forō causam amīcī agō, quamquam iūdex mihi inimīcus vidētur.
translation: I am pleading my friend's case in the forum, though the judge seems hostile to me.

sentence: Vītam quiētam in agrīs agō et strepitum urbis nōn dēsīderō.
translation: I lead a quiet life out in the fields and do not miss the noise of the city.

sentence: Pānem calidum ā pistrīnō domum ferō, dum adhūc fūmat.
translation: I am carrying the warm bread home from the bakery while it is still steaming.

sentence: Dōna ad templum ferō, ut deī nāvem patris incolumem servent.
translation: I am bringing offerings to the temple so that the gods keep my father's ship safe.

sentence: Contumēliās dominī tacitus ferō, quamquam animus meus intus ārdet.
translation: I bear the master's insults in silence, though inside me my heart is burning.

sentence: Ante cēnam lignum scindere et ignem in culīnā accendere dēbeō.
translation: Before dinner I have to split the wood and light the fire in the kitchen.

sentence: Mercātōrī trēs nummōs prō frūmentō dēbeō, nec hodiē solvere possum.
translation: I owe the merchant three coins for the grain, and I can't pay him today.

sentence: Magistrō meō omnia dēbeō, quod mē puerum ex tenebrīs ēdūxit.
translation: I owe my teacher everything, because he led me out of the dark when I was a boy.

sentence: Putō avum nostrum crās adventūrum esse, nam epistulam nūper mīsit.
translation: I think our grandfather will arrive tomorrow, since he sent a letter recently.

sentence: Nōn putō hunc mercātōrem vēra dīcere, cum pretium totiēns mūtet.
translation: I don't think this merchant is telling the truth, since he changes his price so often.

sentence: Stultum mē putāvistī, sed ego tacēbam et omnia dīligenter audiēbam.
translation: You thought me a fool, but I kept quiet and listened carefully to everything.

sentence: Īnfantem in gremiō teneō, dum uxor mea cēnam in culīnā parat.
translation: I hold the baby on my lap while my wife cooks dinner in the kitchen.

sentence: Cum medicus vulnus patris cūrāret, ego lucernam tōtam noctem tenēbam.
translation: While the doctor was treating my father's wound, I held the lamp all night long.

sentence: Prōmissum tuum memoriā teneō, quamquam tū iam oblītus esse vidēris.
translation: I still keep your promise in mind, though you seem to have forgotten it already.

sentence: Puerum ad pistrīnum mittō, ut pānem ante prandium celeriter emat.
translation: I am sending the boy to the bakery to buy bread quickly before lunch.

sentence: Dux nūntium celerrimē mīsit, ut legiō pontem ante noctem occupāret.
translation: The general sent a messenger at top speed so the legion could seize the bridge before nightfall.

sentence: Hanc epistulam cum lacrimīs mittō, quod tē multōs annōs nōn vīdī.
translation: I send this letter in tears, because I have not seen you for many years.

sentence: Ā fīliō meō, quī Athēnīs philosophiam discit, epistulās accipiō.
translation: I get letters from my son, who is studying philosophy in Athens.

sentence: Argentārius in forō nummōs adulterīnōs numquam accipiēbat, sed omnēs dentibus temptābat.
translation: The banker in the forum never took counterfeit coins; he tested every one with his teeth.

sentence: Cōnsilium tuum grātō animō accipiō, quamquam mihi difficile vidētur.
translation: I take your advice gratefully, though it seems hard to me.

sentence: Cotīdiē māne aquam ē fonte prope hortum nostrum petimus.
translation: Every morning we fetch water from the spring near our garden.

sentence: Marcus cōnsulātum petēbat, itaque tōtō diē in forō cīvēs salūtābat.
translation: Marcus was running for the consulship, so he spent the whole day greeting citizens in the forum.

sentence: Ā tē veniam petō, quia epistulam tuam per neglegentiam āmīsī.
translation: I am asking your pardon, because I carelessly lost your letter.

sentence: Ancilla pānem et ōva in mēnsā pōnit, antequam dominus ē lectō surgit.
translation: The maid puts bread and eggs on the table before the master gets out of bed.

sentence: Mīlitēs fessī castra prope flūmen pōnent, quod nox iam appropinquat.
translation: The weary soldiers will pitch camp by the river, because night is already coming on.

sentence: In tē omnem spem meam pōnō, quia nēmō alius mē adiuvābit.
translation: I place all my hope in you, because nobody else will help me.

sentence: Puer piscēs in flūmine capit, dum pater rētia in rīpā siccat.
translation: The boy is catching fish in the river while his father dries the nets on the bank.

sentence: Rōmānī urbem post longam obsidiōnem cēpērunt et incolās in servitūtem redēgērunt.
translation: The Romans took the city after a long siege and reduced its inhabitants to slavery.

sentence: Magnam voluptātem ex fābulīs avī meī capiō, cum hieme ad focum sedēmus.
translation: I get great pleasure from my grandfather's stories, when we sit by the fire in winter.

sentence: Cum rūs proficīscimur, canem apud vīcīnam nostram semper relinquimus.
translation: Whenever we set off for the country, we always leave the dog with our neighbour.

sentence: Agricolae agrōs relīquērunt et in urbem migrāvērunt, quia frūmentum dēfēcerat.
translation: The farmers abandoned their fields and moved to the city, because the grain had run out.

sentence: Amīcum in perīculō numquam relinquam, etiamsī cēterī omnēs fugient.
translation: I will never abandon a friend in danger, even if everyone else runs away.

sentence: Hodiē domī maneō, quod tempestās nocturna omnēs viās lutō complēvit.
translation: I am staying home today, because the night's storm has filled every road with mud.

sentence: Servī in ātriō manēbant, dum dominus in trīclīniō cum hospitibus cēnat.
translation: The slaves waited in the atrium while the master dined with his guests.

sentence: Etsī multa mūtāta sunt, amīcitia nostra integra manet.
translation: Even though much has changed, our friendship remains intact.

sentence: In hāc īnsulā iam decem annōs sine aquā calidā vīvimus.
translation: We have been living in this apartment block for ten years now with no hot water.

sentence: Post bellum frāter meus in pāce et ōtiō laetus vīvēbat.
translation: After the war my brother lived happily in peace and leisure.

sentence: Nēmō beātē vīvit quī dē pecūniā suā semper sollicitus est.
translation: No one lives a happy life who is forever anxious about his money.

sentence: Cotīdiē vestem mūtō antequam ad thermās cum amīcīs eō.
translation: I change my clothes every day before I go to the baths with friends.

sentence: Mercātor pretia cotīdiē mūtat, prout nāvēs ex Aegyptō veniunt.
translation: The merchant changes his prices daily, depending on which ships come in from Egypt.

sentence: Postquam Athēnās vīdī, tōtam dē arte sententiam meam mūtāvī.
translation: After I had seen Athens, I completely changed my view of art.

sentence: Servī mēnsam gravem ad fenestram movent, ut lūce meliōre ūtāmur.
translation: The slaves are moving the heavy table over to the window so that we have better light.

sentence: Imperātor castra nocte movēbit, nē hostēs exercitum nostrum cōnspiciant.
translation: The general will move camp at night, so that the enemy do not spot our army.

sentence: Fābula dē mīlite mortuō mē tantum mōvit ut lacrimārem.
translation: The story about the dead soldier moved me so much that I wept.

sentence: Fīlius meus mē cotīdiē rogat cūr avus dē bellō numquam loquātur.
translation: My son asks me every day why grandfather never talks about the war.

sentence: Cōnsul senātōrēs sententiam rogāvit, sed nēmō prīmus loquī audēbat.
translation: The consul asked the senators for their opinion, but no one dared to speak first.

sentence: Tē rogō ut mihi ignōscās; nōluī tē cōram omnibus reprehendere.
translation: I am asking you to forgive me; I did not mean to criticise you in front of everyone.

sentence: Tōtā nocte īnfāns flēvit, et māter fessa nūllum somnum cēpit.
translation: The baby cried all night long, and his exhausted mother got no sleep.

sentence: Mediā nocte vigilēs per Subūram eunt, nē tabernae ārdeant.
translation: In the middle of the night the watchmen patrol through the Subura, so that the shops do not burn.

sentence: Longae mihi videntur noctēs, ex quō amīcus meus Rōmā discessit.
translation: The nights have seemed long to me ever since my friend left Rome.

sentence: Nōn est mihi tempus cēnam parāre, quia hospitēs mox adveniunt.
translation: I have no time to get dinner ready, because the guests are arriving soon.

sentence: Tempore bellī cīvīlis multī senātōrēs ex urbe in vīllās fūgērunt.
translation: During the civil war many senators fled from the city out to their country estates.

sentence: Nimium temporis apud tōnsōrem perdidī; nunc mē paenitet tantae morae.
translation: I wasted too much time at the barber's; now I regret such a long delay.

sentence: Hōc annō pater meus vīneam novam post vīllam serere cōnstituit.
translation: This year my father decided to plant a new vineyard behind the farmhouse.

sentence: Duōs annōs in Galliā mīlitāvī, priusquam ad uxōrem redīre licuit.
translation: I soldiered in Gaul for two years before I was allowed to go back to my wife.

sentence: Post tot annōs adhūc memoriā teneō vōcem magistrī meī.
translation: After so many years I still remember the voice of my old teacher.

sentence: Prīmā hōrā surgō, ut ignem in culīnā ante lūcem accendam.
translation: I get up at the first hour so that I can light the kitchen fire before daybreak.

sentence: Duās hōrās in thermīs exspectāvī, dōnec amīcus meus tandem vēnit.
translation: I waited two hours at the baths until my friend finally turned up.

sentence: Ultima hōra ante iūdicium mihi longior quam tōtus annus vidēbātur.
translation: The last hour before the trial seemed longer to me than a whole year.

sentence: Manūs meae farīnā albae sunt, quod māter mē pānem facere iussit.
translation: My hands are white with flour, because my mother told me to make the bread.

sentence: Manus latrōnum viātōrēs in Viā Appiā prope Arīciam adorta est.
translation: A band of robbers attacked travellers on the Appian Way near Aricia.

sentence: Manum meam avus moriēns tenuit et dē bellīs antīquīs nārrāvit.
translation: My dying grandfather held my hand and told me about the old wars.

sentence: Caput mihi dolet, quia hesternō diē nimium vīnī apud Mārcum bibī.
translation: My head aches, because yesterday I drank far too much wine at Marcus's house.

sentence: Servus amphoram gravem in capite portat per angustās Subūrae viās.
translation: A slave carries a heavy wine-jar on his head through the narrow streets of the Subura.

sentence: Caesar caput togā vēlāvit, cum coniūrātōs undique venīre vīdisset.
translation: Caesar covered his head with his toga when he saw the conspirators closing in from every side.

sentence: Fūmus ex focō oculōs meōs ūrit; fenestram aperīre statim dēbeō.
translation: Smoke from the hearth is stinging my eyes; I have to open the window at once.

sentence: Medicus oculum senis lēniter tetigit et herbās ad dolōrem parāvit.
translation: The doctor gently touched the old man's eye and prepared herbs for the pain.

sentence: Ubi mātrem meam post decem annōs vīdī, oculī lacrimīs implētī sunt.
translation: When I saw my mother after ten years, my eyes filled with tears.

sentence: Cor mihi celeriter palpitat, cum per gradūs ad cēnāculum ascendō.
translation: My heart pounds whenever I climb the stairs up to my flat.

sentence: Verba ducis mīlitum corda accendērunt, et omnēs in hostem cucurrērunt.
translation: The general's words set the soldiers' hearts on fire, and they all charged at the enemy.

sentence: Epistula tua cor meum gaudiō implēvit, quamquam procul ā tē absum.
translation: Your letter filled my heart with joy, even though I am far away from you.

sentence: Corpus meum post longum iter dolet; in balneō calidō requiēscam.
translation: My body aches after the long journey; I shall rest in a hot bath.

sentence: Mīlitēs corpora sociōrum ex campō tulērunt et rogum magnum exstrūxērunt.
translation: The soldiers carried their comrades' bodies off the field and built a great funeral pyre.

sentence: Athlēta corpus suum cotīdiē in palaestrā exercet, animum numquam.
translation: The athlete trains his body in the wrestling-ground every day, but never his mind.

sentence: Animus meus ad vīllam avītam redit, quotiēns odōrem pānis sentiō.
translation: My mind goes back to my grandfather's farmhouse whenever I catch the smell of bread.

sentence: Bonō animō estō, mīles: crās castra hostium ante lūcem capiēmus.
translation: Keep your courage up, soldier: tomorrow before dawn we will take the enemy's camp.

sentence: Aeger animō sum, quod amīcus meus verba mea in forō rīsit.
translation: I am sick at heart, because my friend laughed at my words in the forum.

sentence: Iānuam noctū pulsat ignōtus, sed ego numquam statim respondeō.
translation: A stranger knocks at the door in the night, but I never answer straight away.

sentence: Mercātōribus in forō clāmantibus nihil respondeō, quia pecūniam nōn habeō.
translation: I give no answer to the traders shouting in the forum, because I have no money.

sentence: Ad epistulam patris īrātī nōndum respondī; verba mihi dēsunt.
translation: I still haven't answered my angry father's letter; I can't find the words.

sentence: Per turbam forī fīlium parvum manū cautē dūcō.
translation: I lead my small son carefully by the hand through the crowd in the forum.

sentence: Dux legiōnēs per montēs nive opertōs in hīberna dūcēbat.
translation: The general was leading the legions through snow-covered mountains into winter quarters.

sentence: Haec via ad flūmen dūcit, sed noctū sōlus īre timeō.
translation: This road leads down to the river, but I'm afraid to walk it alone at night.

sentence: Dum pater abest, ego rēs domesticās sōlus gerō.
translation: While my father is away, I run the household affairs on my own.

sentence: Legiōnēs nostrae in Germāniā bellum per hiemem tōtam gerunt.
translation: Our legions are waging war in Germany right through the winter.

sentence: Novus vīlicus superbē sē gerit, et servī iam murmurant.
translation: The new estate manager carries himself arrogantly, and the household is already grumbling.

sentence: Sub mēnsā canī meō frūsta pānis clam iaciō.
translation: Under the table I secretly throw scraps of bread to my dog.

sentence: Nautae tempestāte territī mercēs gravēs in mare iēcērunt.
translation: Terrified by the storm, the sailors threw the heavy cargo into the sea.

sentence: Spectātōrēs īrātī pōma putrida in scaenam iaciēbant per tōtam fābulam.
translation: The angry audience kept throwing rotten fruit onto the stage all through the play.

sentence: Fīlia mea canem vīcīnī timet et aliā viā domum redit.
translation: My daughter is afraid of the neighbour's dog and goes home by another road.

sentence: Agricolae hanc hiemem timent, quia frūmentum in horreīs dēficit.
translation: The farmers dread this winter, because the grain in the barns is running out.

sentence: Timeō nē pater epistulam illam sub lectō occultātam iam invēnerit.
translation: I'm afraid my father has already found that letter hidden under the bed.

sentence: Spērō tē crās ad cēnam nostram ventūrum esse cum uxōre.
translation: I hope you'll come to dinner at our house tomorrow with your wife.

sentence: Mercātor nāvēs suās ante hiemem in portum reditūrās esse spērat.
translation: The merchant hopes his ships will make it back to harbour before winter.

sentence: Nihil iam spērō, sed tamen cotīdiē ad portum ambulō.
translation: I hope for nothing any more, and yet every day I walk down to the harbour.

sentence: Noctū in lectō iacēns dē rēbus crāstinīs diū cōgitō.
translation: Lying in bed at night, I turn tomorrow's business over in my mind for a long while.

sentence: Faber dē novā tabernā aperiendā iam multōs mēnsēs cōgitat.
translation: The craftsman has been thinking for months now about opening a new shop.

sentence: Senex in hortō sōlus sedet et dē adulēscentiā suā cōgitat.
translation: The old man sits alone in the garden and thinks back on his youth.

sentence: Quid dīcās vix intellegō, quia omnēs in tabernā simul clāmant.
translation: I can barely make out what you're saying, because everyone in the tavern is shouting at once.

sentence: Advena verba nostra nōn intellegit, itaque manibus viam rogat.
translation: The newcomer doesn't understand our language, so he asks the way with his hands.

sentence: Nunc dēmum intellegō cūr pater tot annōs tacuerit.
translation: Only now do I understand why my father kept silent for so many years.

sentence: In thermīs cotīdiē novōs hominēs cognōscō, sed nōmina mihi statim excidunt.
translation: At the baths I get to know new people every day, but the names slip my mind at once.

sentence: Prīmō annō vīlicus omnēs colōnōs et agrōs bene cognōvit.
translation: In his first year the estate manager got to know all the tenants and the fields well.

sentence: Hominem numquam vērē cognōscēs, priusquam cum eō iter fēceris.
translation: You'll never really know a person until you have travelled with him.

sentence: In viā homō pauper ā mē pānem petīvit, sed nihil habēbam.
translation: On the street a poor man asked me for bread, but I had nothing on me.

sentence: Hōc in oppidō omnēs hominēs mercātūram exercent, nēmō agrōs colit.
translation: In this town everybody is in trade; nobody works the land.

sentence: Ille homō semper prōmittit, numquam solvit; iam nēmō eī crēdit.
translation: That man is forever promising and never paying; by now nobody trusts him.

sentence: Vir meus in culīnā pānem frangit, dum ego lucernam accendō.
translation: My husband is breaking the bread in the kitchen while I light the lamp.

sentence: Māne vir togātus clientēs in ātriō salūtat, deinde ad forum dēscendit.
translation: In the morning the man in his toga greets his clients in the hall, then heads down to the forum.

sentence: Illum virum omnēs vītant, quod semper dē pecūniā suā loquitur.
translation: Everyone avoids that man, because he never stops talking about his money.

sentence: Puer in hortō pilā lūdit, dum māter cēnam in culīnā parat.
translation: The boy is playing ball in the garden while his mother gets dinner ready in the kitchen.

sentence: Puerum magister in lūdō laudat, quod versūs Vergiliī bene recitāvit.
translation: The teacher praises the boy in class for reciting Vergil's lines well.

sentence: Puer āmissō cane per tōtam viam maestus domum ambulābat.
translation: Having lost his dog, the boy trudged the whole length of the street home in misery.

sentence: Avia puellae aegrōtae fābulam dē lupō ante somnum nārrat.
translation: Grandmother tells the sick girl a story about a wolf before she goes to sleep.

sentence: Puellās magistra in ātriō litterās docet, sed illae tantum rīdent.
translation: The teacher is teaching the girls their letters in the hall, but they only giggle.

sentence: Puella nova in lūdō tacet, quod nēminem inter tot discipulōs nōvit.
translation: The new girl says nothing in class, because she doesn't know a soul among so many pupils.

sentence: Pater meus ante cēnam in hortō rāmōs arboris veteris secat.
translation: Before dinner my father is out in the garden cutting branches off the old tree.

sentence: Patrem meum in forō vīdī, ubi dē pretiō frūmentī cum mercātōribus disputābat.
translation: I caught sight of my father in the forum, arguing with the traders about the price of grain.

sentence: Patrī meō numquam dīxī quantum eius cōnsilia mē adiūvissent.
translation: I never told my father how much his advice had helped me.

sentence: Soror mea capillōs meōs ante nūptiās cūrā magnā compōnit.
translation: My sister is doing my hair with great care before the wedding.

sentence: Sorōrī meae, quae trāns mare habitat, longam epistulam dē fīliō meō scrīpsī.
translation: I wrote a long letter about my son to my sister, who lives overseas.

sentence: Sine sorōre meā domus tōta mihi vacua et trīstis vidētur.
translation: Without my sister the whole house feels empty and sad to me.

sentence: In ātriō avus noster deō Larī cotīdiē vīnum et flōrēs offert.
translation: In the hall our grandfather offers wine and flowers to the household god every day.

sentence: In templō Iovis sacerdōs deum precātur ut pluviam agrīs siccīs mittat.
translation: In the temple of Jupiter the priest begs the god to send rain to the parched fields.

sentence: Post tantam clādem multī dē deōrum cūrā dubitāre coepērunt.
translation: After a disaster on that scale many began to doubt whether the gods care at all.

sentence: Dominus noster māne per vīllam ambulat et opus servōrum īnspicit.
translation: Our master walks through the villa first thing and inspects the slaves' work.

sentence: Dominō absente, tōta domus in ōtiō et clāmōre diem cōnsūmpsit.
translation: With the master away, the whole household spent the day in idleness and noise.

sentence: Bonum dominum habēmus, quī servōs suōs sine causā numquam verberat.
translation: We have a good master, one who never beats his slaves without a reason.

sentence: Servus aquam ē puteō in culīnam ante prīmam lūcem portat.
translation: The slave carries water from the well into the kitchen before first light.

sentence: Dominus servō fidēlī lībertātem post multōs annōs labōris dedit.
translation: The master granted his loyal slave his freedom after many years of work.

sentence: Nēmō servum interrogāvit num fessus esset, num domum suam dēsīderāret.
translation: Nobody asked the slave whether he was tired, or whether he missed his home.

sentence: In forō populus dē lēge novā ācriter disputat, sed magistrātus tacet.
translation: In the forum the people are arguing fiercely about the new law, but the magistrate keeps quiet.

sentence: Mercātōrēs populum in macellō clāmōribus ad mercēs suās vocant.
translation: In the market the traders shout to pull the crowd over to their wares.

sentence: Senātōrēs populō pānem et lūdōs dabant, nē dē lībertāte cōgitāret.
translation: The senators kept giving the people bread and games, so that it would not think about freedom.

sentence: Māne urbs tōta strepitū plaustrōrum et clāmōre mercātōrum excitātur.
translation: At dawn the whole city is woken by the rattle of carts and the shouting of traders.

sentence: Post decem annōs in urbem rediī et nēminem in viīs agnōvī.
translation: After ten years I came back to the city and recognised nobody in the streets.

sentence: In urbe captā mātrēs per viās timidae fīliōs suōs quaerēbant.
translation: In the captured city frightened mothers went through the streets searching for their sons.

sentence: Post mortem avī tōta domus per multōs mēnsēs tacēbat.
translation: After grandfather's death the whole house stayed silent for months.

sentence: Medicus, quamquam tōtam noctem labōrāvit, mortem puerī āvertere nōn potuit.
translation: Though the doctor worked all night, he could not stave off the boy's death.

sentence: Mīlitēs fortēs mortem prō patriā nōn timent, sed servitūtem ōdērunt.
translation: Brave soldiers do not fear death for their country, but they hate slavery.

sentence: Avus meus dē bellō numquam loquitur, sed noctū saepe clāmat.
translation: My grandfather never talks about the war, but at night he often cries out.

sentence: Cīvēs in forō dē bellō disputābant, quia nūntius nova dē clāde attulerat.
translation: The citizens were arguing about the war in the forum, because a messenger had brought news of a defeat.

sentence: Bellum iam decem annōs trahitur, et nēmō victōriam spērat.
translation: The war has dragged on for ten years now, and nobody hopes for victory any more.

sentence: Puer novum verbum audīvit et statim mātrem rogāvit quid significāret.
translation: The boy heard a new word and immediately asked his mother what it meant.

sentence: Magister nūllum verbum dīxit, sed ūnō vultū omnēs discipulōs tacēre coēgit.
translation: The teacher said not a single word, but with one look forced every pupil into silence.

sentence: Ūnum verbum asperum dīxī, et amīcus meus trēs diēs tacuit.
translation: I said one harsh word, and my friend went three days without speaking.

sentence: Liber quem herī legēbam sub pulvīnō adhūc iacet.
translation: The book I was reading yesterday is still lying under my pillow.

sentence: In tabernā librāriā librum vetustum ēmī, quem scrība manū scrīpserat.
translation: In a bookshop I bought an old book that a scribe had copied out by hand.

sentence: Hic liber mē magis dēlectat quam omnēs fābulae quās avia nārrābat.
translation: This book delights me more than all the stories my grandmother used to tell.

sentence: Via ad casam nostram tam lutōsa est ut plaustra saepe haereant.
translation: The road to our cottage is so muddy that wagons often get stuck.

sentence: Mīlitēs tōtā aestāte viam novam per palūdem lentē mūniēbant.
translation: All summer long the soldiers were slowly building a new road through the marsh.

sentence: Nūlla via facilis ad sapientiam dūcit, ut philosophī nōs monent.
translation: No easy road leads to wisdom, as the philosophers keep reminding us.

sentence: Domus nostra tam angusta est ut hospitēs in hortō cēnent.
translation: Our house is so cramped that our guests end up dining in the garden.

sentence: Post longum iter domum tandem rediī, et canis mē prīmus agnōvit.
translation: After a long journey I finally came home, and the dog was the first to recognise me.

sentence: Senātor in domō suā clientēs cotīdiē māne salūtābat.
translation: Every morning the senator used to greet his clients in his own house.

sentence: Omnem pecūniam in cibum cōnsūmpsimus, itaque nūllum vīnum emere possumus.
translation: We spent all our money on food, so we cannot buy any wine.

sentence: Mercātor mihi pecūniam sine ūsūrā crēdidit, quod patrem meum bene nōverat.
translation: The merchant lent me money without interest, because he knew my father well.

sentence: Sine pecūniā in urbe vīvere difficile est, etiam amīcīs adiuvantibus.
translation: Living in the city without money is hard, even when friends are helping you.

sentence: Māter cibum calidum in mēnsā posuit, et puerī ex hortō accurrērunt.
translation: Mother put the hot food on the table, and the boys came running in from the garden.

sentence: Mīlitibus in castrīs cibus dēerat, quia imber viās clauserat.
translation: The soldiers in camp were short of food, because the rain had closed the roads.

sentence: Cibus in tabernā vīlis erat, sed nēmō illum iterum edere voluit.
translation: The food at the inn was cheap, but nobody wanted to eat it a second time.

sentence: Māne pānem recentem ā pīstōre emō, dum aliī adhūc dormiunt.
translation: Each morning I buy fresh bread from the baker while everyone else is still asleep.

sentence: Servus pānem et olīvās operāriīs in agrō labōrantibus distribuit.
translation: A slave handed out bread and olives to the workmen labouring in the field.

sentence: Nihil mihi dulcius est quam pānis quem avia mea coquēbat.
translation: Nothing tastes sweeter to me than the bread my grandmother used to bake.

sentence: Puella mālum ē rāmō carpsit et in sinum tunicae posuit.
translation: The girl picked an apple off the branch and tucked it into the fold of her tunic.

sentence: Agricola nōbīs mālum gustandum dedit, priusquam tōtum modium ēmimus.
translation: The farmer gave us an apple to taste before we bought a whole bushel.

sentence: Mālum acerbum erat, sed puerō ēsurientī dulcius melle vidēbātur.
translation: The apple was sour, but to the starving boy it seemed sweeter than honey.

sentence: Dominus ipse cēnam coxit, quod coquus noster subitō aegrōtābat.
translation: The master cooked the dinner himself, because our cook had suddenly fallen ill.

sentence: Cōnsul ipse in forum dēscendit et cīvēs nōmine salūtāvit.
