translation: The consul came down into the forum in person and greeted the citizens by name.

sentence: Perīculum ipse vīdī; itaque rūmōribus vestrīs nūllō modō crēdō.
translation: I saw the danger with my own eyes, so I put no trust at all in your rumours.

sentence: Omnis aqua ex puteō nostrō hausta est; nunc ad flūmen īmus.
translation: All the water has been drawn out of our well, so now we are going down to the river.

sentence: Omnis cīvis, quī māne in forum properat, praetōrem clāmantem audit.
translation: Every citizen who hurries down to the forum in the morning gets to hear the praetor shouting.

sentence: In portū nāvēs omnis generis videō, nostram tamen frūstrā quaerō.
translation: In the harbour I can see ships of every kind, but I look for ours in vain.

sentence: Servus rēs nostrās in raedam impōnit, quod crās Rōmam redīmus.
translation: The slave is loading our things into the carriage, because tomorrow we go back to Rome.

sentence: Rēs pūblica nostra in perīculō est, dum cōnsulēs inter sē contendunt.
translation: Our republic is in danger while the consuls are busy fighting each other.

sentence: Rēs nostrae male sē habent: frūmentum dēfēcit et hostēs adsunt.
translation: Things are going badly for us: the grain has run out and the enemy is upon us.

sentence: Senem aegrum fīlius suus cotīdiē ad thermās lentē dūcēbat.
translation: His own son used to walk the sick old man slowly to the baths every day.

sentence: In theātrō suus cuique locus erat, nec quisquam dē ōrdine querēbātur.
translation: In the theatre everyone had his own seat, and nobody complained about the seating.

sentence: Mīlitī in castrīs nihil cārius est quam gladius suus.
translation: For a soldier in camp nothing is dearer than his own sword.

sentence: In fābulā quam avia nārrat, rēx pauperem puellam in mātrimōnium dūcit.
translation: In the story grandmother tells, a king marries a poor girl.

sentence: Rēx Parthōrum lēgātōs nostrōs tōtam hiemem in aulā retinuit.
translation: The king of the Parthians kept our envoys at his court the whole winter.

sentence: Rēx superbus populum contemnēbat, dōnec cīvēs eum ex urbe expulērunt.
translation: The arrogant king kept looking down on the people, until the citizens drove him out of the city.

sentence: Tantum frīgus erat ut etiam canis ā focō discēdere nōllet.
translation: It was so cold that even the dog refused to leave the fireside.

sentence: Pistor etiam noctū labōrat, quod mīlitēs māne pānem calidum poscunt.
translation: The baker works even at night, because the soldiers demand hot bread first thing in the morning.

sentence: Nōn sōlum pecūniam sed etiam amīcōs in illō naufragiō āmīsit.
translation: In that shipwreck he lost not only his money but his friends as well.

sentence: Puerī iam dormiunt; lūmen exstingue et iānuam tacitē claude.
translation: The children are asleep already; put out the lamp and shut the door quietly.

sentence: Sōl iam occidit, sed servī in agrīs adhūc frūmentum metunt.
translation: The sun has already gone down, but the farmhands are still reaping grain out in the fields.

sentence: Iam trēs hōrās tē sub porticū exspectō, et īrāscī incipiō.
translation: I have been waiting for you under the colonnade three hours now, and I am starting to lose my temper.

sentence: Hic diēs fēstus est: māter placentam facit, pater tabernam claudit.
translation: Today is a holiday: mother is making a cake and father is shutting up the shop.

sentence: Trēs diēs in viā Appiā iter fēcimus, priusquam Capuam vīdimus.
translation: We travelled three days along the Appian Way before we caught sight of Capua.

sentence: Longī mihi diēs videntur, postquam frāter in Galliam profectus est.
translation: The days feel long to me now that my brother has set out for Gaul.

sentence: Per hortum ad culīnam cucurrimus, quia imber repente cecidit.
translation: We ran through the garden to the kitchen, because the rain came down all at once.

sentence: Cicerō per servum fidēlem epistulam ad Atticum statim mīsit.
translation: Cicero sent a letter to Atticus at once by the hand of a trusted slave.

sentence: Per tōtam noctem prō aegrō fīliō māter deōs ōrāvit.
translation: All night long the mother prayed to the gods for her sick son.

sentence: Māter ex fenestrā clāmāvit, quod puerī in viā pugnābant.
translation: Mother shouted out of the window, because the boys were fighting in the street.

sentence: Ūnus ex mīlitibus prō signīs stetit et ducem interrogāvit.
translation: One of the soldiers stepped out in front of the standards and questioned the general.

sentence: Ex illō diē nēmō in vīcō dē incendiō loquī audet.
translation: From that day on nobody in the neighbourhood dares to talk about the fire.

sentence: Avus meus vīnum vetus in cellā vīgintī annōs servāvit.
translation: My grandfather kept the old wine down in the cellar for twenty years.

sentence: In tabernā prope forum vīnum aquā mixtum nautīs vendimus.
translation: In the tavern near the forum we sell the sailors wine cut with water.

sentence: Nimium vīnī bibistī, amīce, et iam lingua tua titubat.
translation: You have drunk too much wine, my friend, and now your tongue is stumbling.

sentence: Duo fīliī meī in hortō pilā lūdunt, dum cēna parātur.
translation: My two sons are playing ball in the garden while dinner is being got ready.

sentence: Duōs servōs ad forum mīsī, ut pānem et olīvās emerent.
translation: I sent two slaves down to the forum to buy bread and olives.

sentence: Duo tantum amīcī mihi restant, sed hī fidēlissimī sunt.
translation: Only two friends are left to me, but these two are utterly loyal.

sentence: Quattuor lucernās accendī, quod nox in vīllā longa erat.
translation: I lit four lamps, because the night out at the villa was a long one.

sentence: Quattuor equī currum per Circum Maximum trahunt, et turba clāmat.
translation: Four horses are hauling the chariot round the Circus Maximus, and the crowd is roaring.

sentence: Quattuor annōs iam in castrīs meruī, et domum redīre cupiō.
translation: I have served four years in camp by now, and I long to go home.

sentence: Quīnque ōva sub gallīnā hodiē invēnī, sed ūnum frāctum erat.
translation: I found five eggs under the hen today, but one of them was cracked.

sentence: Quīnque dēnāriōs mercātōrī dedī prō pallā, quae nimis cāra erat.
translation: I paid the trader five denarii for a cloak that was far too dear.

sentence: Quīnque diēs iam pluit, et omnēs in vīllā taedium sentīmus.
translation: It has been raining for five days now, and everyone in the house is bored stiff.

sentence: Māter mea sex pānēs in furnō coxit ante prīmam lūcem.
translation: My mother baked six loaves in the oven before first light.

sentence: Sex mīlitēs ante portam stant et nēminem sine tesserā intrāre sinunt.
translation: Six soldiers are standing in front of the gate and let nobody in without a pass.

sentence: Abhinc sex mēnsēs frāter meus in Graeciam nāvigāvit nec adhūc rediit.
translation: Six months ago my brother sailed for Greece, and he still has not come back.

sentence: Septem collēs urbis nostrae ē tēctō summō cōnspicere possum.
translation: From the top of the roof I can pick out all seven hills of our city.

sentence: Septem diēs iter fēcimus antequam ad rādīcēs Alpium pervēnimus.
translation: We were seven days on the road before we reached the foot of the Alps.

sentence: Septem librōs scrīpsit poēta, sed nūllum ēdere ausus est.
translation: The poet wrote seven books, but never dared to publish a single one.

sentence: Octō convīvae in triclīniō recubuērunt, sed cibus vix omnibus suffēcit.
translation: Eight guests reclined in the dining room, but the food barely stretched to them all.

sentence: Octō rēmigēs scapham adversō flūmine lentē ad pontem impellunt.
translation: Eight rowers are slowly driving the boat upstream toward the bridge.

sentence: Octō versūs tantum hodiē scrīpsī, et omnēs mihi displicent.
translation: I managed only eight lines of verse today, and I dislike every one of them.

sentence: Novem cubicula haec domus habet, sed duōbus tantum ūtimur.
translation: This house has nine bedrooms, but we only ever use two of them.

sentence: Novem mēnsēs mercātor in Aegyptō mānsit priusquam Rōmam rediit.
translation: The merchant stayed nine months in Egypt before he came back to Rome.

sentence: Novem Mūsās poēta invocat, sed nūlla eī hodiē respondet.
translation: The poet calls on the nine Muses, but not one of them answers him today.

sentence: Decem passūs ā iānuā nostrā puteus abest, unde aquam trahimus.
translation: The well we draw our water from stands ten paces from our door.

sentence: Decem annōs Graecī Trōiam obsēdērunt antequam urbs dolō capta est.
translation: The Greeks besieged Troy for ten years before the city was taken by a trick.

sentence: Decem epistulās ad tē mīsī, sed nūllum adhūc respōnsum accēpī.
translation: I have sent you ten letters, and so far I have had no reply at all.

sentence: Centum ovēs pastor per montēs dūxit, sed decem in silvā āmīsit.
translation: The shepherd drove a hundred sheep over the mountains, but lost ten of them in the woods.

sentence: Centum senātōrēs in cūriā convēnērunt ut dē bellō novō dēcernerent.
translation: A hundred senators gathered in the senate house to settle the question of the new war.

sentence: Centum mīlia passuum ā patriā absum, et somnia mē domum ferunt.
translation: I am a hundred miles from my homeland, and my dreams keep carrying me back there.

sentence: Prīmā lūce in oppidum dēscendimus, ubi pānem et vīnum emimus.
translation: At first light we go down into town, where we buy bread and wine.

sentence: Oppidum nostrum mūrō antīquō cingitur, quem Rōmānī ōlim aedificāvērunt.
translation: Our town is ringed by an ancient wall that the Romans built long ago.

sentence: Nūllum oppidum mihi cārius est quam illud in quō puer lūsī.
translation: No town is dearer to me than the one where I played as a boy.

sentence: Hic locus sub arbore mihi placet, quod umbram per tōtum diem praebet.
translation: I like this spot under the tree, because it gives shade all day long.

sentence: Mīlitēs locum castrīs idōneum prope flūmen tandem invēnērunt.
translation: The soldiers finally found a place near the river suitable for a camp.

sentence: Dē eō locō semper cum dolōre loquitur, quod ibi mātrem āmīsit.
translation: He always speaks of that place with grief, because he lost his mother there.

sentence: Post imbrem terra in hortō tam mollis erat ut eam facile foderēmus.
translation: After the rain the soil in the garden was so soft that we dug it easily.

sentence: Multōs annōs per terrās aliēnās errāvimus, priusquam domum vēnimus.
translation: For many years we wandered through foreign lands before we came home.

sentence: Terram patriam relinquere nōlēbam, sed bellum omnēs fugere coēgit.
translation: I did not want to leave my native land, but the war forced everyone to flee.

sentence: Aestāte māne in marī natāmus, et posteā piscēs in lītore coquimus.
translation: In summer we swim in the sea in the morning, and afterwards we cook fish on the shore.

sentence: Nautae trāns mare tempestāte iactātī vix ad portum pervēnērunt.
translation: Tossed by a storm across the sea, the sailors barely reached the harbour.

sentence: Māter mea mare semper timuit, quod pater in flūctibus periit.
translation: My mother always feared the sea, because my father died in the waves.

sentence: Puerī aquam ē puteō hauriunt, quia fōns ante vīllam siccus est.
translation: The boys are drawing water from the well, because the spring in front of the farmhouse is dry.

sentence: Aqua per longōs arcūs in urbem ā Rōmānīs sapienter ducta est.
translation: The water was cleverly brought into the city by the Romans over long arches.

sentence: Sine aquā mīlitēs per campōs āridōs diū prōcēdere nōn poterant.
translation: Without water the soldiers could not march for long across the dry plains.

sentence: Hieme omnēs ante ignem convenīmus, dum avia fābulās dē bellō nārrat.
translation: In winter we all gather in front of the fire while grandmother tells stories about the war.

sentence: Ignis in tabernā ortus multās domōs ante lūcem cōnsūmpsit.
translation: A fire that started in a shop destroyed many houses before daybreak.

sentence: Sacerdōs ignem in ārā tōtā nocte custōdiēbat, nē deī īrāscerentur.
translation: The priest guarded the fire on the altar all night, so that the gods would not grow angry.

sentence: Caelum subitō nigrum fit, et mercātōrēs in forō mercēs celeriter tegunt.
translation: The sky suddenly turns black, and the traders in the forum quickly cover their goods.

sentence: Ante proelium imperātor caelum spectāvit et ōmen bonum mīlitibus nūntiāvit.
translation: Before the battle the general watched the sky and announced a good omen to the soldiers.

sentence: Sub caelō apertō dormīre mālō quam in casā angustā manēre.
translation: I would rather sleep under the open sky than stay in a cramped hut.

sentence: Sub merīdiem sōl per fenestram intrat et cubiculum tōtum calefacit.
translation: Around midday the sun comes in through the window and warms the whole bedroom.

sentence: Agricolae ante sōlis ortum surgunt et ad agrōs statim contendunt.
translation: The farmers get up before sunrise and set off for the fields at once.

sentence: Post longam hiemem sōlem iterum vidēre omnibus grātissimum erat.
translation: After the long winter, seeing the sun again was a delight to everyone.

sentence: Lūnā lūcente sine lucernā per agrōs domum tūtī rediimus.
translation: With the moon shining we got home safely across the fields without a lamp.

sentence: Sacerdōtēs novam lūnam exspectābant, ut diem fēstum populō nūntiārent.
translation: The priests were waiting for the new moon so that they could announce the feast day to the people.

sentence: Lūna plēna super mare surgēbat, et nēmō ex nautīs loquēbātur.
translation: A full moon was rising over the sea, and not one of the sailors was speaking.

sentence: Post cēnam in tēctō sedēmus, dum stellae super hortum lentē oriuntur.
translation: After dinner we sit on the roof while the stars rise slowly over the garden.

sentence: Nautae stellīs ducibus per mare nāvigābant, quia nūllam terram vidēbant.
translation: The sailors steered across the sea by the stars, because they could see no land.

sentence: Astrologus dīcēbat stellās fāta hominum regere, sed pater meus rīsit.
translation: The astrologer claimed that the stars govern the fates of men, but my father laughed.

sentence: Fīlius meus avō suō tam similis est ut hospitēs saepe errent.
translation: My son looks so much like his grandfather that guests often mistake them.

sentence: Hic nummus vērō argentō similis vidētur, sed argentārius fraudem statim dēprehendit.
translation: This coin looks like real silver, but the banker spots the fraud at once.

sentence: Ōrātiō tua vērī similis erat, sed nēmō in cūriā tibi crēdidit.
translation: Your speech sounded plausible, but nobody in the senate house believed you.

sentence: Pānis tam dūrus erat ut mīlitēs eum in vīnō madefacerent.
translation: The bread was so hard that the soldiers had to soak it in wine.

sentence: Agricola manūs dūrās habet, quod trīgintā annōs agrum saxōsum arāvit.
translation: The farmer's hands are calloused from thirty years of ploughing stony ground.

sentence: Hiems illa tam dūra fuit ut multī pauperēs in viīs perīrent.
translation: That winter was so harsh that many poor people died in the streets.

sentence: Māter pulvīnum mollī lānā implēvit ut īnfāns facilius dormīret.
translation: Mother stuffed the pillow with soft wool so the baby would sleep more easily.

sentence: Centuriō iuvenēs urbānōs mollēs vocābat, quod prīmō diē iam querēbantur.
translation: The centurion called the city boys soft, because they were complaining on the very first day.

sentence: Puella mollī vōce carmen cecinit, et omnēs convīvae subitō tacuērunt.
translation: The girl sang in a soft voice, and all the guests suddenly fell silent.

sentence: Amphora tam gravis erat ut duo bāiulī eam per scālās vix ferrent.
translation: The jar was so heavy that two porters could barely carry it up the stairs.

sentence: Medicus dīxit morbum gravem esse et mātrem tōtam noctem vigilāre iussit.
translation: The doctor said the illness was serious and told the mother to stay awake all night.

sentence: Gravis cūra mē premit, ex quō frāter meus in Hispāniam profectus est.
translation: A heavy worry has weighed on me ever since my brother set out for Spain.

sentence: Sarcinam levem sūmpsī, quod iter longum per montēs pedibus faciēbam.
translation: I took a light pack, because I was making the long mountain journey on foot.

sentence: Vulnus leve mīlitī fuit, itaque postrīdiē iam in statiōne stābat.
translation: The soldier's wound was slight, so the next day he was already back on guard duty.

sentence: Nōlī hominī levī crēdere: hodiē prōmittit, crās omnia oblītus est.
translation: Don't trust a fickle man: today he promises, tomorrow he has forgotten the whole thing.

sentence: Lūna tam clāra erat ut sine lucernā tōtam viam vidērēmus.
translation: The moon was so bright that we could see the whole road without a lamp.

sentence: Praecō vōce clārā nōmina victōrum prōnūntiāvit, et tōtum forum plausit.
translation: The herald announced the winners' names in a clear voice, and the whole forum applauded.

sentence: Avus meus in tōtā prōvinciā clārus erat, sed nunc nēmō eius meminit.
translation: My grandfather was famous throughout the province, but now nobody remembers him.

sentence: In cellā obscūrā diū quaesīvī, dōnec amphoram olīvārum tandem invēnī.
translation: I searched a long time in the dark cellar until I finally found the jar of olives.

sentence: Verba testāmentī tam obscūra erant ut iūdex duōs perītōs cōnsuleret.
translation: The wording of the will was so obscure that the judge consulted two experts.

sentence: Poēta locō obscūrō nātus erat, sed carmina eius nunc ubīque cantantur.
translation: The poet was born in an obscure place, yet his songs are sung everywhere now.

sentence: Ante iter māter ad larēs sānctōs tūs incendit et vōtum fēcit.
translation: Before the journey, mother burned incense at the holy household gods and made a vow.

sentence: Virginēs Vestālēs ignem sānctum cūrant, nec eum umquam exstinguī sinunt.
translation: The Vestal Virgins tend the holy fire and never let it go out.

sentence: Iūs hospitiī apud maiōrēs nostrōs sānctum erat; nēmō hospitem prōdēbat.
translation: Among our ancestors the law of hospitality was sacred; nobody betrayed a guest.

sentence: Agricolae quercum sacram Iovī caedere nōn audent, quamquam umbra segetēs premit.
translation: The farmers dare not fell the oak sacred to Jupiter, even though its shade smothers the crops.

sentence: Haec avis Iūnōnī sacra est, itaque sacerdōs eam in templō alit.
translation: This bird is sacred to Juno, so the priest keeps it fed inside the temple.

sentence: Diēs ille nōbīs sacer est: eō patrem meum ex bellō salvum recēpimus.
translation: That day is sacred to us: on it we got my father back safe from the war.

sentence: Rūmor dē incendiō falsus fuit; nihil praeter fūmum culīnae vīdimus.
translation: The rumour about the fire was false; we saw nothing but smoke from the kitchen.

sentence: Testis falsus in iūdiciō locūtus est, sed tabellae vēritātem statim patefēcērunt.
translation: A false witness spoke at the trial, but the documents revealed the truth at once.

sentence: Spēs falsa mē per tōtam hiemem tenuit; nāvis numquam in portum vēnit.
translation: A false hope kept me going all winter; the ship never came into harbour.

sentence: Māter mea herbās viridēs in hortō post culīnam cotīdiē rigat.
translation: My mother waters the green herbs in the garden behind the kitchen every day.

sentence: Mercātor in forō pallium viride vēndit, sed nēmō pretium solvere vult.
translation: A trader in the forum is selling a green cloak, but nobody is willing to pay his price.

sentence: Post imbrem collis viridis mihi pulchrior quam tōtum forum vidētur.
translation: After the rain the green hill looks lovelier to me than the whole forum.

sentence: Avia mea ānulum aureum in arcā sub lectō diū cēlāvit.
translation: My grandmother kept a gold ring hidden for years in a chest under her bed.

sentence: Mīlitēs corōnam auream imperātōrī in castrīs magnō cum clāmōre dedērunt.
translation: In camp the soldiers presented their general with a golden crown, cheering loudly.

sentence: Nummōs aureōs nōn amō; amīcōs fidēlēs plūris quam aurum aestimō.
translation: I have no love for gold coins; I value loyal friends more highly than gold.

sentence: Mēnsa nostra tam lāta est ut tōta familia commodē cēnāre possit.
translation: Our table is so wide that the whole household can dine at it in comfort.

sentence: Via Appia tam lāta est ut duo plaustra simul iter facere possint.
translation: The Appian Way is wide enough for two wagons to travel along it side by side.

sentence: Flūmen lātius erat quam exspectāveram, itaque trānsīre nōn ausus sum.
translation: The river was broader than I had expected, so I did not dare to cross it.

sentence: Scālae ad cēnāculum nostrum tam angustae sunt ut arcam ferre nōn possim.
translation: The stairs up to our flat are so narrow that I cannot carry a chest up them.

sentence: In viā angustā duo plaustra haesērunt, et tōta turba clāmāre coepit.
translation: Two wagons jammed in the narrow street, and the whole crowd started shouting.

sentence: Cubiculum angustum mihi numquam placuit, quod ibi spīrāre vix possum.
translation: I have never liked that narrow bedroom, because I can hardly breathe in there.

sentence: Hodiē plūrimī hospitēs vēnērunt, itaque māter plūs pānis coquere dēbuit.
translation: A great many guests turned up today, so mother had to bake more bread.

sentence: In forō plūrimī mercātōrēs mercēs suās sub sōle ārdentī vēndunt.
translation: In the forum a great many traders sell their wares under the blazing sun.

sentence: Plūrimum tempus in bibliothēcā cōnsūmpsī, sed nihil ūtile invēnī.
translation: I spent a huge amount of time in the library, but found nothing useful.

sentence: Māne faciem meam aquā frīgidā lavō, ut somnum omnem expellam.
translation: In the morning I wash my face with cold water to drive off the last of my sleep.

sentence: Ex faciē mercātōris statim intellēxī eum pretium nimis auxisse.
translation: From the trader's face I saw at once that he had put the price up too far.

sentence: Cum epistulam lēgisset, faciēs patris subitō pallida et trīstis facta est.
translation: When he had read the letter, my father's face suddenly turned pale and grim.

sentence: Puer ōs plēnum pōmōrum habēbat, itaque mātrī respondēre nōn poterat.
translation: The boy had his mouth full of apples, so he could not answer his mother.

sentence: In cūriā senātor ōs aperuit, sed prae timōre nūlla vōx exiit.
translation: In the senate house the senator opened his mouth, but fear left him without a voice.

sentence: Verba tam dūra ex ōre amīcī audīre sine dolōre nōn possum.
translation: I cannot hear such harsh words from a friend's mouth without being hurt.

sentence: Avus meus surdus est, itaque in aurem eius clārē clāmāre dēbeō.
translation: My grandfather is deaf, so I have to shout loudly right into his ear.

sentence: Servus dominō in aurem susurrāvit hospitēs iam ad iānuam stāre.
translation: The slave whispered in his master's ear that the guests were already at the door.

sentence: Aurēs meae tantō clāmōre in circō dolent ut domum redīre cupiam.
translation: My ears ache so much from the roar in the circus that I want to go home.

sentence: Cum cēpās secō, nāsus meus statim ārdet et oculī lacrimant.
translation: Whenever I chop onions, my nose starts burning at once and my eyes water.

sentence: Coquus nāsum super ollam tenuit et condīmentum deesse statim sēnsit.
translation: The cook held his nose over the pot and knew immediately that a spice was missing.

sentence: In pugnā nāsum frēgī, et nunc mē in speculō vidēre nōlō.
translation: I broke my nose in a fight, and now I hate looking at myself in the mirror.

sentence: Fīliolae meae dēns hodiē cecidit, et per tōtam domum rīdēns cucurrit.
translation: My little daughter lost a tooth today and ran laughing all through the house.

sentence: Medicus dentem putridum forcipe extrāxit, dum servī mē firmē tenent.
translation: The doctor pulled the rotten tooth out with forceps while the slaves held me down.

sentence: Propter dentem dolentem tōtam noctem vigilāvī et nēminem vidēre volēbam.
translation: An aching tooth kept me awake all night, and I wanted to see nobody.

sentence: Culīna fūmō plēna erat, quod ancilla ignem nimis magnum fēcerat.
translation: The kitchen was full of smoke, because the maid had built too big a fire.

sentence: Forum hodiē plēnum est mercātōrum clāmantium, itaque per angiportum ambulāre mālō.
translation: The forum today is full of shouting traders, so I would rather walk down the side alley.

sentence: Epistula tua plēna querēlārum fuit, sed tamen eam laetus lēgī.
translation: Your letter was full of complaints, but I was still glad to read it.

sentence: Cum domum vēnissēmus, mēnsa vacua erat, quod canis cēnam nostram cōnsūmpserat.
translation: When we got home the table was bare, because the dog had eaten our dinner.

sentence: Post merīdiem taberna vacua manet, itaque tabernārius sōlus latrunculīs lūdit.
translation: After midday the shop stays empty, so the shopkeeper plays draughts by himself.

sentence: Postquam frāter Rōmam profectus est, cubiculum eius vacuum mihi trīste vidētur.
translation: Ever since my brother left for Rome, his empty room strikes me as a sad place.

sentence: Vīcīnus noster pauper est, sed cotīdiē nōbīs ōva sua dōnat.
translation: Our neighbour is poor, yet every day he gives us his eggs for nothing.

sentence: Medicus etiam pauperēs grātīs cūrat, quia ipse in Subūrā nātus est.
translation: The doctor treats even the poor for free, because he was born in the Subura himself.

sentence: Pater meus pauper erat, sed nēminem umquam beātiōrem vīdī.
translation: My father was a poor man, but I have never seen anyone happier.

sentence: Tabellārius celer epistulam tuam ante merīdiem ad vīllam pertulit.
translation: A quick courier got your letter out to the villa before noon.

sentence: In circō equōs celerēs spectāvimus dōnec sōl post montēs cecidit.
translation: At the circus we watched the fast horses until the sun went down behind the hills.

sentence: Mīror quam celer sit puer noster, cum nūper vix ambulāret.
translation: It amazes me how fast our boy is, when not long ago he could barely walk.

sentence: Avia tarda per hortum ambulat, sed omnēs flōrēs suōs nōmine vocat.
translation: Grandmother walks slowly through the garden, but she calls every one of her flowers by name.

sentence: Servus tardus aquam sērō attulit, postquam hospitēs iam discesserant.
translation: The slow slave brought the water too late, after the guests had already gone.

sentence: Discipulus tardus esse vidētur, sed omnia altius quam cēterī intellegit.
translation: The pupil seems slow, but he understands everything more deeply than the rest do.

sentence: Māter mihi lac calidum ante somnum dabat, cum parvulus essem.
translation: Mother used to give me warm milk before bed when I was little.

sentence: In thermīs diū in aquā calidā sedēmus et dē rēbus urbānīs colloquimur.
translation: At the baths we sit a long while in the hot water and talk over the city news.

sentence: Tam calidus erat diēs ut nēmō in forō diū manēret.
translation: The day was so hot that nobody stayed in the forum for long.

sentence: Aqua in puteō tam frīgida est ut manūs statim doleant.
translation: The water in the well is so cold that your hands ache at once.

sentence: Mīlitēs in castrīs hiemem frīgidam patiuntur et ignēs tōtā nocte alunt.
translation: In camp the soldiers endure a freezing winter and keep the fires fed all night.

sentence: Nihil mihi molestius est quam ventus frīgidus quī per fenestram irrumpit.
translation: Nothing annoys me more than the cold wind that bursts in through the window.

sentence: Ancilla vestem albam lāvit, quod crās nūptiae sorōris meae erunt.
translation: The maid washed the white dress, because my sister's wedding is tomorrow.

sentence: Sacerdōtēs bovem album ad āram dūcunt, dum populus tacitus spectat.
translation: The priests lead the white ox up to the altar while the crowd watches in silence.

sentence: Capillī patris iam albī sunt, quamquam sē iuvenem esse putat.
translation: Father's hair has gone white already, though he still thinks of himself as young.

sentence: Fēlēs nigra sub lectō sē cēlat, quotiēns hospitēs iānuam pulsant.
translation: The black cat hides under the bed every time visitors knock at the door.

sentence: Nautae nūbēs nigrās procul vīdērunt et vēla celeriter contrāxērunt.
translation: The sailors saw black clouds far off and quickly took in the sails.

sentence: Post mortem patris māter vestem nigram per tōtum annum gerēbat.
translation: After my father died, my mother wore black for a whole year.

sentence: Māla rubra dē arbore dēcidunt, et puerī ea in sinū portant.
translation: Red apples are dropping off the tree, and the boys carry them home in the fold of their tunics.

sentence: Caupō vīnum rubrum mihi obtulit, quod album iam dēfēcerat.
translation: The innkeeper offered me red wine, since the white had already run out.

sentence: Genae eius rubrae fīēbant, quotiēns dē nūptiīs futūrīs loquēbāmur.
translation: Her cheeks would turn red whenever we talked about the coming wedding.

sentence: Avus meus mīlle passūs cotīdiē ambulat, quamquam genua dolent.
translation: My grandfather walks a thousand paces every day, even though his knees ache.

sentence: Mercātor mīlle nummōs prō equō poposcit, sed pater meus rīsit.
translation: The dealer demanded a thousand coins for the horse, but my father just laughed.

sentence: Mīlle annōs stābit hoc templum, ut poēta superbē canēbat.
translation: This temple will stand for a thousand years, as the poet proudly used to sing.

sentence: Prīmā lūce coquus fornācem accendit, antequam dominus ē cubiculō vēnit.
translation: At first light the cook lit the oven, before the master came out of his bedroom.

sentence: Prīmus in cūriam vēnit senātor, ut locum meliōrem occupāret.
translation: The senator got into the senate house first, so as to grab a better seat.

sentence: Prīmus liber quem lēgī adhūc in memoriā manet.
translation: The first book I ever read still stays with me.

sentence: Secunda fīlia in hortō lūdit, dum prīma epistulās patris legit.
translation: The second daughter is playing in the garden while the eldest reads their father's letters.

sentence: Secundō locō ōrātor surrēxit et populum vehementer commōvit.
translation: Speaking second, the orator rose and stirred the crowd powerfully.

sentence: In lūdīs secundus ēvāsit, itaque per tōtam noctem tacitus sēdit.
translation: He came out second at the games, and so he sat silent the whole night.

sentence: Tertium cubiculum avia occupat, quia fenestra eius in hortum spectat.
translation: Grandmother takes the third bedroom, because its window looks out onto the garden.

sentence: Tertiā hōrā magister discipulōs in umbrā porticūs docēbat.
translation: At the third hour the teacher was giving his pupils their lesson in the shade of the colonnade.

sentence: Tertiam iam epistulam mittō, sed amīcus meus nihil respondet.
translation: This is the third letter I am sending now, and my friend answers nothing.

sentence: Magnam partem cēnae canis noster arripuit, dum coquus vīnum petit.
translation: Our dog snatched a large part of the dinner while the cook went off for wine.

sentence: Pars mīlitum vallum fodiēbat, pars in silvā lignum caedēbat.
translation: Some of the soldiers were digging the rampart, others were cutting timber in the wood.

sentence: Dīmidiam partem hērēditātis sorōrī relīquit, et frātrēs statim īrātī sunt.
translation: He left half the inheritance to his sister, and his brothers were furious at once.

sentence: Bonum vīnum avus in cellā cēlat, nē hospitēs illud bibant.
translation: Grandfather hides the good wine down in the cellar, so the guests won't drink it.

sentence: In tabernā bonum pānem ēmimus, quia pistor tōtā nocte labōrāverat.
translation: We bought good bread at the shop, because the baker had been working all night.

sentence: Bonus amīcus tacet cum tacēre oportet, et hoc rārum est.
translation: A good friend keeps quiet when quiet is what's needed, and that is rare.

sentence: Mala tempestās tēctum nostrum frēgit, et tōtā nocte aquam exhausimus.
translation: A bad storm broke our roof, and we were bailing water out all night.

sentence: Malus servus vīnum dominī bibit et amphoram vacuam sub lectō cēlāvit.
translation: A bad slave drank the master's wine and hid the empty jar under the couch.

sentence: Malōs mōrēs poēta reprehendit, sed populus in theātrō tantum rīsit.
translation: The poet attacked the bad morals of the day, but the crowd in the theatre only laughed.

sentence: Magna arbor in hortō stat, et sub eā aestāte cēnāmus.
translation: A big tree stands in the garden, and in summer we eat our dinner under it.

sentence: Magnus clāmor in Circō ortus est, cum equī ultimum spatium currerent.
translation: A huge roar went up in the Circus as the horses ran the final lap.

sentence: Magnum est amīcum in perīculō nōn dēserere, etiam cum omnēs fugiunt.
translation: It is a great thing not to abandon a friend in danger, even when everyone else runs.

sentence: Parva fīlia sub mēnsā sedēbat et canem pāne clam pāscēbat.
translation: The little daughter was sitting under the table, secretly feeding the dog scraps of bread.

sentence: In parvā tabernā sūtor tōtum diem calceōs mīlitum reficiēbat.
translation: In his small shop the cobbler spent the whole day mending soldiers' boots.

sentence: Parvum mūnus ex Aegyptō mīsit, sed mihi cārius fuit quam aurum.
translation: He sent a small gift from Egypt, but to me it was worth more than gold.

sentence: Multae ovēs in agrō nostrō errant, quia puer portam aperuit.
translation: Many sheep are wandering loose in our field, because the boy left the gate open.

sentence: Multī clientēs ante ātrium stābant, dum patrōnus lentē togam induit.
translation: Many clients were standing outside the hall while their patron slowly put on his toga.

sentence: Multa dē bellō nārrāvit avus, sed nōmina numquam commemorāvit.
translation: Grandfather told us many things about the war, but he never mentioned any names.

sentence: Hieme nox longa est; lucernam ter replēre dēbeō antequam dormiō.
translation: In winter the night is long; I have to refill the lamp three times before I sleep.

sentence: Via Appia longa est, sed mīlitēs ante noctem ad castra pervēnērunt.
translation: The Appian Way is long, but the soldiers reached camp before nightfall.

sentence: Cōnsulis ōrātiō tam longa erat ut senātōrēs tacitī obdormīrent.
translation: The consul's speech was so long that the senators quietly fell asleep.

sentence: Puteus noster altus est; aqua frīgida etiam aestāte manet.
translation: Our well is deep; the water stays cold even in summer.

sentence: Mūrī urbis tam altī sunt ut hostēs scālās longissimās parent.
translation: The city walls are so high that the enemy are getting very long ladders ready.

sentence: Altum mare timeō, quamquam frāter meus longē ā lītore natat.
translation: I am afraid of the deep sea, although my brother swims far out from the shore.

sentence: Novum tēctum fēcimus, quod hieme aqua in ātrium fluēbat.
translation: We put on a new roof, because in winter the water used to run into the atrium.

sentence: Novus magister in lūdō sedet et nōmina discipulōrum lentē recitat.
translation: The new teacher sits in the schoolroom and slowly reads out the pupils' names.

sentence: Avus meus nihil novī amat, nē novum quidem vīnum.
translation: My grandfather loves nothing new — not even new wine.

sentence: Vetus mēnsa in culīnā adhūc stat, quamquam ūnum pedem āmīsit.
translation: The old table is still standing in the kitchen, although it has lost one leg.

sentence: In tabernā mīles vetus dē proeliīs suīs saepe nārrat.
translation: In the tavern an old soldier often tells the tale of his own battles.

sentence: Veterēs amīcōs mālō quam novōs, sīcut vīnum vetus.
translation: I prefer old friends to new ones, just as I prefer old wine.

sentence: In hortō nummum antīquum invēnī, quem avus meus statim agnōvit.
translation: In the garden I found an ancient coin, which my grandfather recognised at once.

sentence: Templum antīquum in forō stat, et multī peregrīnī id spectant.
translation: An ancient temple stands in the forum, and many visitors from abroad come to look at it.

sentence: Antīquōs mōrēs laudāmus, sed paucī nostrum eōs hodiē servant.
translation: We praise the old ways, but few of us actually keep them nowadays.

sentence: Rosae in hortō pulchrae sunt, sed spīnae digitōs meōs vulnerant.
translation: The roses in the garden are beautiful, but the thorns keep cutting my fingers.

sentence: Artifex statuam pulchram in forō posuit, et populus plausit.
translation: The sculptor set up a beautiful statue in the forum, and the crowd applauded.

sentence: Cantrīx nōn pulchra est, sed vōx eius tōtum theātrum tenet.
translation: The singer is not beautiful, but her voice holds the whole theatre.

sentence: Fīlia mea fortis est: vulnus lavat neque lacrimam ūllam fundit.
translation: My daughter is brave: she washes the wound and does not shed a single tear.

sentence: Centuriō mīlitēs fortēs laudāvit, quod portam per tōtam noctem tenuērunt.
translation: The centurion praised the brave soldiers, because they held the gate all night long.

sentence: Fortior mihi vidētur agricola quī sōlus contrā tempestātem labōrat.
translation: To me the farmer who works alone against the storm seems the braver man.

sentence: Avus meus servus fuit; nunc līber cum familiā suā habitat.
translation: My grandfather was a slave; now he lives as a free man with his own family.

sentence: Cīvitās nostra lībera manet, dum cīvēs lēgēs sine metū servant.
translation: Our state stays free as long as the citizens keep the laws without fear.

sentence: Avem ē caveā ēmīsī, et lībera trāns hortum ēvolāvit.
translation: I let the bird out of its cage, and free at last it flew off across the garden.

sentence: Hodiē fēlīx fuī, quod ānulum āmissum sub lectō invēnī.
translation: Today I was lucky, because I found the lost ring under the bed.

sentence: Mercātor sē fēlīcem vocat, quod nāvēs eius tūtae domum rediērunt.
translation: The merchant calls himself a lucky man, because his ships came home safe.

sentence: Fēlīcēs sunt quī cum amīcīs cēnant, etiam sine vīnō bonō.
translation: Happy are the people who dine with friends, even when there is no good wine.

sentence: Canis miser ante iānuam sedet et per tōtam noctem ululat.
translation: The wretched dog sits at the front door and howls the whole night through.

sentence: Miserī in viīs dormiunt, dum dīvitēs in thermīs sē lavant.
translation: The wretched sleep in the streets while the rich are bathing at the baths.

sentence: Mē miserum! Epistulam exspectō quae numquam ā tē venit.
translation: Poor me! I keep waiting for a letter that never comes from you.

sentence: Per nivem in montibus dux noster nōbīs viam tandem invēnit.
translation: In the snow up in the mountains our guide finally found us a way through.

sentence: Mīlitēs fessī ducem in castrīs per tōtam noctem exspectābant.
translation: The exhausted soldiers waited in camp for their general the whole night.

sentence: Nēmō ducī crēdit quī mīlitēs suōs in perīculum semper mittit.
translation: Nobody trusts a leader who is forever sending his own men into danger.

sentence: Imperātor ipse per forum ambulābat, et omnēs tabernāriī tacuērunt.
translation: The emperor himself was walking through the forum, and every shopkeeper fell silent.

sentence: Post victōriam mīlitēs ducem suum in castrīs imperātōrem salūtāvērunt.
translation: After the victory the soldiers in camp hailed their general as commander.

sentence: Imperātōris īram timēmus, quia nūllī senātōrī adhūc pepercit.
translation: We are afraid of the emperor's anger, since he has spared no senator so far.

sentence: Cōnsul novus ante lūcem surrēxit ut auspicia in Capitōliō caperet.
translation: The new consul got up before dawn to take the auspices on the Capitol.

sentence: Clientēs cōnsulem domī salūtant priusquam ille in forum dēscendat.
translation: His clients greet the consul at his house before he goes down to the forum.

sentence: Cōnsulis ōrātiō tam longa erat ut senātōrēs paene obdormīrent.
translation: The consul's speech went on so long that the senators nearly fell asleep.

sentence: Māne in cūriā convēnit senātus, quod nūntius ex Galliā vēnerat.
translation: The senate met in the senate house at dawn, because a messenger had arrived from Gaul.

sentence: Avus meus ex senātū sērō rediit et cēnam frīgidam invēnit.
translation: My grandfather came home late from the senate and found his dinner cold.

sentence: Multī senātum culpant, quod frūmentum plēbī hōc annō nōn dedit.
translation: Plenty of people blame the senate for giving the common folk no grain this year.

sentence: Cōnsul lēgem novam in forō recitāvit, et populus vehementer clāmāvit.
translation: The consul read out the new law in the forum, and the crowd shouted furiously.

sentence: Domī nostrae lēx est ut nēmō ante patrem cēnāre incipiat.
translation: The rule in our house is that nobody starts eating before father does.

sentence: Lēgibus pārēre difficile est, cum iūdicēs ipsī pecūniam accipiant.
translation: Obeying the laws is hard when the judges themselves are taking bribes.

sentence: Frāter meus iūs suum in iūdiciō fortiter dēfendit et vīcit.
translation: My brother defended his rights stoutly in court and won the case.

sentence: Cīvēs Rōmānī iūre suffrāgiī in comitiīs quotannīs ūtēbantur.
translation: Roman citizens exercised their right to vote in the assemblies every year.

sentence: Quid est iūs, sī potentēs iniūriās semper impūne faciunt?
translation: What is justice worth, if the powerful always do harm and go unpunished?

sentence: Post mortem ducis imperium exercitūs cōnsulī novō trāditum est.
translation: After the general's death command of the army was handed over to the new consul.

sentence: Mercātōrēs per tōtum imperium mercēs vehunt, ā Britanniā usque ad Syriam.
translation: Traders carry their goods across the whole empire, from Britain all the way to Syria.

sentence: Sub imperiō Rōmānō nātus sum, sed linguae patriae nōn oblīvīscor.
translation: I was born under Roman rule, but I have not forgotten my native language.

sentence: Trāns montēs iacet rēgnum in quō nēmō umquam bellum vīdit.
translation: Beyond the mountains lies a kingdom where nobody has ever seen a war.

sentence: Rōmānī rēgnum ōdērunt et rēgēs ex urbe ōlim expulērunt.
translation: The Romans hated the very idea of monarchy and drove the kings out of the city long ago.

sentence: Duo frātrēs dē rēgnō patris ācriter certābant, dum māter flēbat.
translation: Two brothers were quarrelling bitterly over their father's kingdom while their mother wept.

sentence: Post multōs annōs mīlitī fidēlī cīvitās Rōmāna tandem data est.
translation: After many years of service the loyal soldier was finally granted Roman citizenship.

sentence: Hostēs cīvitātem nostram trēs mēnsēs obsēdērunt, sed numquam cēpērunt.
translation: The enemy besieged our city-state for three months but never took it.

sentence: Cīvitātis nostrae lēgēs mē melius quam mūrī altī dēfendunt.
translation: The laws of our state protect me better than high walls ever could.

sentence: Exercitus per nivem trēs diēs iter fēcit et multōs mīlitēs āmīsit.
translation: The army marched through the snow for three days and lost many of its soldiers.

sentence: Fīlius meus iam decem annōs in exercitū Rōmānō mīlitat.
translation: My son has been serving in the Roman army for ten years now.

sentence: Timēmus exercitum quī per agrōs nostrōs sine duce vagātur.
translation: We are afraid of an army that wanders across our fields with nobody commanding it.

sentence: Lapis ingēns in mediā viā iacēbat, itaque plaustrum nostrum trānsīre nōn poterat.
translation: A huge stone was lying in the middle of the road, so our wagon could not get past.

sentence: Fabrī lapidēs ex monte ad templum novum cotīdiē trahēbant.
translation: Every day the workmen dragged stones down from the mountain to the new temple.

sentence: Puer īrātus lapidem in canem iēcit, sed statim eum factī paenituit.
translation: The angry boy threw a stone at the dog, but he regretted it at once.

sentence: Ventus per fenestram apertam irrūpit et omnēs tabulās meās dispersit.
translation: The wind burst in through the open window and scattered all my writing tablets.

sentence: Nautae in portū manēbant, quod ventus adversus nāvēs exīre vetābat.
translation: The sailors stayed in the harbour, because a headwind kept the ships from sailing.

sentence: Nocte ventus inter arborēs ita gemuit ut puerī somnum capere nōn possent.
translation: At night the wind moaned in the trees so loudly that the boys could not get to sleep.

sentence: Nūbēs ātrae dē montibus dēscendunt, itaque agricolae in vīllam properant.
translation: Black clouds are coming down off the mountains, so the farmers hurry back to the farmhouse.

sentence: Augur nūbēs diū spectāvit et populō tempestātem crāstinam praedīxit.
translation: The augur watched the clouds for a long time and told the people what tomorrow's weather would be.

sentence: Māter mea semper trīstis est cum nūbēs sōlem tōtum diem operiunt.
translation: My mother is always low when the clouds cover the sun all day long.

sentence: Imber tōtam noctem cecidit et aqua per tēctum in culīnam mānāvit.
translation: Rain fell all night and water trickled through the roof into the kitchen.

sentence: Imbre subitō oppressī, mercātōrēs mercēs suās sub porticum tulērunt.
translation: Caught by a sudden downpour, the traders carried their goods in under the colonnade.

sentence: Diū siccitātem passī, agricolae hunc imbrem dōnum deōrum vocābant.
translation: After enduring a long drought, the farmers called this rain a gift from the gods.

sentence: Nix tantā altitūdine cecidit ut portam vīllae aperīre nōn possēmus.
translation: The snow fell so deep that we could not get the farmhouse gate open.

sentence: Mercātor iter per Alpēs distulit, quod nix omnēs viās clauserat.
translation: The merchant put off his journey over the Alps, because snow had closed every road.

sentence: Puerī nive gaudent, sed senēs eam ōdērunt, quia ossa eōrum dolent.
translation: Children delight in the snow, but old men hate it, because it makes their bones ache.

sentence: Māter nostra frūmentum ad pistrīnum tulit ut pānem ad cēnam coqueret.
translation: Our mother took the grain to the mill so she could bake bread for dinner.

sentence: Legiōnēs sine frūmentō trēs diēs mānsērunt, quod nāvēs tempestās retinēbat.
translation: The legions went three days without grain, because a storm was holding the ships back.

sentence: Post grandinem agricola frūmentum āmissum flēvit, quod nihil in horreō relictum erat.
translation: After the hailstorm the farmer wept over his ruined wheat, since nothing was left in the barn.

sentence: Post cēnam in herbā sub arbore iacēbāmus et stēllās numerābāmus.
translation: After dinner we lay on the grass under the tree and counted the stars.

sentence: Medicus herbās amārās contrīvit et vulnus mīlitis dīligenter cūrāvit.
translation: The doctor ground up bitter herbs and carefully dressed the soldier's wound.

sentence: Pāstor timēbat nē ovēs herbam in campō ūstō invenīre nōn possent.
translation: The shepherd was afraid that the sheep would find no grass on the scorched plain.

sentence: Quīnque cīvēs ante domum nostram dē pretiō frūmentī vehementer disputābant.
translation: Five citizens were arguing furiously outside our house about the price of grain.

sentence: Cīvēs Rōmānī in comitiīs suffrāgium ferunt et magistrātūs novōs creant.
translation: Roman citizens cast their votes in the assembly and elect the new magistrates.

sentence: Mārcus sē cīvem Rōmānum esse clāmāvit, itaque lictor virgās statim dēposuit.
translation: Marcus shouted that he was a Roman citizen, and the lictor lowered his rods at once.

sentence: Mīles vulnerātus ad casam nostram vēnit et aquam frīgidam rogāvit.
translation: A wounded soldier came to our cottage and asked for cold water.

sentence: Mīlitēs fossam ante castra tōtum diem sub sōle fōdērunt.
translation: The soldiers dug a ditch in front of the camp all day under the sun.

sentence: Māter mīlitis epistulās ex Germāniā legēbat et tacitē lacrimābat.
translation: The soldier's mother was reading his letters from Germany and quietly weeping.

sentence: Cīvēs portās clausērunt, quod hostis ad mūrōs nocte appropinquābat.
translation: The citizens shut the gates, because the enemy was coming up to the walls during the night.

sentence: Dux noster hostium castra explōrāvit et cōnsilium novum centuriōnibus aperuit.
translation: Our general scouted the enemy's camp and laid a new plan before the centurions.

sentence: Avus meus semper dīcēbat nūllum hostem crūdēliōrem quam famem esse.
translation: My grandfather always used to say that no enemy is crueller than hunger.

sentence: Tōtā nocte in agrō labōrāvī, et dolor umerōrum mihi somnum abstulit.
translation: I worked in the field all night, and the ache in my shoulders robbed me of sleep.

sentence: Medicus dolōrem dentis meī herbīs amārīs per trēs diēs levāvit.
translation: The doctor eased my toothache with bitter herbs over three days.

sentence: Nūntiō audītō, māter tantō dolōre affecta est ut loquī nōn posset.
translation: When she heard the news, the mother was struck by such grief that she could not speak.

sentence: Cum pater aeger esset, māter cōnsilium cēpit agrum vīcīnō locāre.
translation: When father fell ill, mother formed a plan to rent the field out to a neighbour.

sentence: Dux, mīlitibus in castrīs convocātīs, cōnsilium dē pugnā crāstinā habuit.
translation: With the soldiers summoned into camp, the general held a council about tomorrow's battle.

sentence: Utinam cōnsiliō tuō pāruissem: nunc pecūniam omnem in mercātū perdidī.
translation: If only I had followed your advice — now I have lost every coin at the market.

sentence: Quaerēbam causam strepitūs, sed in culīnā nihil nisi fēlem invēnī.
translation: I was hunting for the cause of the noise, but in the kitchen I found nothing but the cat.

sentence: Ōrātor causam agricolae pauperis apud iūdicem tōtum diem ēgit.
translation: The advocate pleaded the poor farmer's case before the judge for a whole day.

sentence: Nōn pecūniae causā labōrō, sed ut līberī meī scholam adeant.
translation: I don't work for the sake of money, but so that my children can go to school.

sentence: Avia mihi modum mōnstrāvit quō pānis sine furnō coquī possit.
translation: Grandmother showed me the way bread can be baked without an oven.

sentence: Fabrī tēctum eōdem modō reficiunt quō maiōrēs eōrum reficiēbant.
translation: The workmen are repairing the roof in the same way their forefathers used to repair it.

sentence: Frāter meus nūllum modum in emendō tenet: iam ter aes aliēnum contrāxit.
translation: My brother keeps no limit on his spending — he has already run into debt three times.

sentence: Hoc genus pānis avia mea ex farre et melle coquere solēbat.
translation: My grandmother used to bake this kind of bread out of emmer and honey.

sentence: Mercātor omne genus mercium in forō vēndit, ā fīcīs ad ferrum.
translation: The trader sells every sort of goods in the forum, from figs to iron.

sentence: Quamquam humilī genere nātus est, ā tōtā cīvitāte propter virtūtem colitur.
translation: Although he was born of humble stock, the whole city honours him for his courage.

sentence: Hodiē domī multum negōtiī habeō: tēctum stillat et furnus frāctus est.
translation: I have a great deal to do at home today: the roof is dripping and the oven is broken.

sentence: Pater meus Brundisium profectus est negōtiī causā, nec ante Kalendās redībit.
translation: My father has set out for Brundisium on business, and he will not be back before the first of the month.

sentence: Nūllum negōtium mihi molestius est quam cum sordidīs pūblicānīs disputāre.
translation: No task irritates me more than arguing with grubby tax-collectors.

sentence: Post messem paucōs diēs ōtiī habēmus, quōs in umbrā fīcī cōnsūmimus.
translation: After the harvest we have a few days of leisure, which we spend in the shade of the fig tree.

sentence: Senātor negōtiīs urbis fessus ad vīllam sēcessit ut ōtiō litterīsque fruerētur.
translation: Worn out by the city's affairs, the senator withdrew to his country house to enjoy leisure and literature.

sentence: Ōtium sine librīs mē magis fatīgat quam labor ipse in agrīs.
translation: Leisure without books tires me more than the work in the fields itself.

sentence: Fīlia maior officium suum esse putat parentēs senēs domī cūrāre.
translation: The elder daughter considers it her duty to look after her aged parents at home.

sentence: Custōs portae officiō suō tam dīligenter fungitur ut nēminem sine tesserā admittat.
translation: The gatekeeper performs his duty so scrupulously that he lets no one in without a token.

sentence: Prō tantō officiō tibi grātiās agō: sine tē causam āmīsissem.
translation: I thank you for such a kindness: without you I would have lost the case.

sentence: Fēlēs tōtum merīdiem in gradū calidō iacet nec ūllum mūrem capit.
translation: The cat lies on the warm doorstep all midday long and catches not a single mouse.

sentence: Post pugnam multa arma per campum iacēbant, quae agricolae mox collēgērunt.
translation: After the battle a great deal of weaponry lay scattered across the plain, and the farmers soon gathered it up.

sentence: Tōtam noctem vigil iacuī, dum ventus fenestram sine fīne pulsat.
translation: I lay awake the whole night while the wind beat at the window without stopping.

sentence: Puerī nūdīs pedibus per hortum currunt, dum māter pānem in furnō coquit.
translation: The boys are running barefoot through the garden while their mother bakes bread in the oven.

sentence: Nūntius per tōtam noctem cucurrit ut epistulam ducī ante proelium trāderet.
translation: The messenger ran all night so as to hand the letter to the general before the battle.

sentence: Tonitrū audītō, tam celeriter domum cucurrī ut calceum in viā āmitterem.
translation: At the sound of the thunder I ran home so fast that I lost a shoe in the road.

sentence: Avus meus dē proeliō Cannēnsī loquitur, quotiēns nimium vīnī bibit.
translation: My grandfather talks about the battle of Cannae whenever he drinks too much wine.

sentence: Ante proelium mīlitēs in castrīs gladiōs acuunt et deōs ōrant.
translation: Before the battle the soldiers sharpen their swords in camp and pray to the gods.

sentence: Illud proelium tam ātrōx fuit ut nēmō dē eō libenter nārret.
translation: That battle was so savage that nobody willingly speaks about it.

sentence: Post victōriam pater noster corōnam laureām in ātriō suspendit.
translation: After the victory our father hung a laurel wreath up in the atrium.

sentence: Victōria ducis nostrī tōtum forum hodiē corōnīs et lucernīs implēvit.
translation: Our general's victory has filled the whole forum today with garlands and lamps.

sentence: Hāc victōriā nēmō vērē laetātur, cum tot cīvēs ceciderint.
translation: Nobody really rejoices in this victory, since so many citizens have fallen.

sentence: Puer imāginēs maiōrum in ātriō spectat et glōriam eōrum aemulātur.
translation: The boy looks at the ancestors' masks in the atrium and strives to match their glory.

sentence: Multī iuvenēs glōriā ductī ad extrēmās Britanniae ōrās nāvigāvērunt.
translation: Many young men, drawn on by glory, sailed to the farthest shores of Britain.

sentence: Glōria imperātōris cito perit, nisi poētae eam carminibus servāverint.
translation: A general's fame dies quickly unless poets preserve it in their songs.

sentence: Māter mea virtūtem in fīliābus magis quam fōrmam laudāre solet.
translation: My mother tends to praise character in her daughters more than good looks.

sentence: Centuriō virtūte suā aciem hostium prīmus perrūpit et corōnam accēpit.
translation: By his own courage the centurion was first to break the enemy line, and he received a crown.

sentence: Virtūs sōla, nōn cēnsus, hominem apud maiōrēs nostrōs nōbilem faciēbat.
translation: Among our ancestors it was character alone, not wealth, that made a man noble.

sentence: Vīcīnus meus mihi sine tabulīs pecūniam crēdidit; tantam fidem habēbat.
translation: My neighbour lent me money without any written contract; that was how much he trusted me.

sentence: Dux hostium, fidē datā, captīvōs nostrōs incolumēs ad castra remīsit.
translation: The enemy commander gave his word and sent our prisoners back to camp unharmed.

sentence: Nūlla amīcitia diū manet in quā fidēs semel violāta est.
translation: No friendship lasts long once trust in it has been broken.

sentence: Agricola siccōs agrōs spectāns spem pluviae nōndum dēposuit.
translation: Looking at his dried-out fields, the farmer has not yet given up hope of rain.

sentence: Mercātōrēs in portū spē lucrī nāvēs etiam per hiemem mittunt.
translation: In the harbour the merchants send ships out even through winter in hope of profit.

sentence: Spēs ultima aegrōtī in medicō Graecō ā familiā posita erat.
translation: The sick man's last hope had been placed by his household in a Greek doctor.

sentence: Puer parvus timōre tonitrūs sub lectō mātris tōtam noctem latuit.
translation: Out of fear of the thunder the little boy stayed hidden under his mother's bed all night.

sentence: Nautae timōrem tempestātis vīnō et cantū inter sē cēlābant.
translation: The sailors hid their fear of the storm from one another with wine and singing.

sentence: Timor poenae multōs continet quōs pudor continēre nōn potest.
translation: Fear of punishment holds back many people whom shame cannot hold back.

sentence: Pater amōre fīliae victus nūptiās cum paupere iuvene tandem permīsit.
translation: Won over by love for his daughter, the father finally allowed her marriage to a poor young man.

sentence: Iuvenis amōrem suum in pariete tabernae carmine brevī scrīpsit.
translation: The young man wrote about his love on the tavern wall in a short verse.

sentence: Amor patriae mīlitem in Germāniā retinēbat, quamquam uxor domum vocābat.
translation: Love of his country kept the soldier in Germany, although his wife was calling him home.

sentence: Coquus īrā commōtus patinam in pavīmentum culīnae statim iēcit.
translation: Stirred up by anger, the cook threw the dish straight onto the kitchen floor.

sentence: Dominus īram in servum innocentem effūdit, deinde tacuit ērubēscēns.
translation: The master poured out his anger on an innocent slave, then fell silent, blushing.

sentence: Īra populī, ubi pānis in forō dēest, nūllō ēdictō comprimitur.
translation: When there is no bread in the market, the people's anger is checked by no decree.

sentence: Māter, cum fīlium incolumem vīdisset, gaudiō lacrimāre subitō coepit.
translation: When the mother saw her son safe and sound, she suddenly began to weep for joy.

sentence: Tōta vīcīnia gaudium nostrum in nūptiīs vīnō et saltātiōne celebrāvit.
translation: The whole neighbourhood celebrated our joy at the wedding with wine and dancing.

sentence: Brevia sunt agricolae gaudia, sī grandō vīneās ūnā nocte perdidit.
translation: A farmer's joys are short-lived if hail has ruined the vines in a single night.

sentence: Avis sub tēctō vīllae nīdum fēcit et nōs prīmā lūce excitat.
translation: A bird has built its nest under the roof of the villa, and it wakes us at first light.

sentence: Augur in arce sedet et avem ā sinistrā volantem exspectat.
translation: The augur sits on the citadel and waits for a bird to come flying from the left.

sentence: Avī captae lībertātem reddidī, quod eam in caveā morī nōlēbam.
translation: I gave the captured bird its freedom back, because I did not want it to die in a cage.

sentence: Piscis, quem herī ēmī, in culīnā iam male olet.
translation: The fish I bought yesterday is already going off in the kitchen.

sentence: Piscātor Ōstiae rēte trahit, sed hodiē paucōs piscēs cēpit.
translation: The fisherman at Ostia hauls in his net, but today he has caught only a few fish.

sentence: Avunculus meus tam grandem piscem cēpit ut nēmō eī crēderet.
translation: My uncle caught a fish so huge that nobody would believe him.

sentence: Puer parvus leōnem in pariete pictum vīdit et statim ad mātrem cucurrit.
translation: The little boy saw a lion painted on the wall and ran straight to his mother.

sentence: Leō ē caveā ēmissus harēnam circumit, dum spectātōrēs clāmant.
translation: Released from its cage, the lion prowls around the arena while the spectators roar.

sentence: Leōnis vestīgia in pulvere vīdimus, et nēmō nostrum ultrā prōcēdere voluit.
translation: We saw a lion's tracks in the dust, and none of us was willing to go any further.

sentence: Nocte lupī ululātum audīvimus, et omnēs canēs in vīllā lātrāvērunt.
translation: In the night we heard a wolf howling, and every dog on the farm started barking.

sentence: Pāstōrēs lupum in ovīle irrumpentem vīdērunt, sed duōs agnōs āmīsērunt.
translation: The shepherds saw a wolf breaking into the fold, but they still lost two lambs.

sentence: Dē Mārcō loquēbāmur, cum subitō ipse intrāvit: lupus in fābulā!
translation: We were talking about Marcus when in he walked himself — speak of the devil!

sentence: Ovēs nostrae in prātō pāscuntur, dum puer eās ā lupīs custōdit.
translation: Our sheep are grazing in the meadow while the boy keeps them safe from wolves.

sentence: Ante bellum cōnsul ovem albam Mārtī prō exercitū nostrō immolāvit.
translation: Before the war the consul sacrificed a white sheep to Mars on behalf of our army.

sentence: Ūna ovis ē grege aberrāvit, et pāstor tōtam noctem eam quaesīvit.
translation: A single sheep wandered off from the flock, and the shepherd spent the whole night looking for it.

sentence: Ex fenestrā cubiculī nostrī mōns nive tēctus tōtā hieme vidētur.
translation: From our bedroom window the mountain can be seen covered in snow all winter long.

sentence: Mīlitēs nostrī per montem angustā viā iter fēcērunt, quod hostēs vallem tenēbant.
translation: Our soldiers marched over the mountain by a narrow path, because the enemy held the valley.

sentence: In summō monte cōnstitimus, et tōtum mare sub nōbīs iacēre vīdimus.
translation: We stopped at the summit of the mountain and saw the whole sea lying below us.

sentence: Puerī aestāte in flūmine natant, dum mātrēs in rīpā vestīmenta lavant.
translation: In summer the boys swim in the river while their mothers wash the clothes on the bank.

sentence: Mercātōrēs frūmentum nāvibus per flūmen ab Ōstiā ad urbem cotīdiē vehunt.
translation: Merchants bring grain up the river from Ostia to the city by boat every day.

sentence: Flūmen tantā vī crēvit ut pontem veterem ūnā nocte tōtum auferret.
translation: The river rose with such force that in a single night it swept the old bridge clean away.

sentence: Māne in silvam īmus, ut lignum et fungōs ante prandium colligāmus.
translation: In the morning we go into the woods to gather firewood and mushrooms before lunch.

sentence: Servī arborēs in silvā caedunt, quod dominus novam vīllam aedificāre vult.
translation: The slaves are felling trees in the wood because the master wants to build a new villa.

sentence: Silva nocte tam obscūra erat ut nēmō nostrum sōlus prōgredī audēret.
translation: The wood was so dark at night that none of us dared to go on alone.

sentence: Sub arbore in hortō sedēmus, quia sōl merīdiē nimis ārdet.
translation: We sit under the tree in the garden, because the sun burns too fiercely at midday.

sentence: Arbor vetus nocte in viam cecidit, et nēmō iam carrō trānsīre potest.
translation: An old tree fell across the road in the night, and now no cart can get through.

sentence: Avus meus hanc arborem sēvit, ut nepōtēs ōlim sub eā sedērent.
translation: My grandfather planted this tree so that his grandchildren would one day sit in its shade.

sentence: Puella flōrēs in hortō carpit, ut mēnsam ad cēnam ōrnet.
translation: The girl is picking flowers in the garden to decorate the table for dinner.

sentence: Spōnsa corōnam flōrum gerit, dum amīcae ante iānuam carmina canunt.
translation: The bride is wearing a garland of flowers while her friends sing outside the door.

sentence: Flōs, quem mihi dedistī, iam āruit, sed eum adhūc in librō servō.
translation: The flower you gave me has dried up, but I still keep it pressed in a book.

sentence: Noctū hortum meum ā vulpibus canibusque vīcīnī sōlus dēfendō.
translation: At night I guard my garden all alone against the foxes and the neighbour's dogs.

sentence: In forō reum pauperem contrā potentem accūsātōrem hodiē dēfendō.
translation: Today in the forum I am defending a poor man on trial against a powerful prosecutor.

sentence: Amīcī absentis fāmam inter convīvās rīdentēs semper ācriter dēfendō.
translation: I always stand up fiercely for an absent friend's name among laughing dinner guests.

sentence: Cum legiōne nostrā mūrōs oppidī hostīlis prīmā lūce oppugnō.
translation: With our legion I attack the walls of the enemy town at first light.

sentence: In tabulā latrunculōrum aciem patris meī audācter oppugnō.
translation: On the game board I boldly go after my father's line of pieces.

sentence: Nōn hominem sed sententiam eius in cūriā verbīs oppugnō.
translation: In the senate house I attack not the man himself but his proposal.

sentence: Vesperī cum avō tesserīs lūdō et saepe eum vincō.
translation: In the evening I play dice with my grandfather, and I often beat him.

sentence: Certāmine versuum in lūdō magistrī omnēs condiscipulōs vincō.
translation: In the verse contest at the schoolmaster's I beat every one of my classmates.

sentence: Metum meum, quotiēns nāvem cōnscendō, vix precibus vincō.
translation: Every time I board a ship I barely master my fear, and only by praying.

sentence: Mūlō vectus altum montis iugum ante noctem superō.
translation: Riding a mule, I get over the high mountain ridge before nightfall.

sentence: In pistrīnō nostrō omnēs vīcīnōs pānis dulcēdine facile superō.
translation: In our bakery I easily outdo all the neighbours for the sweetness of my bread.

sentence: Cōnsiliō amīcōrum frētus omnēs domūs meae difficultātēs superō.
translation: Relying on my friends' advice, I get through every trouble my household has.

sentence: Olīvās et mel in cellā frīgidā per tōtam hiemem servō.
translation: I keep olives and honey in the cold cellar right through the winter.

sentence: Custōs nocturnus iānuam dominī meī tōtā nocte fidēliter servō.
translation: As the night watchman I guard my master's door faithfully all night long.

sentence: Fidem semel datam servō, etiam sī mihi damnō est.
translation: I keep a promise once given, even when it costs me dearly.

sentence: Clāvēs meās cotīdiē perdō et tōtam domum sollicitus scrūtor.
translation: I lose my keys every single day and then anxiously ransack the whole house.

sentence: Tōtum diem in tabernā tōnsōris inter rūmōrēs vānōs perdō.
translation: I waste a whole day in the barber's shop amid empty gossip.

sentence: Aleā lūdēns patrimōnium ā patre relictum paulātim perdō.
translation: Gambling at dice, I am slowly squandering the estate my father left me.

sentence: Ānulum aviae meae post trēs diēs sub lectō tandem inveniō.
translation: After three days I finally find my grandmother's ring under the bed.

sentence: In tabulāriō veterēs epistulās inter chartās neglēctās forte inveniō.
translation: In the archive I come across old letters by chance among neglected papers.

sentence: Diū cōgitō, sed nūllum verbum quod tē cōnsōlētur inveniō.
translation: I think for a long time, but I can find no word to comfort you.

sentence: Per tōtum vīcum canem meum fugitīvum clāmāns anxius quaerō.
translation: I go through the whole neighbourhood shouting anxiously for my runaway dog.

sentence: Ex agrō parvō victum mihi et līberīs cotīdiē quaerō.
translation: Out of one small field I scrape a daily living for myself and my children.

sentence: Ex nautīs in portū quaerō num nāvis Alexandrīna vēnerit.
translation: I ask the sailors down at the harbour whether the ship from Alexandria has come in.

sentence: Prīmā lūce, gallō canente, pānem in furnō coquere incipiō.
translation: At first light, while the cock is crowing, I start baking bread in the oven.

sentence: Ubi omnēs discipulī cōnsēdērunt, fābulam dē Trōiā nārrāre incipiō.
translation: Once all the students have sat down, I begin telling the story of Troy.

sentence: Post tot annōs tandem intellegere incipiō quantum mē amāverit.
translation: After so many years I am finally beginning to understand how much she loved me.

sentence: Ante Kalendās ratiōnēs dominī meī omnēs dīligenter cōnficiō.
translation: Before the first of the month I carefully settle all my master's accounts.

sentence: Vīgintī mīlia passuum per nivem ante merīdiem cōnficiō.
translation: I cover twenty miles through the snow before midday.

sentence: Lacrimāns epistulam ad frātrem in Britanniā mīlitantem cōnficiō.
translation: In tears I finish the letter to my brother serving in the army in Britain.

sentence: Post longum iter pēs dexter mihi tam dolēbat ut vix ambulārem.
translation: After the long march my right foot ached so badly that I could hardly walk.

sentence: Servus hospitis pedēs in triclīniō lāvit, antequam cēna appōnerētur.
translation: The slave washed the guest's feet in the dining room before dinner was served.

sentence: Captīva ante pedēs imperātōris prōcubuit et vītam fīliōrum implōrāvit.
translation: The captive woman threw herself at the general's feet and begged for her sons' lives.

sentence: Puer dē arbore lāpsus bracchium frēgit, et māter medicum statim arcessīvit.
translation: The boy fell out of the tree and broke his arm, and his mother sent for a doctor at once.

sentence: Rēmex fessus bracchia vix movēbat, cum tempestās nāvem in scopulōs impelleret.
translation: The exhausted oarsman could barely move his arms as the storm drove the ship onto the rocks.

sentence: Avia nepōtem ex Hispāniā reducem bracchiīs complexa diū dīmittere nōluit.
translation: The grandmother wrapped her arms around her grandson, home from Spain, and would not let him go.

sentence: Coquus, dum holera in culīnā secat, digitum cultrō graviter vulnerāvit.
translation: The cook was chopping vegetables in the kitchen and cut his finger badly with the knife.

sentence: Senātor, quotiēns per forum ambulat, digitīs praetereuntium mōnstrātur.
translation: Whenever the senator walks across the forum, passers-by point him out with their fingers.

sentence: Spōnsus ānulum in digitō puellae posuit, omnibus propinquīs plaudentibus.
translation: The bridegroom slipped the ring onto the girl's finger while all the relatives applauded.

sentence: Cum puer genū in saxō laesisset, sanguis per crūs eius fluēbat.
translation: When the boy hurt his knee on a rock, blood ran down his leg.

sentence: Gladiātor victus multum sanguinem in harēnam effūdit, populō tamen plaudente.
translation: The beaten gladiator spilled a great deal of blood onto the sand, and still the crowd applauded.

sentence: Uxor, cum tunicam marītī sanguine tīnctam vīdisset, exanimāta humī cecidit.
translation: When the wife saw her husband's tunic soaked in blood, she fainted and fell to the ground.

sentence: Ancilla os bovis in ollam coniēcit, ut iūs pinguius fieret.
translation: The maid dropped an ox bone into the pot so that the broth would be richer.

sentence: Ossa senis frācta male coaluērunt, itaque medicus eum ambulāre vetuit.
translation: The old man's broken bones knitted badly, so the doctor forbade him to walk.

sentence: Māter ossa fīliī ē rogō collēcta in urnam marmoream flēns condidit.
translation: Weeping, the mother gathered her son's bones from the pyre and laid them in a marble urn.

sentence: Nūtrīx fābulam nārrāns vōcem submittēbat, nē īnfantem dormientem excitāret.
translation: As she told the story the nurse kept lowering her voice so as not to wake the sleeping baby.

sentence: Ōrātor in rōstrīs vōce clārā locūtus est, ut tōtum forum audīret.
translation: The orator spoke from the rostra in a clear voice, so that the whole forum could hear him.

sentence: Vōx mea in mediā ōrātiōne dēfēcit, cum nōmen patris mortuī recitārem.
translation: My voice failed in the middle of the speech, as I was reading out my dead father's name.

sentence: Animal aegrum, quod puer in viā invēnit, iam in hortō nostrō placidē dormit.
translation: The sick animal the boy found in the street is now sleeping peacefully in our garden.

sentence: Mercātor animālia ante prīmam lūcem in forum Boārium ēgit.
translation: The dealer drove his animals to the cattle market before first light.

sentence: Philosophus in scholā disputābat hominem sōlum esse animal quod ratiōne ūtātur.
translation: In the lecture hall the philosopher argued that man is the only animal that uses reason.

sentence: Canis noster sub mēnsā sedet et frūsta cēnae patienter exspectat.
translation: Our dog sits under the table and waits patiently for scraps from dinner.

sentence: Ā cane vīlicī territus, fūr per mūrum hortī nocte effūgit.
translation: Frightened by the farm foreman's dog, the thief escaped over the garden wall in the night.

sentence: Pāstor canem fidēlem, quī lupum fugāverat, plūris quam ovēs aestimābat.
translation: The shepherd valued his faithful dog, which had driven off a wolf, more highly than his sheep.

sentence: Equus meus in stabulō claudicat, itaque hodiē in urbem pedibus ībō.
translation: My horse is lame in the stable, so today I shall go into the city on foot.

sentence: Aurīga equōs per Circum Maximum incitāvit, dum turba nōmen eius clāmat.
translation: The charioteer drove his horses hard down the Circus Maximus while the crowd shouted his name.

sentence: Dē equō lāpsus, iuvenis rīsum spectantium diū ferre nōn potuit.
translation: Thrown from his horse, the young man could not bear the onlookers' laughter for long.

sentence: Bōs, quem pater meus ēmerat, prīmā lūce agrum arāre coepit.
translation: The ox my father had bought started ploughing the field at first light.

sentence: Sacerdōs bovem albam Iūnōnī ante templum immolāvit, tōtō populō spectante.
translation: The priest sacrificed a white cow to Juno in front of the temple while the whole people looked on.

sentence: Bovī fessō agricola aquam dedit, priusquam ipse cēnāre coepit.
translation: The farmer gave his tired ox water before he sat down to his own dinner.

sentence: Prīmā lūce per hortum ambulō, dum avia rosās rigat.
translation: At first light I walk through the garden while my grandmother waters the roses.

sentence: Ad forum cotīdiē ambulō, quia viae tam angustae sunt ut raedae haereant.
translation: I walk to the forum every day, because the streets are so narrow that the carriages get stuck.

sentence: Post cēnam per porticum sōlus ambulō, quod inter columnās melius cōgitō.
translation: After dinner I walk alone along the colonnade, because I think better among the columns.

sentence: Dum tegulās in tēctō reficiō, dē scālīs in hortum cadō.
translation: While I am mending the tiles on the roof, I fall off the ladder into the garden.

sentence: In proeliō equus meus titubat et ego statim in lutum cadō.
translation: In the battle my horse stumbles and I go straight down into the mud.

sentence: Cum tōtum diem labōrāvī, vesperī in lectum quasi mortuus cadō.
translation: When I have worked the whole day, in the evening I fall into bed like a dead man.

sentence: Ante lūcem surgō, quia gallus vīcīnī sub fenestrā meā cantat.
translation: I get up before dawn, because the neighbour's rooster crows under my window.

sentence: In cūriā surgō ut sententiam meam dīcam, sed nēmō tacet.
translation: I rise in the senate house to give my opinion, but nobody will keep quiet.

sentence: Hieme aegrē ē lectō surgō, cum frīgus per rīmās fenestrae intrat.
translation: In winter I drag myself out of bed, when the cold comes in through the cracks in the window.

sentence: Aestāte sub arbore in hortō dormiō, dum apēs circum flōrēs volitant.
translation: In summer I sleep under a tree in the garden while the bees flit around the flowers.

sentence: In caupōnā vix dormiō, quod plaustra tōtā nocte per viam strepunt.
translation: I barely sleep at the inn, because wagons rumble down the street all night.

sentence: Cum dē pecūniā sollicitus sum, tōtam noctem nōn dormiō sed cōgitō.
translation: When I am worried about money, I do not sleep all night but lie there thinking.

sentence: Māne pānem cum melle edō, quia avus noster apēs in vīllā alit.
translation: In the morning I eat bread with honey, because our grandfather keeps bees at the farm.

sentence: In popīnā stāns olīvās et ōva dūra edō, quia ad forum properāre dēbeō.
translation: I eat olives and hard-boiled eggs standing in the cookshop, because I have to hurry to the forum.

sentence: Cēnās dīvitum nōn amō; apud mātrem pultem simplicem libentius edō.
translation: I have no taste for rich men's dinners; I would rather eat plain porridge at my mother's.

sentence: Post merīdiem aquam frīgidam ē puteō bibō, dum bovēs in umbrā quiēscunt.
translation: In the afternoon I drink cold water from the well while the oxen rest in the shade.

sentence: In tabernā prope forum vīnum aquā mixtum cum sociīs bibō.
translation: At a tavern near the forum I drink wine cut with water with my business partners.

sentence: Merum sine aquā nōn bibō, quia postrīdiē semper caput mihi dolet.
translation: I never drink wine neat, because the next day my head always aches.

sentence: In macellō ōva et holera cotīdiē emō, sed piscēs nimis cārī sunt.
translation: I buy eggs and vegetables at the food market every day, but the fish are far too expensive.

sentence: In portū Ostiae frūmentum magnō pretiō emō, quia nāvēs sērō vēnērunt.
translation: At the harbour of Ostia I buy grain at a steep price, because the ships came in late.

sentence: Libellōs poētārum novōrum semper emō, quamquam uxor mea dīcit mē nimium pecūniae cōnsūmere.
translation: I always buy the new poets' little books, though my wife says I spend too much money.

sentence: Ōva et cāseum vīcīnīs vēndō, quia gallīnae nostrae plūs pariunt quam familia cōnsūmit.
translation: I sell eggs and cheese to the neighbours, because our hens lay more than the household gets through.

sentence: In forō bovēs meōs vēndō, sed emptōrēs pretium nimis parvum offerunt.
translation: I am selling my oxen in the forum, but the buyers are offering far too low a price.

sentence: Invītus vīllam avītam vēndō, quod aes aliēnum mē cotīdiē magis premit.
translation: I am selling my grandfather's farm against my will, because the debt presses harder on me every day.

sentence: Tōtum diem in agrō labōrō, deinde vesperī pedēs in aquā lavō.
translation: I work in the field the whole day, then in the evening I wash my feet in water.

sentence: In officīnā patris labōrō, ubi ferrum ā prīmā lūce tundimus.
translation: I work in my father's workshop, where we hammer iron from first light.

sentence: Multās hōrās frūstrā labōrō, nam dominus mercēdem iūstam numquam mihi solvit.
translation: I work long hours for nothing, since the master never pays me a fair wage.

sentence: Cum frātre minōre nucibus lūdō, dum imber in impluvium cadit.
translation: I play at nuts with my little brother while the rain falls into the impluvium.
