sentence: Cotīdiē ante balneum pilā cum amīcīs in campō Mārtiō lūdō.
translation: Every day before my bath I play ball with friends on the Campus Martius.

sentence: Āleā numquam lūdō, quia frāter meus omnem pecūniam ūnā nocte perdidit.
translation: I never play dice, because my brother lost all his money in a single night.

sentence: Diū in culīnā labōrāvimus; dēnique cēna in mēnsā fūmābat.
translation: We worked in the kitchen for ages; at last dinner sat steaming on the table.

sentence: Senātōrēs trēs hōrās disputāvērunt, dēnique lēgem novam probāvērunt.
translation: The senators argued for three hours, and in the end they passed the new law.

sentence: Prīmum agrōs, tum domum, dēnique etiam ānulum mātris vēndidit.
translation: First he sold the fields, then the house, and finally even his mother's ring.

sentence: Tōtam noctem vigilāvimus; tandem sub aurōram īnfāns dormīre coepit.
translation: We were awake the whole night; at last, toward dawn, the baby began to sleep.

sentence: Post trēs mēnsēs mercātor tandem pecūniam quam mihi dēbēbat reddidit.
translation: After three months the merchant finally paid back the money he owed me.

sentence: Quam diū nōs tandem in hōc frīgore stāre iubēbis?
translation: How much longer are you going to keep us standing out here in the cold?

sentence: Prīmum ignem in focō accendō, deinde aquam in ollā calefaciō.
translation: First I light the fire on the hearth, then I heat water in the pot.

sentence: Medicus vulnus prīmum lāvit, deinde fasciā artē alligāvit.
translation: The doctor washed the wound first, then bound it up tightly with a bandage.

sentence: Verba eius prīmō mē mōvērunt, deinde tamen fraudem intellēxī.
translation: His words moved me at first; then, though, I saw the trick behind them.

sentence: Puerī prīmum in flūmine natant, dein sōle calidō corpora siccant.
translation: The boys swim in the river first, then dry themselves off in the hot sun.

sentence: Cōnsul paucīs verbīs locūtus est, dein castra statim movēre iussit.
translation: The consul spoke a few words, then ordered the camp struck at once.

sentence: Diū tacuit, dein lacrimāns tōtam rem mātrī suae cōnfessa est.
translation: She said nothing for a long while, then confessed the whole thing to her mother in tears.

sentence: Tōtum diem in hortō labōrāvī; posteā vix ambulāre poteram.
translation: I worked in the garden the whole day; afterward I could hardly walk.

sentence: Hospes prīmō mē cōmiter accēpit, posteā pretium nimium postulāvit.
translation: The innkeeper welcomed me courteously at first, and afterward demanded an outrageous price.

sentence: Illud verbum īrātus dīxī, sed posteā mē eius paenituit.
translation: I said that word in anger, but afterward I was sorry for it.

sentence: Haec via mihi nōta est; anteā hīc cum avō saepe ambulābam.
translation: I know this road well; I used to walk here with my grandfather.

sentence: Nunc rhētoricam docet, sed anteā in Galliā multōs annōs mīlitāvit.
translation: He teaches rhetoric now, but before that he soldiered in Gaul for many years.

sentence: Numquam anteā tantum silentium in hāc domō sēnsī, et timeō.
translation: I have never felt such silence in this house before, and it frightens me.

sentence: Nūbēs ātrae ab occidente surgunt; mox imber ūvās nostrās corrumpet.
translation: Black clouds are rising in the west; the rain will ruin our grapes soon.

sentence: Nāvis in portū stat; mox nautae mercēs in lītus expōnent.
translation: The ship is lying in the harbour; soon the sailors will unload the cargo onto the shore.

sentence: Nōlī flēre, fīlia: pater tuus mox ex bellō incolumis redībit.
translation: Don't cry, daughter: your father will come home safe from the war soon.

sentence: Hīc ōlim silva erat, ubi nunc tabernae et viae strepunt.
translation: There was a wood here once, where shops and streets now clatter away.

sentence: Avus meus ōlim in hāc officīnā gladiōs legiōnibus faciēbat.
translation: My grandfather used to make swords for the legions in this workshop.

sentence: Haec quoque ōlim, cum senēs erimus, meminisse nōs iuvābit.
translation: One day, when we are old, we will be glad to remember even this.

sentence: Vīcīna nostra nūper puerum peperit; tōta domus per noctem vigilat.
translation: Our neighbour had a baby boy recently; the whole house is awake all night.

sentence: Faber quī nūper tēctum refēcit hodiē mercēdem suam poscit.
translation: The workman who repaired the roof the other day is here today asking for his pay.

sentence: Nūper amīcum veterem in viā vīdī, sed mē nōn agnōvit.
translation: I saw an old friend in the street recently, but he did not recognize me.

sentence: Media nox est, sed pater adhūc in tablīnō ad lūcernam scrībit.
translation: It is the middle of the night, but father is still writing by the lamp in his study.

sentence: Trēs epistulās mīsī, sed nūllum adhūc respōnsum ab illīs accēpī.
translation: I have sent three letters, but so far I have had no reply from them.

sentence: Multōs annōs abest, et adhūc eum cotīdiē ad iānuam exspectō.
translation: He has been away for many years, and I still wait for him at the door every day.

sentence: Vīlla nostra prope flūmen sita est, itaque hieme semper ūmida est.
translation: Our farmhouse stands near the river, so it is always damp in winter.

sentence: Cum prope forum ambulārēmus, subitō clāmōrem mercātōrum audīvimus.
translation: As we were walking near the forum, we suddenly heard the traders shouting.

sentence: Cum lupum vīdissem, tantus terror mē cēpit ut prope ex equō dēciderim.
translation: When I caught sight of the wolf, such terror seized me that I nearly fell off my horse.

sentence: Tōtam noctem ūnā vigilāvimus, dum māter aegra tandem obdormīvit.
translation: We sat up together all night, until our sick mother finally fell asleep.

sentence: Mīlitēs ūnā cum ducē per nivem trēs diēs iter fēcērunt.
translation: The soldiers marched for three days through the snow together with their commander.

sentence: Post vīndēmiam ūnā cēnāre solēbāmus, et illōs diēs nunc dēsīderō.
translation: After the grape harvest we used to eat together, and I miss those days now.

sentence: Tōtam domum frūstrā perscrūtātus sum; ānulus mātris nusquam apparet.
translation: I searched the whole house for nothing; my mother's ring is nowhere to be seen.

sentence: Frūstrā ōrātor per tōtam hōram causam dīxit; iūdicēs iam dēcrēverant.
translation: The advocate pleaded for a whole hour in vain; the jurors had already made up their minds.

sentence: Frūstrā tē ad cēnam invītāvī, quia numquam epistulās meās legis.
translation: I invited you to dinner for nothing, since you never read my letters.

sentence: Puer lucernam ēvertit et paene tōtum tablīnum patris incendit.
translation: The boy knocked over the lamp and almost burned down his father's whole study.

sentence: Nāvis mercātōris paene ad Ostiam pervēnerat, cum tempestās vēla scidit.
translation: The merchant's ship had almost reached Ostia when a storm tore the sails apart.

sentence: Epistulam tuam legēns paene lacrimāvī, tantum mē dēsīderium tenuit.
translation: Reading your letter I almost wept, such longing took hold of me.

sentence: Post morbum avia vix per hortum sine baculō ambulāre potest.
translation: Since her illness Grandmother can hardly walk across the garden without a stick.

sentence: Tanta erat turba in Subūrā ut vix pedem prōferre possēmus.
translation: The crowd in the Subura was so thick that we could scarcely put one foot forward.

sentence: Vix crēdere possum tē tantam pecūniam hesternā nocte āleā perdidisse.
translation: I can hardly believe you threw away that much money at dice last night.

sentence: Nēmō domī erat cum vēnī; etiam iānitor ad forum abierat.
translation: Nobody was at home when I arrived; even the doorkeeper had gone off to the forum.

sentence: In hāc officīnā nēmō scit quō modo rota frācta reficiātur.
translation: In this workshop nobody knows how a broken wheel is to be mended.

sentence: Post tot annōs nēmō iam meminit quam fortiter avus pugnāverit.
translation: After so many years nobody remembers any longer how bravely grandfather fought.

sentence: In arcā nihil relictum erat praeter pānem dūrum et paucās olīvās.
translation: Nothing was left in the chest except stale bread and a few olives.

sentence: Servus tacēbat; dominō īrātō nihil respondēre audēbat, nē verberārētur.
translation: The slave kept quiet; he dared say nothing to his angry master, for fear of a beating.

sentence: Nihil mihi dulcius est quam post longum iter domum redīre.
translation: Nothing is sweeter to me than coming home after a long journey.

sentence: Māter rogāvit num umquam tam sordidam tunicam anteā lāvisset.
translation: Mother asked whether she had ever washed such a filthy tunic before.

sentence: Sī umquam Rōmam vēneris, in tabernā meā prope Circum manēbis.
translation: If you ever come to Rome, you will stay at my inn near the Circus.

sentence: Nesciō an umquam ōrātōrem tam vehementem in cūriā audīverim.
translation: I doubt whether I have ever heard so fierce a speaker in the senate house.

sentence: Nocte undique canēs lātrāvērunt, itaque tōta familia usque ad lūcem vigilāvit.
translation: Dogs barked on every side all night, so the whole household lay awake until dawn.

sentence: Hostēs undique castra nostra petīvērunt, sed vallum ante lūcem nōn cessit.
translation: The enemy attacked our camp from all sides, but the rampart held until daybreak.

sentence: Undique tot cūrae mē premunt ut nocte quiētē dormīre nequeam.
translation: So many worries press on me from every side that I cannot sleep peacefully at night.

sentence: Frāter meus plūs vīnī bibit quam decet, et māter tacita īrāscitur.
translation: My brother drinks more wine than he should, and mother seethes in silence.

sentence: Hōc mēnse plūs frūmentī vēndidimus quam tōtō annō superiōre.
translation: This month we sold more grain than in the whole of last year.

sentence: Magistrum plūs timeō quam amō, quamquam multa ab eō didicī.
translation: I fear my teacher more than I love him, though I have learned a great deal from him.

sentence: Ubi māter clāmāvit, puerī statim ē culīnā fūgērunt et in hortō latuērunt.
translation: When their mother shouted, the boys fled the kitchen at once and hid in the garden.

sentence: Cum nūntius ā cōnsule vēnisset, mīlitēs statim arma cēpērunt et castra relīquērunt.
translation: When the messenger had arrived from the consul, the soldiers immediately took up arms and left the camp.

sentence: Sī statim mihi respondissēs, tantum dolōrem numquam sēnsissem.
translation: If you had written back to me straight away, I would never have felt such pain.

sentence: Dum cēnam parāmus, lucerna subitō exstīncta est et in tenebrīs sedēbāmus.
translation: While we were getting dinner ready, the lamp suddenly went out and we sat there in the dark.

sentence: In forō dē pretiīs disputābāmus, cum subitō imber magnus omnēs in porticum ēgit.
translation: We were arguing about prices in the forum when a heavy downpour suddenly drove everyone under the colonnade.

sentence: Vōcem patris in turbā subitō audīvī et lacrimās tenēre nōn potuī.
translation: I suddenly heard my father's voice in the crowd, and I could not hold back my tears.

sentence: Dum in hortō fodiō, forte nummum antīquum sub rādīcibus arboris inveniō.
translation: While digging in the garden I happen to find an old coin down among the roots of a tree.

sentence: Cum forte in balneīs cōnsulem convēnissem, dē agrīs meīs diū loquēbāmur.
translation: Since I happened to run into the consul at the baths, we talked about my land for a long while.

sentence: Sī forte hanc epistulam lēgeris, nōlī mihi propter longum silentium īrāscī.
translation: If you should happen to read this letter, please don't be angry with me over the long silence.

sentence: Pater nōndum rediit; fortasse in viā carrum frāctum invēnit et morātur.
translation: Father still isn't back; perhaps he came across a broken wagon on the road and is held up.

sentence: Fortasse crās dominus nōs dīmittet, sī opus ante noctem cōnfēcerimus.
translation: Perhaps the master will let us go tomorrow, if we get the work finished before nightfall.

sentence: Fortasse stultus sum, sed adhūc crēdō amīcum meum ad mē reditūrum esse.
translation: Maybe I am a fool, but I still believe my friend will come back to me.

sentence: Iānuam clausisse nōn meminī, sed lucernam certē ante somnum exstīnxī.
translation: I don't remember locking the door, but I definitely put the lamp out before going to sleep.

sentence: Pecūniam tibi reddere nunc nōn possum; ante Kalendās certē reddam.
translation: I can't pay you back right now, but I will certainly pay before the first of the month.

sentence: Nesciō quid dē mē dīcant, sed hoc certē sciō: nēmō mē magis amāvit.
translation: I don't know what people say about me, but I know this much for sure: nobody has loved me more.

sentence: Frāter meus in urbe habitat; ego vērō in vīllā avītā manēre mālō.
translation: My brother lives in the city; I, on the other hand, would rather stay at the family farmhouse.

sentence: Tum vērō omnēs cīvēs clāmāre coepērunt et forum tōtum complēvērunt.
translation: Then indeed all the citizens began to shout, and they filled the whole forum.

sentence: Illud vērō mē maximē angit, quod nēmō ex amīcīs ad fūnus vēnit.
translation: But what really eats at me is that not one of my friends came to the funeral.

sentence: Ego quidem hanc viam nōvī, sed nocte sine lūnā nihil vidēre possum.
translation: I for one know this road, but at night without a moon I can't see a thing.

sentence: Dominus tam īrātus erat ut nē salūtem quidem nōbīs redderet.
translation: The master was so angry that he did not even return our greeting.

sentence: Vincere quidem nōn potuimus, sed hostēs ā portīs urbis nostrae reppulimus.
translation: We couldn't win, admittedly, but we did push the enemy back from the gates of our city.

sentence: Ūnum tantum cēnae nostrae dēest, scīlicet vīnum, quod ex urbe crās afferam.
translation: Only one thing is missing from our dinner, namely the wine, which I'll bring from town tomorrow.

sentence: Tacuī scīlicet quod timēbam nē dominus mē ex agrīs expelleret.
translation: I kept quiet, of course, because I was afraid the master would throw me off the land.

sentence: Pecūniam nūllam habēre dīcit; scīlicet ideō vīllam novam in monte aedificat.
translation: He claims he has no money — which is obviously why he is building a new villa up on the hill.

sentence: Hieme domī manēre mālumus, praesertim cum nix viās omnēs operuerit.
translation: In winter we would rather stay at home, especially once the snow has buried every road.

sentence: Longum iter per montēs perīculōsum est, praesertim mercātōribus quī sine custōdibus proficīscuntur.
translation: A long journey through the mountains is dangerous, especially for merchants who set out without guards.

sentence: Nēmō tibi ignōscet, praesertim cum patrem tuum in perīculō relīquerīs.
translation: Nobody is going to forgive you, especially since you left your own father in danger.

sentence: Aviam meam rārō videō, quod procul ā marī in montibus habitat.
translation: I rarely see my grandmother, because she lives far from the sea up in the mountains.

sentence: Nautae procul in marī vēla nāvis onerāriae cōnspexērunt et clāmāre coepērunt.
translation: The sailors spotted the sails of a cargo ship far out at sea and started shouting.

sentence: Procul ā patriā mīlitāns, noctū semper dē agrīs paternīs cōgitābam.
translation: Soldiering far from home, I thought every night about my father's fields.

sentence: Ancilla nostra nimis multum aquae in vīnum īnfūdit; hospitēs tacitī rīsērunt.
translation: Our maid poured far too much water into the wine, and the guests laughed under their breath.

sentence: Dominus meus nimis sevērē cum servīs agit, itaque nēmō diū manet.
translation: My master treats the slaves too harshly, so nobody stays in the household for long.

sentence: Nimis diū in forō morātus es; cēna tua iam tōta frīget.
translation: You hung about the forum far too long; your dinner has gone stone cold by now.

sentence: Frūmentī parum in horreō relīquimus, et hiems nōndum cōnfecta est.
translation: We have left too little grain in the granary, and winter is not over yet.

sentence: Puer noster parum dīligenter scrībit, itaque magister tabellās eius cotīdiē dēlet.
translation: Our boy writes with too little care, so the teacher wipes his tablets clean every day.

sentence: Parum tibi crēdidī, et nunc mē huius suspīciōnis vehementer paenitet.
translation: I trusted you too little, and now I bitterly regret having suspected you.

sentence: Ferē tōtam noctem vigilāvimus, quod īnfāns sine causā clāmābat.
translation: We lay awake almost the whole night, because the baby was screaming for no reason at all.

sentence: Mercātōrēs in forō ferē cotīdiē dē pretiīs frūmentī acerbē contendunt.
translation: The traders in the forum quarrel bitterly about the price of grain nearly every day.

sentence: Ferē omnēs amīcī mē dēseruērunt, ūnus tamen Mārcus fidem servāvit.
translation: Almost all my friends abandoned me; Marcus alone stayed loyal.

sentence: Propter imbrem subitum sub porticū diū stetimus nec domum redīre potuimus.
translation: Because of a sudden downpour we stood a long time under the colonnade and could not get home.

sentence: Propter bellum in Galliā mercātūra nostra per tōtam aestātem cessāvit.
translation: Because of the war in Gaul our business came to a standstill for the whole summer.

sentence: Frāter meus propter invidiam, nōn propter iūstitiam, mē apud iūdicem accūsāvit.
translation: My brother brought me before the judge out of envy, not out of any love of justice.

sentence: Herī apud avunculum meum cēnāvimus et fābulās dē bellō Pūnicō audīvimus.
translation: Yesterday we had dinner at my uncle's house and listened to stories about the Punic War.

sentence: Apud iūdicēs causam amīcī crās agam, sī vōx mihi suffēcerit.
translation: Tomorrow I shall plead my friend's case before the judges, if my voice holds out.

sentence: Apud Germānōs haec cōnsuētūdō turpis habētur, apud nōs autem laudātur.
translation: Among the Germans this custom is thought shameful, whereas among us it is praised.

sentence: Trāns flūmen nāvicula cotīdiē nōs ad hortōs avī vehit.
translation: A little boat ferries us across the river to grandfather's gardens every day.

sentence: Caesar legiōnēs trāns Rhēnum dūxit ut Germānōs terrōre premeret.
translation: Caesar led his legions across the Rhine in order to cow the Germans with terror.

sentence: Fīlia mea trāns mare habitat, et litterās eius per tōtum annum exspectō.
translation: My daughter lives across the sea, and I wait a whole year for a letter from her.

sentence: Circā mēnsam tōta familia sedēbat, dum avia dē pueritiā suā nārrat.
translation: The whole household sat around the table while grandmother told them about her childhood.

sentence: Circā merīdiem mercātor advēnit, cum omnēs iam in tabernā dormīrent.
translation: The merchant turned up around midday, when everyone in the shop was already asleep.

sentence: Circā mūrōs urbis hostēs tōtam noctem ignēs accendēbant; nēmō dormīvit.
translation: All night the enemy kept lighting fires around the city walls; nobody slept a wink.

sentence: Secundum rīpam Tiberis ambulābāmus, dum piscātōrēs rētia sua siccant.
translation: We were walking along the bank of the Tiber while the fishermen dried out their nets.

sentence: Iūdex secundum lēgem antīquam dēcrēvit, quamquam omnēs aliud spērāverant.
translation: The judge ruled according to the ancient law, although everyone had hoped for something else.

sentence: Secundum nātūram vīvere difficile est, ut Stōicī nōbīs cotīdiē persuādēre cōnantur.
translation: Living according to nature is hard work, whatever the Stoics try to talk us into every day.

sentence: Māter mea ergā vīcīnōs semper benigna fuit, etiam cum ipsa egēret.
translation: My mother was always kind towards the neighbours, even when she was in want herself.

sentence: Fidem ergā patrōnum servāvī, quamquam mihi nihil umquam praemiī dedit.
translation: I kept faith with my patron, even though he never gave me any reward at all.

sentence: Odium tuum ergā frātrem tantum crēvit ut nōmen eius audīre nōn possīs.
translation: Your hatred towards your brother has grown so great that you cannot bear to hear his name.

sentence: Extrā portam Capēnam avus meus parvam vīllam cum vīneā possidēbat.
translation: Just outside the Porta Capena my grandfather owned a small farmhouse with a vineyard.

sentence: Mīlitēs extrā mūrōs castra posuērunt, quod urbs tot hominēs capere nōn poterat.
translation: The soldiers pitched camp outside the walls, because the town could not hold so many men.

sentence: Nunc dēnique extrā perīculum sum, sed noctēs adhūc sine somnō agō.
translation: At last I am out of danger, and yet I still spend my nights without sleep.

sentence: Coquus hodiē cēnam sērō parat, quia ignis in culīnā exstīnctus est.
translation: The cook is getting dinner ready late today, because the kitchen fire has gone out.

sentence: Mercātor in forō magnā vōce clāmat, quia nēmō hodiē piscēs emit.
translation: The trader is shouting at the top of his voice in the forum, because nobody is buying fish today.

sentence: Puerum nōn reprehendō, quia magistrum timuit et vērum cēlāre māluit.
translation: I don't blame the boy, because he was frightened of the teacher and chose to hide the truth.

sentence: Quoniam tōtum diem pluit, in tabernā mānsimus et vīnum calidum bibimus.
translation: Since it rained the whole day, we stayed in the tavern and drank hot wine.

sentence: Quoniam nāvis nōndum advēnit, mercātōrēs in portū ōtiōsī sedent et queruntur.
translation: Since the ship still hasn't come in, the merchants sit around idle at the harbour and grumble.

sentence: Quoniam iam senex sum, agrum fīliō trādō et tandem quiēscō.
translation: Since I'm an old man now, I'm handing the farm over to my son and finally taking my rest.

sentence: Sub arbore in agrō sedēbāmus, dōnec sōl post montēs occidit.
translation: We sat under the tree out in the field until the sun went down behind the mountains.

sentence: In viā exspectā, dōnec pater tabernam claudat et clāvēs inveniat.
translation: Wait out in the street until father shuts the shop and finds his keys.

sentence: Dōnec māter vīvēbat, nēmō in hāc domō famem umquam sēnsit.
translation: As long as mother was alive, nobody in this house ever went hungry.

sentence: Postquam hospitēs discessērunt, tōtam noctem pōcula et mēnsās lāvimus.
translation: After the guests had left, we spent the whole night washing cups and tables.

sentence: Postquam imber tēctum frēgit, fabrum ē proximō vīcō statim arcessīvimus.
translation: After the downpour broke the roof, we sent for a builder from the nearest village straight away.

sentence: Postquam epistulam fīliī lēgī, prīmum flēvī, deinde tōtam domum cantū implēvī.
translation: After I read my son's letter I cried at first, and then filled the whole house with singing.

sentence: Antequam ad forum exeō, gallīnās pāscō et ignem in culīnā accendō.
translation: Before I head out to the forum, I feed the hens and light the fire in the kitchen.

sentence: Mīlitēs pontem trānsiērunt, antequam hostēs in rīpā aciem īnstrūxērunt.
translation: The soldiers got across the bridge before the enemy drew up their line on the bank.

sentence: Puer domō fugere cōnstituit, antequam pater dē vāse frāctō audīret.
translation: The boy decided to run away from home before his father could hear about the broken jar.

sentence: Priusquam sōl oritur, pistor iam pānem calidum in furnō habet.
translation: Before the sun comes up, the baker already has warm bread in his oven.

sentence: Nauta fūnem celeriter solvit, priusquam magister nāvis signum dare posset.
translation: The sailor cast the rope off in a hurry, before the ship's captain could give the signal.

sentence: Multa dē amīcō meō dīxī, priusquam vēritātem tōtam cognōvī; nunc mē paenitet.
translation: I said a great deal about my friend before I learned the whole truth; now I'm sorry for it.

sentence: Quamquam tōtā nocte nix cecidit, māne ad thermās tamen ambulāvimus.
translation: Although snow fell all night long, we still walked to the baths in the morning.

sentence: Quamquam dominus mercēdem auxit, operāriī in vīneā adhūc murmurant.
translation: Although the owner has raised their wages, the workers in the vineyard are still muttering.

sentence: Quamquam multōs annōs Rōmae habitō, nocturnōs Subūrae clāmōrēs numquam amāvī.
translation: Although I have lived in Rome for many years, I have never come to love the night-time din of the Subura.

sentence: Licet tōtum diem pluat, avia in hortō rosās suās cūrat.
translation: Even though it rains all day, grandmother is out in the garden looking after her roses.

sentence: Licet dominus īrātus sit, hodiē ante merīdiem officīnam claudam.
translation: Even though the master is furious, I am shutting the workshop before noon today.

sentence: Licet omnēs mē dērīdeant, sententiam meam dē bellō nōn mūtābō.
translation: Even though everyone laughs at me, I will not change my view about the war.

sentence: Māter īnfantem tenet et simul pultem in ollā lentē miscet.
translation: Mother is holding the baby and at the same time slowly stirring the porridge in the pot.

sentence: Omnēs nautae simul rēmōs dūcunt, aliter nāvis in scopulōs impingitur.
translation: All the sailors pull their oars together, otherwise the ship is driven onto the rocks.

sentence: Fīliam nūbentem spectāns, simul gaudēbam et lacrimās tenēre nōn poteram.
translation: Watching my daughter on her wedding day, I was happy and at the same time could not hold back my tears.

sentence: Tēctum stillat; praetereā mūrēs tōtam farīnam in cellā cōnsūmpsērunt.
translation: The roof is leaking, and on top of that the mice have eaten all the flour in the storeroom.

sentence: Puer scrībere didicit; praetereā numerōs celerius quam magister ipse computat.
translation: The boy has learned to write, and what is more he reckons up figures faster than the teacher himself.

sentence: Iter longum est; praetereā nēmō nōbīs in montibus hospitium praebēbit.
translation: The journey is long, and besides, nobody up in the mountains will give us shelter.

sentence: Fīlium meum litterās Graecās in atriō cotīdiē māne doceō.
translation: Every morning I teach my son his Greek letters in the atrium.

sentence: In forō adulēscentēs causās agere prō amīcīs doceō.
translation: In the forum I teach young men to plead cases on behalf of their friends.

sentence: Servōs quoque litterās doceō, quamquam vīcīnī mē stultum vocant.
translation: I teach my slaves their letters as well, even though the neighbours call me a fool for it.

sentence: Ā mātre meā pānem coquere in culīnā lentē discō.
translation: I am slowly learning from my mother how to bake bread in the kitchen.

sentence: In castrīs prīmā lūce gladium tenēre et parēre discō.
translation: In camp at first light I am learning to hold a sword and to obey orders.

sentence: Sērō discō tacēre, sed lingua mea saepe mē prōdit.
translation: I am learning to keep quiet far too late — my tongue still gives me away.

sentence: Fīlium aegrum, quamquam recūsat, amārum medicāmentum bibere cōgō.
translation: My son is sick and refuses, but I make him drink the bitter medicine.

sentence: Ante tempestātem servōs et gregēs in vīllam properē cōgō.
translation: Before the storm breaks I hurriedly gather the farmhands and the flocks into the villa.

sentence: Nēminem ad cēnam venīre cōgō; invītī convīvae omnia corrumpunt.
translation: I force nobody to come to dinner; guests who came unwillingly spoil the whole evening.

sentence: Fīliae meae post cēnam cum amīcīs in hortō ambulāre permittō.
translation: After dinner I let my daughter walk in the garden with her friends.

sentence: Vīlicō fidēlī tōtam vīllam et ratiōnēs meās absēns permittō.
translation: While I am away I entrust the whole farm and my accounts to a trustworthy overseer.

sentence: Servō meō lūdōs Circēnsēs spectāre permittō, quoniam et ille homō est.
translation: I let my slave go and watch the races at the Circus, since he too is a human being.

sentence: Canem meum ā culīnā prohibeō, nam herī tōtum pānem abstulit.
translation: I keep my dog out of the kitchen, because yesterday he made off with the whole loaf.

sentence: Operāriōs meōs merīdiē in sōle labōrāre semper prohibeō.
translation: I never let my workmen labour out in the sun at midday.

sentence: Frūstrā tē prohibeō, nam cotīdiē ad illam mulierem clam redīs.
translation: I forbid you in vain: every day you slip back to that woman.

sentence: Ante lūcem gregem ex stabulō in montēs aestāte pellō.
translation: In summer I drive the flock out of the stable up into the hills before daybreak.

sentence: Fūrem clāmantem ex tabernā meā baculō in viam pellō.
translation: With a stick I drive the thief, shouting all the while, out of my shop into the street.

sentence: Cūrās nocturnās vīnō et cantū ā pectore meō pellō.
translation: With wine and singing I drive the night's worries out of my heart.

sentence: Cēnā cōnfectā, mappās et pōcula dē mēnsā tollō.
translation: Once dinner is over I clear the napkins and the cups off the table.

sentence: In portū amphorās gravēs dē nāve in umerōs meōs tollō.
translation: Down at the harbour I heave the heavy amphorae off the ship onto my shoulders.

sentence: Manūs ad caelum tollō et deōs prō salūte fīliī ōrō.
translation: I raise my hands to the sky and beg the gods for my son's safety.

sentence: Autumnō olīvās sub prēlō gravī cum servīs meīs premō.
translation: In autumn I press the olives under the heavy beam together with my slaves.

sentence: Digitum in vulnus mīlitis premō, nē plūs sanguinis effluat.
translation: I press my finger into the soldier's wound so that no more blood runs out.

sentence: Dolōrem meum silentiō premō, nē māter mea lacrimās videat.
translation: I hold my grief down in silence so that my mother will not see the tears.

sentence: Lucernam ārdentem imprūdēns tangō et digitum meum statim ūrō.
translation: Carelessly I touch the burning lamp and instantly scorch my finger.

sentence: Ante iūdicem āram tangō et mē vēra dictūrum esse iūrō.
translation: Before the judge I lay my hand on the altar and swear that I will tell the truth.

sentence: Cinerēs patris in urnā tangō et lacrimās tenēre nōn possum.
translation: I touch my father's ashes in the urn and cannot hold back my tears.

sentence: Sub palliō tenuī frīgus nocturnum per omnia membra sentiō.
translation: Under a thin cloak I feel the night cold in every limb.

sentence: Ex vultū tuō sentiō tē mihi nōn omnia dīxisse.
translation: From your face I can tell that you have not told me everything.

sentence: Dē bellō aliter quam cēterī senātōrēs sentiō, itaque tacēre nōn possum.
translation: On the war I take a different view from the other senators, and so I cannot keep silent.

sentence: Nāvis frūmentō onusta post longam tempestātem tandem Ōstiam pervēnit.
translation: The ship, loaded with grain, finally reached Ostia after a long storm.

sentence: Nautae nāvem in lītore reficiunt, quod ventus vēla lacerāverat.
translation: The sailors are repairing the ship on the beach, because the wind had ripped the sails.

sentence: Māter fīlium in nāve stantem vīdit et lacrimās tenēre nōn potuit.
translation: The mother saw her son standing on the ship and could not hold back her tears.

sentence: Cotīdiē māne in portum dēscendimus ut piscēs recentēs emāmus.
translation: Every morning we go down to the harbour to buy fresh fish.

sentence: In portū servī tōtum diem clāmant, dum amphorās gravēs ex nāve tollunt.
translation: In the harbour the slaves shout all day long while they haul heavy amphorae off the ship.

sentence: Nautīs fessīs nihil dulcius est quam portum patrium tandem cōnspicere.
translation: For exhausted sailors nothing is sweeter than sighting their home harbour at last.

sentence: Epistulam frātris ad lūcernam lēgī, postquam omnēs in vīllā dormīre coepērunt.
translation: I read my brother's letter by lamplight, once everyone in the house had gone to sleep.

sentence: Servus epistulam sigillō obsignātam per tōtam urbem ad senātōrem tulit.
translation: A slave carried the letter, sealed with a signet, right across the city to the senator.

sentence: Epistula tua mē tantopere commōvit ut noctem tōtam vigilārem.
translation: Your letter moved me so much that I lay awake the whole night.

sentence: Puer in cērā litterās magnās scrībit, sed manus eius adhūc tremit.
translation: The boy is writing big letters in the wax, but his hand still shakes.

sentence: Lapicīda litterās in marmore sculpit, ut nōmen mortuī semper maneat.
translation: The stonecutter carves the letters into the marble so that the dead man's name will last.

sentence: Litterīs Graecīs dēditus Mārcus rūrī vīvere quam in urbe māvult.
translation: Devoted to Greek literature, Marcus would rather live in the country than in the city.

sentence: Avia nōbīs fābulam dē lupō nārrābat, dum ignis in focō ārdēbat.
translation: Grandmother used to tell us the story about the wolf while the fire burned on the hearth.

sentence: Fābula Plautī in theātrō tantum rīsum mōvit ut spectātōrēs plauderent.
translation: Plautus' play raised so much laughter in the theatre that the audience broke into applause.

sentence: Nēmō tibi crēdit; ista dē thēsaurō fābula puerīs sōlīs placet.
translation: Nobody believes you; that story about the treasure only appeals to children.

sentence: Māter fīliae carmen cantābat, dōnec puella in cūnīs obdormīvit.
translation: The mother kept singing a song to her daughter until the girl fell asleep in the cradle.

sentence: Poēta in convīviō carmen novum recitāvit, sed nēmō attentē audiēbat.
translation: The poet recited a new poem at the dinner party, but nobody was listening closely.

sentence: Hoc carmen Vergilī semper mē cōnsōlātur, quotiēns amīcōs absentēs dēsīderō.
translation: This poem of Virgil's always comforts me whenever I miss absent friends.

sentence: Puer linguam adussit, dum pultem ferventem nimis avidē gustat.
translation: The boy burned his tongue tasting the scalding porridge too greedily.

sentence: In tabernā Ōstiēnsī quīnque linguae simul audiuntur, cum nāvēs adveniunt.
translation: In an Ostian tavern you hear five languages at once when the ships come in.

sentence: Linguam Graecam decem annōs discō, sed adhūc mē loquī pudet.
translation: I have been learning Greek for ten years, and I am still ashamed to speak it.

sentence: Cicerō ōrātiōnem in senātū habuit, et coniūrātī pallidī tacuērunt.
translation: Cicero delivered a speech in the senate, and the conspirators went pale and fell silent.

sentence: Puer ōrātiōnem suam ante speculum recitat, dum pater in hortō audit.
translation: The boy practises his speech in front of the mirror while his father listens from the garden.

sentence: Ōrātiō tua tam longa fuit ut multī ante fīnem discēderent.
translation: Your speech was so long that many people left before the end.

sentence: In senātū sententiam meam līberē dīxī, quamquam paucī mihi assēnsī sunt.
translation: I stated my opinion freely in the senate, though few agreed with me.

sentence: Dē pretiō agrī cum frātre disputō, sed sententiam meam mūtāre nōlō.
translation: I keep arguing with my brother about the price of the field, but I refuse to change my mind.

sentence: Ubi omnēs tacent, ūnīus hominis sententia plūs quam clāmor valet.
translation: When everyone else stays silent, one person's opinion counts for more than a shout.

sentence: Avus noster nōmina nepōtum iam memoriā tenēre nōn potest.
translation: Our grandfather can no longer keep his grandchildren's names in his memory.

sentence: Discipulī tōtum carmen memoriae mandant, priusquam magister eōs interrogat.
translation: The pupils learn the whole poem by heart before the teacher questions them.

sentence: Memoria illīus aestātis, quam ad mare ēgimus, mihi dulcis manet.
translation: The memory of that summer we spent by the sea stays sweet for me.

sentence: Tōtam noctem dentis dolōrem passus sum nec somnum cēpī.
translation: I suffered a toothache the whole night through and never got to sleep.

sentence: Dominus servōs in culīnā clāmāre nōn patitur, dum cēnam parant.
translation: The master does not allow the slaves to shout in the kitchen while they are getting dinner ready.

sentence: Tantam iniūriam ā frātre meō patī diūtius nōn possum.
translation: I cannot put up with such an insult from my own brother any longer.

sentence: Avus meus in lectō suō placidē mortuus est, tōtā familiā adstante.
translation: My grandfather died peacefully in his own bed, with the whole family standing around him.

sentence: Nisi statim medicum vocāveritis, hic homō ante lūcem moriētur.
translation: Unless you call a doctor at once, this man will die before daybreak.

sentence: Mālō honestē morī quam sub tyrannō turpiter vīvere.
translation: I would rather die with honour than live in disgrace under a tyrant.

sentence: Fīlia mea sub prīmā lūce nāta est, dum gallus in hortō canit.
translation: My daughter was born at first light, while the cock was crowing out in the garden.

sentence: Quotiēns in hāc familiā puer nāscitur, pater arborem in agrō serit.
translation: Whenever a boy is born into this family, the father plants a tree in the field.

sentence: Servus noster in servitūte nātus est, sed animō semper līber mānsit.
translation: Our slave was born into slavery, but in spirit he always remained a free man.

sentence: Māter mea pānem in furnō coquere cōnātur, sed carbōnēs madent.
translation: My mother is trying to bake bread in the oven, but the coals are damp.

sentence: Frūstrā per turbam in forō ad rōstra pervenīre cōnātī sumus.
translation: We tried in vain to push through the crowd in the forum and reach the speakers' platform.

sentence: Crās iterum cōnābor equum domāre, quamquam mē herī dēiēcit.
translation: Tomorrow I will try to break the horse again, even though it threw me yesterday.

sentence: Tempestātem crās fore meliōrem arbitror, quia hirundinēs altē volant.
translation: I reckon the weather will be better tomorrow, because the swallows are flying high.

sentence: Iūdex illum testem mentītum esse arbitrātus est, itaque eum dīmīsit.
translation: The judge decided that the witness had lied, and so dismissed him.

sentence: Multī cīvēs hunc cōnsulem optimum fuisse arbitrābantur, dōnec fūrtum patuit.
translation: Many citizens thought this consul had been the best of all, until his theft came to light.

sentence: Ad templī gradūs mendīcus cotīdiē sedet et stipem ā praetereuntibus petit.
translation: A beggar sits at the temple steps every day and asks the passers-by for a coin.

sentence: Fabrī novum templum in Capitōliō aedificant, sed senātus pecūniam nōndum solvit.
translation: The builders are putting up a new temple on the Capitol, but the senate has not paid them yet.

sentence: In templō obscūrō stetī et deōs prō frātre aegrō ōrāvī.
translation: I stood in the dark temple and prayed to the gods for my sick brother.

sentence: Mūrus vetus post imbrēs cecidit et viam tōtam obstrūxit.
translation: The old wall collapsed after the rains and blocked the whole road.

sentence: Mīlitēs mūrum urbis noctū custōdiunt, quia hostēs prope castra vīsī sunt.
translation: The soldiers guard the city wall at night, because enemies have been spotted near the camp.

sentence: Puerī in mūrō tabernae nōmina sua carbōne scrīpsērunt, et caupō īrātus est.
translation: The boys wrote their names in charcoal on the shop wall, and the innkeeper was furious.

sentence: Portā Capēnā ēgressī, ad avunculī vīllam ante merīdiem pervēnimus.
translation: Once we had gone out by the Porta Capena, we reached my uncle's country house before noon.

sentence: Custōs portam urbis prīmā lūce aperit et mercātōrēs intrāre iubet.
translation: The watchman opens the city gate at first light and lets the traders come in.

sentence: Cum hostēs ad portās vēnissent, mātrēs trepidae līberōs domum abdūxērunt.
translation: When the enemy had reached the gates, the frightened mothers led their children away home.

sentence: Iānuam vespere clāve clausī, quod fūrēs in vīcō nostrō vagantur.
translation: I locked the front door with the key in the evening, because thieves are prowling round our street.

sentence: Cliēntēs ante patrōnī iānuam stant, dum ōstiārius nōmina eōrum recitat.
translation: The clients stand at their patron's door while the doorkeeper reads their names out.

sentence: Puer per rīmam iānuae spectābat, quia parentēs dē pecūniā clāmābant.
translation: The boy was watching through a crack in the door, because his parents were shouting about money.

sentence: Ex fenestrā superiōre māter clāmāvit ut statim domum venīrēmus.
translation: Mother shouted down from the upstairs window for us to come home at once.

sentence: Aestāte pistor fenestram apertam relinquit, ut odor pānis viātōrēs alliciat.
translation: In summer the baker leaves his window open, so that the smell of bread draws travellers in.

sentence: Fenestrā clausā, tamen strepitum plaustrōrum tōtā nocte audīvī nec dormīvī.
translation: Even with the window shut, I heard the rumble of the carts all night and got no sleep.

sentence: Servō quī hortum cūrat magis quam vīlicō ipsī crēdō.
translation: I trust the slave who looks after the garden more than the overseer himself.

sentence: Nūntiō dē victōriā nōn statim crēdō, dōnec ipse litterās lēgerō.
translation: I don't believe a report of victory straight away, not until I have read the dispatch myself.

sentence: Vix crēdō tē per tantam nivem sōlum ad nōs vēnisse.
translation: I can hardly believe you came all the way to us alone through snow like that.

sentence: Ubi māter clāvēs cellae vīnāriae cēlāverit plānē nesciō.
translation: I have absolutely no idea where mother has hidden the keys to the wine cellar.

sentence: Nesciō utrum dominus mē ad urbem an ad vīllam crās mittat.
translation: I don't know whether the master is sending me into the city tomorrow or out to the country house.

sentence: Cantāre nesciō, sed in balneīs semper canō, ut omnēs rīdeant.
translation: I can't sing to save my life, but I always sing at the baths, so everybody laughs.

sentence: Duās tabulās glūtine iungō, ut mēnsa prīstinam fōrmam recipiat.
translation: I glue the two boards together so the table gets its original shape back.

sentence: Dextram tibi iungō et amīcitiam nostram testibus deīs cōnfirmō.
translation: I clasp your right hand and seal our friendship with the gods as witnesses.

sentence: Cōpiās meās cum sociīs libenter iungō, quia sōlus hostem nōn sustineō.
translation: I am glad to combine my troops with the allies', because on my own I cannot hold off the enemy.

sentence: Vespere zōnam solvō et fessa membra ad focum tepidum trahō.
translation: In the evening I loosen my belt and drag my tired limbs over to the warm hearth.

sentence: Mercēdem operāriīs ante occāsum sōlis solvō, ut lēx iubet.
translation: I pay the labourers their wages before sunset, just as the law requires.

sentence: Quaestiōnem quam magister tōtī scholae prōpōnit nūllō negōtiō solvō.
translation: The problem the teacher sets the whole class I solve without the slightest trouble.

sentence: Ante somnum iānuam obserō et fenestrās contrā ventum frīgidum claudō.
translation: Before bed I bolt the door and shut the windows against the cold wind.

sentence: Tabernam merīdiē claudō, quia nēmō hōc calōre in forum dēscendit.
translation: I shut the shop at midday, because in this heat nobody comes down to the forum.

sentence: Oculōs claudō, sed clāmor ex viā veniēns somnum mihi ēripit.
translation: I close my eyes, but the shouting coming up from the street robs me of sleep.

sentence: Cum hospes pulsat, iānuam aperiō et eum ad focum dūcō.
translation: Whenever a guest knocks, I open the door and take him over to the fire.

sentence: Rīvum in hortō aperiō ut aqua ad rādīcēs vītium fluat.
translation: I open the channel in the garden so the water runs down to the roots of the vines.

sentence: Epistulam ā frātre missam tremēns aperiō, nam bellum in Galliā gerit.
translation: I open the letter sent by my brother with shaking hands, because he is fighting a war in Gaul.

sentence: Fīlium prīmum avī nōmine Mārcum appellō, ut mōs maiōrum postulat.
translation: I name my eldest son Marcus after his grandfather, as ancestral custom demands.

sentence: Vīcīnum meum patrem comiter appellō, quia mē puerum ipse ēducāvit.
translation: I warmly call my neighbour father, because he was the one who raised me as a boy.

sentence: Cum iūdex mē iniūstē damnat, tribūnōs plēbis statim appellō.
translation: When the judge condemns me unjustly, I appeal at once to the tribunes of the plebs.

sentence: Domī cum līberīs Graecē loquor, ut linguam ā tenerīs annīs discant.
translation: At home I speak Greek with the children, so that they pick the language up from their earliest years.

sentence: In cūriā dē frūmentī pretiō loquor, dum senātōrēs mihi obstrepunt.
translation: I speak in the senate house about the price of grain while the senators shout me down.

sentence: Nōn temere loquor, nam quae dīcō oculīs meīs ipse vīdī.
translation: I am not talking carelessly: what I am telling you I saw with my own eyes.

sentence: Vestīgia lupī in nive per silvam ad antrum sequor.
translation: I follow the wolf's tracks through the snow, across the wood, right to its den.

sentence: Ducem nostrum etiam in Britanniam sequor, quamquam mē mīlitiae taedet.
translation: I will follow our general even as far as Britain, though I am sick of soldiering.

sentence: Cicerōnis cōnsilium sequor potius quam clāmōrem turbae in forō.
translation: I follow Cicero's advice rather than the roar of the crowd in the forum.

sentence: Ad cēnam parandam ollā fictilī, nōn argentō, cotīdiē ūtor.
translation: For getting dinner ready I use an earthenware pot every day, not silver.

sentence: In tabernā patris statērā antīquā ūtor, quam avus mihi relīquit.
translation: In my father's shop I use the old set of scales my grandfather left me.

sentence: Bonā valētūdine adhūc ūtor, quamquam iam septuāgēsimum annum agō.
translation: I still enjoy good health, even though I am now in my seventieth year.

sentence: Avia mea mēnsam ligneam cotīdiē ante cēnam dīligenter pūrgat.
translation: My grandmother scrubs the wooden table carefully every day before dinner.

sentence: In caupōnā caupō mēnsās vīnō sordidās celeriter lāvit.
translation: In the tavern the innkeeper quickly washed down the tables stained with wine.

sentence: Nihil mē magis dēlectat quam cum amīcī circum mēnsam nostram sedent.
translation: Nothing pleases me more than when friends are sitting around our table.

sentence: Māter puerum aegrum in lectum posuit et fābulam longam nārrāvit.
translation: Mother put the sick boy to bed and told him a long story.

sentence: Convīvae in lectīs recumbēbant dum servī vīnum frīgidum ferēbant.
translation: The guests reclined on the couches while the slaves carried in cold wine.

sentence: Māne aegrē surgō, quod lectus meus hieme calidissimus vidētur.
translation: I get up only with difficulty in the morning, because my bed feels warmest in winter.

sentence: Māter cēnam parābat, cum subitō amīcī patris ex urbe advēnērunt.
translation: Mother was getting dinner ready when father's friends suddenly arrived from the city.

sentence: Ad cēnam tē invītō, sī hodiē negōtiīs tandem līberāberis.
translation: I am inviting you to dinner, if you finally get free of business today.

sentence: Nūlla cēna mihi umquam suāvior fuit quam illa apud avum.
translation: No dinner was ever more delightful to me than that one at my grandfather's house.

sentence: Cotīdiē māne in forum dēscendō ut pānem et piscēs emam.
translation: Every morning I go down to the marketplace to buy bread and fish.

sentence: In forō ōrātor dē lēgibus dīcēbat, sed turba clāmābat.
translation: In the forum a speaker was arguing about the laws, but the crowd kept shouting.

sentence: Semper mē dēlectat forum, ubi omnia rūmōribus et clāmōribus fervent.
translation: The forum always delights me, where everything seethes with rumours and shouting.

sentence: Avus meus in hortō rosās et herbās omnī vēre serēbat.
translation: My grandfather used to plant roses and herbs in the garden every spring.

sentence: Post cēnam in hortō ambulāvimus et dē philosophiā diū disputāvimus.
translation: After dinner we walked in the garden and argued about philosophy for a long time.

sentence: Hortus meus neglēctus est; sentēs rosās meās iam superant.
translation: My garden has been left to itself; the brambles are already getting the better of my roses.

sentence: Agricola agrōs suōs ante lūcem arat, dum terra rōre ūmida est.
translation: The farmer plows his fields before dawn, while the ground is still damp with dew.

sentence: Post bellum mīlitibus veterānīs agrī prope Capuam distribūtī sunt.
translation: After the war, fields near Capua were handed out to the veteran soldiers.

sentence: Ager ille siccus nihil praeter spīnās multōs iam annōs tulit.
translation: That dry field has produced nothing but thorns for many years now.

sentence: Iuvenēs cotīdiē in Campō Mārtiō equitāre et natāre solent.
translation: The young men ride and swim on the Campus Martius every day.

sentence: Ante prīmam lūcem exercitus in campō apertō aciem īnstrūxit.
translation: Before first light the army drew up its battle line on the open plain.

sentence: Ex colle campum lātē patentem vīdimus, ubi ovēs errābant.
translation: From the hill we saw the plain stretching far and wide, with sheep wandering over it.

sentence: Nāvis nostra ad īnsulam parvam tempestāte adversā ācta est.
translation: Our ship was driven onto a small island by a storm against us.

sentence: In īnsulā angustā habitāmus, ubi fūmus per omnia cēnācula errat.
translation: We live in a cramped apartment block where the smoke drifts through every upstairs room.

sentence: Ōlim in īnsulā vīvere cupiēbam, procul ab urbis strepitū.
translation: I once longed to live on an island, far from the noise of the city.

sentence: Pōns ligneus tam angustus est ut plaustra vix trānsīre possint.
translation: The wooden bridge is so narrow that carts can barely get across.

sentence: Mīlitēs pontem post sē incendērunt nē hostēs flūmen trānsīrent.
translation: The soldiers burned the bridge behind them so that the enemy could not cross the river.

sentence: In ponte stantēs diū spectāvimus nāvēs sub nōbīs lābentēs.
translation: Standing on the bridge, we watched the boats slipping past beneath us for a long time.

sentence: Trēs diēs difficile iter fēcimus, quod imber viās corrūperat.
translation: We travelled a hard road for three days, because the rain had ruined the way.

sentence: Caesar magnīs itineribus ad Rhēnum contendit priusquam hostēs convenīrent.
translation: Caesar hurried to the Rhine by forced marches before the enemy could gather.

sentence: Hoc iter brevius est, sed per silvam obscūram et perīculōsam dūcit.
translation: This route is shorter, but it leads through a dark and dangerous forest.

sentence: Magister, quī in casā proximā habitābat, fīliam meam vespere docēbat.
translation: The teacher who lived in the house next door used to give my daughter lessons in the evening.

sentence: Tōta schola magistrum novum exspectat, quī herī Athēnīs vēnit.
translation: The whole school is waiting for the new teacher, who arrived from Athens yesterday.

sentence: Grātiās magistrō meō agō, quod mē Graecē legere docuit.
translation: I am grateful to my teacher, because he taught me to read Greek.

sentence: Discipulus ante lūcem surgit et tabulam suam ad lūdum portat.
translation: The pupil gets up before daylight and carries his writing tablet to school.

sentence: Ūnus tantum discipulus respondēre potuit; cēterī tacitī sedēbant.
translation: Only one pupil managed to answer; the rest sat there in silence.

sentence: Patientia magistrī discipulō timidō plūs prōdest quam ūlla poena.
translation: A teacher's patience does a nervous pupil more good than any punishment.

sentence: In vīllā nostrā avus semper iūdex inter frātrēs pugnantēs erat.
translation: At our house grandfather was always the judge between the squabbling brothers.

sentence: Iūdex, testibus audītīs, reum absolvit et populus in forō clāmāvit.
translation: Once the witnesses had been heard, the judge acquitted the defendant, and the crowd in the forum roared.

sentence: Nēmō iūdicī crēdit quī ā mercātōre dīvite pecūniam accēpit.
translation: Nobody trusts a judge who has taken money from a rich merchant.

sentence: Duo testēs in tabernā aderant, ubi mercātor pecūniam meam abstulit.
translation: Two witnesses were there in the shop where the trader made off with my money.

sentence: Iūdex testem interrogāvit, sed ille prae timōre nihil respondēre potuit.
translation: The judge questioned the witness, but he was too frightened to get a word out.

sentence: Sine testibus nēmō in forō tibi crēdet, quamvīs vēra dīcās.
translation: Without witnesses nobody in the forum will believe you, however true what you say is.

sentence: Avia mea, quamquam legere numquam didicit, fēmina sapiēns habēbātur.
translation: My grandmother never learned to read, and yet she was considered a wise woman.

sentence: Senātōrēs virum sapientem ex Graeciā arcessīvērunt, quī cōnsilium dē bellō daret.
translation: The senators summoned a wise man from Greece to advise them about the war.

sentence: Sapientī satis est pauca habēre, dummodo animus quiētus maneat.
translation: For a wise man it is enough to own little, so long as his mind stays at peace.

sentence: Frāter meus stultus canem aliēnum in viā vexāvit et morsus est.
translation: My foolish brother tormented somebody else's dog in the street and got bitten.

sentence: Mercātor stultus tōtam pecūniam ūnā nāve mīsit, quae periit.
translation: A foolish trader shipped his entire fortune in a single vessel, and it went down.

sentence: Nōlī mē stultum vocāre priusquam causam meam audīveris.
translation: Don't call me a fool before you have heard my side of it.

sentence: Pater meus iūstam partem hērēditātis etiam sorōrī minimae relīquit.
translation: My father left a fair share of the inheritance even to his youngest sister.

sentence: Dominus iūstus servīs suīs post messem cibum vīnumque dedit.
translation: A fair master gave his slaves food and wine once the harvest was in.

sentence: Iūdicium iūstum nōn semper omnibus placet, sed cīvitātem servat.
translation: A just verdict does not please everyone, but it is what holds the state together.

sentence: Mēnsa in pavīmentō nōn aequō stat, itaque vīnum semper effunditur.
translation: The table stands on a floor that isn't level, so the wine keeps spilling.

sentence: Agricolae frūmentum aequīs partibus inter sē post messem dīvīsērunt.
translation: After the harvest the farmers split the grain into equal shares among themselves.

sentence: Nōn aequum est puerum pūnīre propter culpam frātris suī.
translation: It is not fair to punish a boy for something his brother did.

sentence: Puteus in āreā commūnis est, unde omnēs vīcīnī aquam trahunt.
translation: The well in the courtyard is shared, and all the neighbours draw their water from it.

sentence: Frātrēs meī tabernam commūnem in forō tenent et lucrum dīvidunt.
translation: My brothers keep a shop together in the forum and split the profits.

sentence: Perīculum commūne omnibus cīvibus erat, itaque etiam inimīcī convēnērunt.
translation: The danger was common to every citizen, so even enemies came together.

sentence: Fīlia mea nunc cubiculum proprium habet, nam frāter Rōmam discessit.
translation: My daughter has a room of her own now, since her brother has gone off to Rome.

sentence: Nūllum agrum proprium habēmus, sed dominī agrōs quotannīs colimus.
translation: We own no land of our own, but year after year we farm the master's fields.

sentence: Rīdēre sine causā stultī proprium est, tacēre sapientis.
translation: Laughing for no reason is the mark of a fool; staying silent, of a wise man.

sentence: Avia mea scientiam herbārum ā mātre suā in hortō didicit.
translation: My grandmother learned her knowledge of herbs from her own mother out in the garden.

sentence: Medicus novus scientiam suam in castrīs ostendit, ubi multī mīlitēs vulnerātī iacēbant.
translation: The new doctor proved his knowledge in the camp, where many wounded soldiers were lying.

sentence: Frātrī meō scientia magna est, sed nūlla modestia, itaque omnēs eum vītant.
translation: My brother has great knowledge but no modesty, so everyone avoids him.

sentence: Māter mea sapientiā, nōn clāmōre, lītem inter frātrēs meōs composuit.
translation: My mother settled the quarrel between my brothers with wisdom, not with shouting.

sentence: Senātōrēs veterem cōnsulem propter sapientiam eius saepe in cūriā audiēbant.
translation: The senators often listened to the old consul in the senate house because of his wisdom.

sentence: Sapientia sine ūsū vītae mihi vidētur vōx inānis et frīgida.
translation: Wisdom without any experience of life strikes me as an empty, cold word.

sentence: Vīlicus ratiōnēs vīllae ante Kalendās dominō semper reddere dēbet.
translation: The farm manager always has to hand the villa's accounts to the master before the first of the month.

sentence: Dux novam ratiōnem oppugnandī excōgitāvit, quia mūrī urbis nimis altī erant.
translation: The general worked out a new method of attack, because the city walls were too high.

sentence: Hominem ā bēstiīs nōn vīrēs sed ratiō atque ōrātiō sēparat.
translation: What separates a human being from the beasts is not strength but reason and speech.

sentence: Puer tandem mātrī vēritātem dē amphorā frāctā trementī vōce cōnfessus est.
translation: The boy finally confessed the truth about the broken jar to his mother in a trembling voice.

sentence: In forō testis vēritātem cēlāre nōn ausus est, quamquam valdē timēbat.
translation: In the forum the witness did not dare to hide the truth, though he was very frightened.

sentence: Vēritās saepe amāra est, sed mendācium amīcitiam celerius perdit.
translation: The truth is often bitter, but a lie destroys a friendship faster.

sentence: Nātūra lupī numquam mūtātur, etiam sī catulum domī tuae nūtrīs.
translation: A wolf's nature never changes, even if you rear the cub in your own house.

sentence: Philosophus in hortō dīcēbat nātūram ipsam optimam ducem vītae esse.
translation: In the garden the philosopher used to say that nature herself is the best guide in life.

sentence: Soror mea nātūrā timida est, itaque in convīviīs vix loquitur.
translation: My sister is shy by nature, so she hardly says a word at dinner parties.

sentence: Postquam fīlia nostra nāta est, tōtus mundus mihi novus vidēbātur.
translation: After our daughter was born, the whole world seemed new to me.

sentence: Mercātor noster per tōtum mundum nāvigāvit et nāvēs pipere plēnās redūxit.
translation: Our merchant sailed all over the world and brought back ships full of pepper.

sentence: Avus meus dīcere solēbat mundum ante bellum multō meliōrem fuisse.
translation: My grandfather used to say that the world had been far better before the war.

sentence: Puerī in harēnā orbem virgā dūxērunt et intrā eum diū lūsērunt.
translation: The boys drew a circle in the sand with a stick and played inside it for a long time.

sentence: Rōmānī antīquī sē tōtīus orbis terrārum dominōs esse crēdēbant.
translation: The Romans of old believed that they were masters of the whole world.

sentence: Post mortem uxōris tōtus orbis terrārum mihi vacuus atque mūtus erat.
translation: After my wife's death the whole world felt empty and silent to me.

sentence: Māter mea in culīnā tamquam rēgīna imperat, et nēmō contrādīcere audet.
translation: My mother rules the kitchen like a queen, and nobody dares to contradict her.

sentence: Rēgīna Aegyptī classem suam ad Actium mīsit et proelium ipsa spectāvit.
translation: The queen of Egypt sent her fleet to Actium and watched the battle herself.

sentence: Lēgātī rēgīnae dōna attulērunt, sed illa eōs ante vesperum nōn accēpit.
translation: The envoys brought gifts to the queen, but she did not receive them before evening.

sentence: Mulier in macellō holera vēndit et dē pretiīs cum omnibus cotīdiē contendit.
translation: The woman sells vegetables in the market and haggles with everybody over prices every day.

sentence: Mulier quaedam ad iānuam pulsāvit et aquam ā mātre meā petīvit.
translation: Some woman knocked at our door and asked my mother for water.

sentence: Illa mulier tot bella vīdit ut nihil iam eam terrēre possit.
translation: That woman has seen so many wars that nothing can frighten her any more.

sentence: Coniūnx mea tōtam noctem vigilāvit, dum īnfāns aegrōtus in cūnīs plōrat.
translation: My wife stayed awake the whole night while the sick baby cried in his cradle.

sentence: Coniugem meum in tabernā exspectō, quia hodiē mercēdem suam accipiet.
translation: I'm waiting for my husband at the tavern, because he collects his wages today.

sentence: Post trīgintā annōs coniugī meae adhūc flōrēs ex hortō nostrō ferō.
translation: After thirty years I still bring my wife flowers from our own garden.

sentence: Puer stilum manū dextrā tenet, sed litterās prāvē scrībit.
translation: The boy holds the stylus in his right hand, but his letters come out crooked.

sentence: Hostēs in dextrō cornū aciēī nostrae subitō impetum fēcērunt.
translation: The enemy suddenly charged the right wing of our battle line.

sentence: Vulnus in umerō dextrō acceptum mē omnī hieme adhūc torquet.
translation: The wound I took in my right shoulder still torments me every winter.

sentence: Māter puerum monet nē cibum sinistrā manū umquam capiat.
translation: Mother warns the boy never to take food with his left hand.

sentence: Mīles scūtum sinistrō bracchiō sustinēbat, quamquam vulnus adhūc sanguinem fundēbat.
translation: The soldier kept holding up his shield with his left arm, though the wound was still bleeding.

sentence: Nautae, ōmine sinistrō territī, nāvem eō diē solvere nōluērunt.
translation: The sailors, frightened by an unlucky omen, refused to set sail that day.

sentence: Puella sōla per hortum nocte īre nōn audet, quia canēs lātrant.
translation: The girl doesn't dare walk through the garden alone at night, because the dogs are barking.

sentence: Nēmō in senātū contrā cōnsulem tam ācriter dīcere ausus est.
translation: Nobody in the senate dared to speak so fiercely against the consul.

sentence: Sī vērē mē amās, patrem tuum dē nūptiīs rogāre audē.
translation: If you really love me, find the courage to ask your father about the marriage.

sentence: Avia gaudet quod nepōs tandem ex castrīs domum rediit.
translation: Grandmother is overjoyed that her grandson has finally come home from camp.

sentence: Vīcīnī nostrī victōriā aurīgae in circō tōtam noctem gāvīsī sunt.
translation: Our neighbours celebrated the charioteer's win at the Circus all night long.

sentence: Nōn gaudeō malīs inimīcī meī, quamquam saepe mē laesit.
translation: I take no pleasure in my enemy's misfortunes, even though he has hurt me often.

sentence: Post longum iter caput mihi dolet et pedēs vix moveō.
translation: After the long journey my head aches and I can barely move my feet.

sentence: Tōta urbs mortem puerī doluit, quem plaustrum in viā oppressit.
translation: The whole city mourned the boy whom a wagon crushed in the street.

sentence: Dē amīcī exsiliō magis doleō quam dē meā ipsīus paupertāte.
translation: My friend's exile grieves me more than my own poverty does.

sentence: Gelū nocturnum vītibus nostrīs in colle plūs quam grandō nocuit.
translation: The night frost did more damage to our vines on the hillside than the hail did.

sentence: Falsus rūmor in forō sparsus mercātōrī nostrō magnopere nocuit.
translation: A false rumour spread around the forum did our merchant serious harm.

sentence: Nōlī tibi ipsī nocēre, dum inimīcum tuum ulcīscī cupis.
translation: Don't do yourself harm while you're set on getting revenge on your enemy.

sentence: Servī dominae semper pārent, quamquam eōs saepe in culīnā increpat.
translation: The slaves always obey the mistress, even though she often scolds them in the kitchen.

sentence: Legiōnēs imperiō ducis pāruērunt et flūmen ante lūcem trānsiērunt.
translation: The legions obeyed the general's order and crossed the river before daybreak.

sentence: Lēgibus pārēre dēbēmus, etiam sī nōbīs dūrae aut inīquae videntur.
translation: We have to obey the laws, even when they strike us as harsh or unfair.

sentence: Nova vīlla uxōrī meae placet, mihi autem nimis remōta vidētur.
translation: My wife likes the new country house, but to me it seems too far out of the way.

sentence: Novus histriō populō in theātrō placuit, senātōribus autem displicuit.
translation: The new actor went down well with the crowd at the theatre, but the senators disliked him.

sentence: Dum omnibus placēre studeō, mihi ipsī iam displiceō.
translation: In trying to please everybody, I have ended up disliking myself.

sentence: Frāter meus tōtam noctem litterīs Graecīs sub lūcernā studēbat.
translation: My brother spent the whole night studying Greek literature by lamplight.

sentence: Multī adulēscentēs Athēnās mittuntur, ut ibi philosophiae ēloquentiaeque studeant.
translation: Many young men are sent to Athens to study philosophy and rhetoric there.

sentence: Pater pecūniae semper studuit; ego ōtiō et librīs studeō.
translation: My father only ever cared about money; what I care about is leisure and books.

sentence: Avus meus nōnāgintā annōs nātus adhūc valet et cotīdiē in hortō labōrat.
translation: My grandfather is ninety and still in good health, working in the garden every day.

sentence: Ille ōrātor apud iūdicēs plūs grātiā quam argūmentīs valēbat.
translation: That speaker carried more weight with the jurors through influence than through arguments.

sentence: Post tantum labōrem in agrīs vix valeō ad cēnam surgere.
translation: After so much work in the fields I barely have the strength to get up for dinner.

sentence: Tōtam noctem intrā parietēs mānsimus, quia imber nōn cessābat.
translation: We stayed indoors the whole night, because the rain would not let up.

sentence: Mīlitēs intrā castra tabernācula pōnunt, priusquam nox venit.
translation: The soldiers pitch their tents inside the camp before night comes on.

sentence: Intrā trēs diēs respondēre dēbēs, aut spem omnem āmittēs.
translation: You have to answer within three days, or you will lose every hope.

sentence: Coquum nostrum iubeō cēnam ante noctem parāre, quia hospitēs veniunt.
translation: I am telling our cook to have dinner ready before nightfall, since guests are coming.

sentence: Imperātor legiōnēs ante prīmam lūcem flūmen trānsīre iussit.
translation: The general ordered the legions to cross the river before first light.

sentence: Cūr mē semper prīmum surgere iubēs, numquam frātrem meum?
translation: Why do you always order me to get up first, and never my brother?

sentence: Post longum iter per pulverem nihil nisi aquam frīgidam cupiō.
translation: After a long march through the dust I want nothing but cold water.

sentence: Multī iuvenēs Rōmam venīre cupiunt, ubi glōriam et pecūniam quaerunt.
translation: Many young men long to come to Rome, where they go looking for glory and money.

sentence: Puella epistulam aperīre cupiēbat, sed manūs eius metū tremēbant.
translation: The girl was desperate to open the letter, but her hands were shaking with fear.

sentence: Cēnam frīgidam edere nōlō; ignem in culīnā iterum accende.
translation: I don't want to eat a cold dinner; light the fire in the kitchen again.

sentence: Nōlīte in flūmen dēscendere, puerī; aqua altior est quam vidētur.
translation: Don't go down into the river, boys; the water is deeper than it looks.

sentence: Nōluī tibi vērum dīcere, quia dolōrem tuum vidēre nōn poteram.
translation: I didn't want to tell you the truth, because I couldn't bear to see you hurting.

sentence: Aestāte in hortō dormīre mālō quam in cubiculō calidō.
translation: In summer I would rather sleep out in the garden than in a hot bedroom.

sentence: Frāter meus in agrīs labōrāre māvult quam in tabernā vēndere.
translation: My brother would rather work in the fields than sell things in a shop.

sentence: Semper vēritātem dūram audīre māluī quam blanda mendācia amīcōrum.
translation: I have always preferred a hard truth to the flattering lies of friends.

sentence: Semper anxius fīō, cum per angustās urbis viās nocte ambulō.
translation: I always get anxious when I walk through the city's narrow streets at night.

sentence: Ubi mercātōrēs in forō conveniunt, subitō omnia cārissima fīunt.
translation: Once the traders gather in the forum, everything suddenly becomes horribly expensive.

sentence: Quid dē līberīs nostrīs fīet, sī bellum iterum incipiet?
translation: What will become of our children if war starts up again?

sentence: Cotīdiē vespere clāvēs tabernae dominō meō reddō et domum eō.
translation: Every evening I hand the shop keys back to my master and go home.

sentence: Nūntius epistulam signātam cōnsulī reddidit et statim discessit.
translation: The messenger delivered the sealed letter to the consul and left at once.

sentence: Nūlla pecūnia mihi patrem meum reddet, quem bellum abstulit.
translation: No amount of money will give me back my father, whom the war took away.

sentence: Cistam cum pecūniā vīcīnō fidēlī trādō, dum Rōmae absum.
translation: I am handing the money box over to a trustworthy neighbour while I am away in Rome.

sentence: Dux victus gladium suum hostibus trādidit et arma dēposuit.
translation: The defeated general handed his sword over to the enemy and laid down his weapons.

sentence: Haec carmina avī nostrī nōbīs trādidērunt, nē memoria perīret.
translation: Our grandfathers handed these songs down to us so that the memory would not die.

sentence: Avia mea nōbīs ānulum ostendit, quem ab avō accēperat.
translation: My grandmother showed us the ring she had been given by my grandfather.

sentence: Hospitibus novīs tōtam vīllam ostendō, etiam cellam vīnāriam.
translation: I show the new guests around the whole villa, even the wine cellar.

sentence: Ostende mihi manūs tuās; pulverem et sanguinem cēlāre nōn potes.
translation: Show me your hands; you cannot hide the dust and the blood.

sentence: Māter mē dē serpentibus in agrō saepe monuerat, sed nōn audīvī.
translation: My mother had often warned me about the snakes in the field, but I didn't listen.

sentence: Magister discipulōs monet ut tabulās cērātās sēcum ferant.
translation: The teacher reminds his pupils to bring their wax tablets with them.

sentence: Tē moneō ut cautus sīs, quia ille homō dē pretiō mentītur.
translation: I am warning you to be careful, because that man lies about the price.

sentence: Ante imbrem olīvās in fundō avī celeriter colligō.
translation: I gather the olives quickly on my grandfather's farm before the rain comes.

sentence: Servus tabellās per tōtum forum dispersās colligit et dominō reddit.
translation: The slave collects the tablets scattered all over the forum and hands them back to his master.

sentence: Post incendium miser senex reliquiās domūs suae lacrimāns colligēbat.
translation: After the fire the poor old man was gathering up what was left of his house in tears.

sentence: In Subūrā togam virīlem fīliō meō ex multīs dēligō.
translation: In the Subura I am picking out a man's toga for my son from a whole rack of them.

sentence: Cōnsul ex omnibus centuriōnibus fortissimōs ad lēgātiōnem dēligit.
translation: The consul selects the bravest of all the centurions for the mission.

sentence: Amīcōs paucōs sed fidēlēs dēlēgī, nec umquam mē paenituit.
translation: I chose a few loyal friends rather than many, and I have never regretted it.

sentence: Bovēs per Viam Appiam plaustrum amphorīs onerātum lentē vehunt.
translation: The oxen slowly haul a wagon loaded with wine jars along the Appian Way.

sentence: Ligna ex silvā asinō meō cotīdiē ad casam vehō.
translation: Every day I bring firewood down from the woods to my cottage on my donkey.

sentence: Tempestās nāvem, quae marmor Rōmam vehēbat, in saxa impulit.
translation: The storm drove the ship that was carrying marble to Rome onto the rocks.

sentence: Avia mea, iam gravis aetāte, hortum tamen cotīdiē fodit.
translation: My grandmother, weighed down by her years by now, still digs the garden every day.

sentence: Tīrōnēs in castra nōn ante septimum decimum aetātis annum recipiuntur.
translation: Recruits are not taken into camp before their seventeenth year of age.

sentence: Nostra aetās plūs aurī quam virtūtis habet, ut senēs queruntur.
translation: Our age has more gold in it than courage, as the old men keep complaining.

sentence: Initium annī novī apud nōs sacrificiō et cēnā longā celebrātur.
translation: At our house the start of the new year is celebrated with a sacrifice and a long dinner.

sentence: Magister nōbīs dīxit initium omnis operis difficillimum esse.
translation: The teacher told us that the beginning of any piece of work is the hardest part.

sentence: Ab initiō huic mercātōrī nōn crēdidī, et rēctē timuī.
translation: From the very start I did not trust that merchant, and I was right to worry.

sentence: Ad fīnem cēnae pater semper eandem fābulam dē bellō nārrat.
translation: At the end of dinner my father always tells the same story about the war.

sentence: Agricolae dē fīnibus agrōrum apud praetōrem diū contendēbant.
translation: The farmers argued before the praetor for ages about the boundaries of their fields.

sentence: Labōrum meōrum nūllus fīnis est, dum dominus tam avārus vīvit.
translation: There is no end to my labours as long as so greedy a master is alive.

sentence: Post lūdōs turba omnem amphitheātrī exitum diū obsēdit.
translation: After the games the crowd blocked every exit of the amphitheatre for a long while.

sentence: Nēmō in castrīs dē exitū obsidiōnis quicquam praedīcere audēbat.
translation: Nobody in the camp dared to say a word about how the siege would turn out.

sentence: Fābulae exitus multō fēlīcior fuit quam spectātōrēs timuerant.
translation: The play's ending turned out far happier than the audience had feared.

sentence: Ante adventum avunculī tōta domus ā servīs pūrgātur.
translation: Before my uncle's arrival the whole house is being cleaned by the slaves.

sentence: Adventū lēgātī novī tōtum oppidum ad portās convēnit.
translation: When the new governor arrived, the entire town gathered at the gates.

sentence: Fīliī adventus ē Britanniā mātrem per tōtam hiemem sollicitam recreāvit.
translation: Her son's arrival from Britain revived his mother, who had been anxious the whole winter.

sentence: Avus meus post cāsum in scālīs trēs mēnsēs ambulāre nōn potuit.
translation: After his fall on the stairs my grandfather could not walk for three months.

sentence: Cāsū in forō amīcum vīdī quem decem annōs nōn vīderam.
translation: By chance I ran into a friend in the forum whom I had not seen for ten years.

sentence: Nēmō tam fortis est ut omnēs cāsūs aequō animō ferat.
translation: Nobody is brave enough to bear every misfortune with a calm mind.

sentence: Post patris mortem fortūna familiae nostrae in peius mūtāta est.
translation: After my father's death our family's fortunes changed for the worse.

sentence: Dux mīlitibus dubitantibus clāmāvit fortūnam semper audācēs adiuvāre.
translation: The general shouted to his wavering soldiers that fortune always helps the bold.

sentence: Nēmō fortūnae diū cōnfīdat: hodiē favet, crās omnia aufert.
translation: Let nobody trust luck for long: today it smiles on you, tomorrow it takes everything away.

sentence: Frāter meus in decimā legiōne septem annōs sub Caesare mīlitāvit.
translation: My brother served seven years in the Tenth Legion under Caesar.

sentence: Senātus novam legiōnem hieme cōnscrīpsit, quia veterānī domum redīre cupiēbant.
translation: The senate enrolled a new legion over the winter, because the veterans wanted to go home.

sentence: Sine legiōne fīdā nūlla urbs diū tūta manēbit, ut opīnor.
translation: Without a loyal legion no city will stay safe for long, in my view.

sentence: Hodiē in castrīs pluit, et mīlitēs sub pellibus miserī sedent.
translation: It is raining in the camp today, and the soldiers sit wretchedly under their leather tents.

sentence: Prīmā lūce mīlitēs castrōrum portās aperuērunt et mercātōrēs admīsērunt.
translation: At first light the soldiers opened the camp gates and let the traders in.

sentence: Numquam castra tam trīstia vīdī quam illa quae post proelium relīquimus.
translation: I have never seen a camp as grim as the one we left after the battle.

sentence: Avus arma sua vetera super focum suspendit et nēminem tangere sinit.
translation: Grandfather hangs his old weapons above the hearth and lets nobody touch them.

sentence: Fabrī in officīnā tōtam noctem arma equitibus nostrīs parābant.
translation: The smiths in the workshop spent the whole night making weapons for our cavalry.

sentence: Ad arma cīvēs cōnsul vocāvit, sed bellum nēmō in forō cupiēbat.
translation: The consul called the citizens to arms, but nobody in the forum actually wanted war.

sentence: Pater gladium avītum lentē dētersit, priusquam eum fīliō trādidit.
translation: Father slowly wiped the ancestral sword clean before he handed it to his son.

sentence: Tīrōnēs in campō gladiīs ligneīs contrā pālum cotīdiē sē exercent.
translation: On the drill field the recruits train every day against a post with wooden swords.

sentence: Gladius meus, quem per decem annōs gessī, nunc frūstrā in arcā iacet.
translation: My sword, which I carried for ten years, now lies uselessly in a chest.

sentence: Puer hastam patris vix duābus manibus sustinēre poterat, tam gravis erat.
translation: The boy could barely hold his father's spear with both hands, it was so heavy.

sentence: Fētiālis hastam in fīnēs hostium iēcit et bellum rīte indīxit.
translation: The fetial priest hurled a spear into enemy territory and duly declared war.

sentence: Hastā per umerum trānsfīxus, mīles tacuit, nē comitēs terrērentur.
translation: Run through the shoulder by a spear, the soldier kept quiet so his comrades would not panic.

sentence: Puerī in hortō scūtīs ex tabulīs factīs inter sē pugnābant.
translation: The boys were fighting each other in the garden with shields made out of planks.

sentence: Mīlitēs scūta super capita sustulērunt et testūdinem sub mūrō fēcērunt.
translation: The soldiers raised their shields over their heads and formed a tortoise beneath the wall.

sentence: Sine scūtō ex proeliō rediit, et pater eum domum recipere nōluit.
translation: He came back from the battle without his shield, and his father refused to take him back into the house.

sentence: Vēnātor tēlum in aprum iēcit, sed manus eius propter frīgus tremēbat.
translation: The hunter threw his spear at the boar, but his hand was shaking from the cold.

sentence: Dēfēnsōrēs dē mūrīs dēnsissima tēla in hostēs appropinquantēs coniēcērunt.
translation: The defenders hurled a thick volley of missiles from the walls at the advancing enemy.

sentence: Nihil mē magis terret quam tēlum quod noctū per tenebrās volat.
translation: Nothing frightens me more than a missile flying through the dark at night.

sentence: Māter vulnus fīliī aquā et acētō lāvit, dum ille lacrimās retinēbat.
translation: The mother washed her son's wound with water and vinegar while he held back his tears.

sentence: Medicus castrōrum vulnera gravia sine quiēte tōtam noctem cūrāvit.
translation: The camp doctor treated the serious wounds all night without a break.
