sentence: Vulnus quod in Galliā accēpī hieme etiam nunc dolet.
translation: The wound I took in Gaul still hurts me every winter.

sentence: Tertium iam mēnsem pater domō abest, et māter cotīdiē epistulās exspectat.
translation: Father has been away from home for three months now, and mother waits for letters every day.

sentence: Hōc mēnse mercātor tōtam frūmentī cōpiam maiōre pretiō vēndidit.
translation: This month the merchant sold his entire stock of grain at a higher price.

sentence: Mēnsis Iānuārius mihi semper longissimus vidētur, quia sōl tam sērō oritur.
translation: January always feels like the longest month to me, because the sun rises so late.

sentence: Haec vīlla in colle iam per tria saecula eandem familiam aluit.
translation: This villa on the hill has supported the same family for three centuries now.

sentence: Nostrō saeculō hominēs plūra itinera faciunt quam avī nostrī umquam fēcērunt.
translation: In our age people travel more than our grandfathers ever did.

sentence: Ō saecula corrupta, in quibus pecūnia plūs quam virtūs valet!
translation: What a corrupt age, in which money counts for more than character!

sentence: Cotīdiē māne per scālās angustās in cēnāculum nostrum ascendō.
translation: Every morning I climb the narrow stairs up to our top-floor flat.

sentence: Tubā signum dante, mūrum castrōrum cum commīlitōnibus ascendō.
translation: When the trumpet gives the signal, I climb the camp wall with my fellow soldiers.

sentence: Quotiēns Capitōlium ascendō, memoria maiōrum nostrōrum animum meum movet.
translation: Every time I climb the Capitol, the memory of our ancestors stirs me.

sentence: Imbre subitō ortō, ad vīllam nostram per agrōs madidōs contendō.
translation: A sudden downpour has come on, and I am hurrying home to our farmhouse across the soaked fields.

sentence: Cum frātre meō dē hērēditāte patris apud praetōrem diū contendō.
translation: I have been fighting my brother over our father's estate before the praetor for a long time.

sentence: Omnibus vīribus contendō ut patris meī glōriam aliquandō aequem.
translation: I am striving with all my might to match my father's reputation one day.

sentence: Per angustās Subūrae viās plaustrum bōbus iūnctīs vix regō.
translation: Through the narrow streets of the Subura I can barely steer the ox-drawn cart.

sentence: Ipse nāvem inter scopulōs, cum ventus surgit, clāvō regō.
translation: When the wind gets up, I steer the ship through the rocks at the tiller myself.

sentence: Prōvinciam iūstē regō, quamquam multī mē nimis sevērum esse putant.
translation: I govern the province fairly, though plenty of people think me far too harsh.

sentence: Nē gelū pereant, rosās meās strāmentō per hiemem tegō.
translation: So the frost will not kill them, I cover my roses with straw all winter.

sentence: In aciē scūtō meō corpus amīcī vulnerātī fortiter tegō.
translation: In the battle line I stoutly cover my wounded friend's side with my shield.

sentence: Rīsū vultum tegō, nē quis dolōrem meum in convīviō sentiat.
translation: I hide my face behind a laugh, so that nobody at the dinner notices my grief.

sentence: Amphorās vīnō gravēs ex viā in tabernam patris trahō.
translation: I haul the wine-heavy jars in from the street into my father's shop.

sentence: Cum cēterīs servīs columnam marmoream ad forum novum trahō.
translation: Together with the other slaves I am dragging a marble column to the new forum.

sentence: Noctēs longās īnsomnēs trahō, dum dē fīliī perīculō cōgitō.
translation: I drag out long sleepless nights while I turn my son's danger over in my mind.

sentence: Ex aquaeductū novō aqua in lacum vīcī nostrī cotīdiē fluit.
translation: Water flows down from the new aqueduct into our neighbourhood basin every day.

sentence: Sarcinam gravem per Forum ferēns, tōtus sūdōre fluō.
translation: Carrying a heavy load across the Forum, I am streaming with sweat from head to foot.

sentence: Dum in exsiliō longō maneō, annī sine spē lentē fluunt.
translation: While I stay on in this long exile, the years flow slowly past without hope.

sentence: In vīllā avī nostrī inter olīvās et capellās crēscō.
translation: I am growing up on my grandfather's farm among the olive trees and the goats.

sentence: Postquam portus refectus est, urbis nostrae opēs cotīdiē crēscunt.
translation: Ever since the harbour was rebuilt, our city's wealth has been growing by the day.

sentence: Quō diūtius tacēs, eō magis in animō meō timor crēscit.
translation: The longer you say nothing, the more the fear grows inside me.

sentence: In balneīs pūblicīs senī tremulō locō meō statim cēdō.
translation: At the public baths I give up my place at once to a shaky old man.

sentence: In cūriā, cum argūmenta tua meliōra sint, tibi cēdō.
translation: Here in the senate house, since your arguments are the better ones, I yield to you.

sentence: Nēminī amīcōrum meōrum fidē cēdō, etiam sī pauper videor.
translation: I take second place to none of my friends in loyalty, poor as I may look.

sentence: Ad pistrīnum vīcīnum prīmā lūce accēdō, ubi pānis calidus fūmat.
translation: At first light I go over to the bakery next door, where the warm bread is steaming.

sentence: Māne ad patrōnī meī domum cum multīs clientibus accēdō.
translation: In the morning I approach my patron's house along with a crowd of other clients.

sentence: Post longam disceptātiōnem ad sententiam tuam accēdō, victus argūmentīs.
translation: After a long argument I come round to your view, beaten by your reasoning.

sentence: Ante lūcem ex casā tacitus discēdō, nē uxōrem dormientem excitem.
translation: Before daybreak I slip out of the cottage quietly, so as not to wake my sleeping wife.

sentence: Sōle occidente fessus ab officīnā discēdō et domum lentē eō.
translation: As the sun goes down I leave the workshop worn out and walk slowly home.

sentence: Ex hāc urbe, ubi tot annōs vīxī, invītus crās discēdō.
translation: Tomorrow I leave this city where I have lived so many years, and I go unwillingly.

sentence: Avō meō summus honor in pāgō est, quia templum suā pecūniā refēcit.
translation: My grandfather is held in the highest honor in the village, because he rebuilt the temple at his own expense.

sentence: Cicerō quaestūram suō annō petīvit, et populus eī hunc honōrem libenter dedit.
translation: Cicero stood for the quaestorship in his own year, and the people gladly gave him that office.

sentence: Mīlitēs sine praedā rediērunt, sed honōre victōriae nēmō eōs fraudāre poterat.
translation: The soldiers came home without any plunder, but nobody could cheat them of the honor of the victory.

sentence: Pater in familiā tantam potestātem habet ut nēmō eī resistere audeat.
translation: The father holds such power in the household that no one dares stand up to him.

sentence: Cōnsulī summa potestās erat, sed tribūnus eam ūnō verbō impedīre poterat.
translation: The consul held the highest power, yet a tribune could block it with a single word.

sentence: Postquam prōvinciam accēpit, potestāte suā abūsus est et sociōs graviter vexāvit.
translation: Once he took over the province, he abused his power and harassed the allies badly.

sentence: Avia nostra litterās nescit, sed magnam auctōritātem inter propinquōs habet.
translation: Our grandmother cannot read a word, but she carries great authority among the relatives.

sentence: Senātūs auctōritāte permōtus, cōnsul exercitum trāns flūmen dūcere dēstitit.
translation: Swayed by the senate's authority, the consul gave up leading the army across the river.

sentence: Nūlla auctōritās mihi vidētur maior quam eius quī numquam mentītus est.
translation: No authority seems greater to me than that of a man who has never lied.

sentence: Vīs tempestātis nāvem nostram tribus diēbus ad lītus Āfricae abstulit.
translation: The force of the storm carried our ship off to the African coast in three days.

sentence: Latrōnēs iānuam vī frēgērunt et omne argentum ex tablīnō abstulērunt.
translation: Robbers broke the door open by force and carried off all the silver from the study.

sentence: Nēmō vim adhibēre dēbet ubi ratiō et verba satis valent.
translation: Nobody should resort to violence where reason and words are enough.

sentence: Equitēs nostrī prīmā lūce impetum in hostium cornū sinistrum fēcērunt.
translation: At first light our cavalry charged the enemy's left wing.

sentence: Tantus flūminis impetus fuit ut pōns mediā nocte corruerit.
translation: The river came down with such force that the bridge collapsed in the middle of the night.

sentence: Prīmō impetū animī epistulam scrīpsit, quam posterō diē combussit.
translation: On a first rush of feeling he wrote the letter, and burned it the next day.

sentence: Hōc annō tanta frūmentī cōpia fuit ut prētium in forō caderet.
translation: There was such a glut of grain this year that the price dropped in the market.

sentence: Caesar cōpiās suās trāns Rhodanum trādūxit et castra in colle posuit.
translation: Caesar led his troops across the Rhône and pitched camp on a hill.

sentence: Mihi dīcendī cōpiam nōn dedistī, et tamen dē mē iūdicāvistī.
translation: You gave me no chance to speak, and yet you passed judgment on me.

sentence: Tanta multitūdō ad thermās vēnit ut in apodytēriō locus dēesset.
translation: Such a crowd came to the baths that there was no room left in the changing room.

sentence: Ōrātor ē rōstrīs multitūdinī persuāsit ut lēgem novam in comitiīs antīquāret.
translation: From the rostra the speaker talked the crowd into voting the new bill down at the assembly.

sentence: Multitūdinem hostium nōn timēmus, quia virtūs paucōrum saepe plūs valet.
translation: We do not fear the enemy's sheer numbers, because the courage of a few often counts for more.

sentence: Tantā turbā via Subūrae complēta erat ut lectīca mea cōnsisteret.
translation: The street in the Subura was so packed with people that my litter came to a standstill.

sentence: Puer per turbam macellī currēns pānem ē manibus meīs excussit.
translation: A boy running through the crowd at the market knocked the bread out of my hands.

sentence: Cum aurīga noster victōriam āmīsisset, ingēns turba in circō orta est.
translation: When our charioteer threw away the win, a huge uproar broke out in the circus.

sentence: Vīlicus numerum ovium cotīdiē recēnset, nē pāstor ūnam clam vēndat.
translation: The farm manager counts the sheep over every day, so that the shepherd cannot quietly sell one off.

sentence: Magnus numerus mīlitum in castrīs aegrōtābat, itaque lēgātus proelium distulit.
translation: A large number of the soldiers in camp were sick, so the legate put the battle off.

sentence: Tē in amīcōrum numerō semper habuī, etiam cum omnēs tacēbant.
translation: I have always counted you among my friends, even back when everyone else kept quiet.

sentence: Servus ante cēnam lucernās per tōtum triclīnium in ōrdinem disposuit.
translation: Before dinner the slave set the lamps out in a row all through the dining room.

sentence: Centuriō mīlitēs clāmōre revocāvit, quia ōrdinēs in mediō proeliō turbābantur.
translation: The centurion shouted the men back, because the ranks were breaking up in the middle of the fight.

sentence: Quamquam ex equestrī ōrdine ortus erat, populus eum senātōribus praetulit.
translation: Although he came from the equestrian order, the people preferred him to the senators.

sentence: Postquam fīlia mea nāvem cōnscendit, in lītore sōlus fleō.
translation: Now that my daughter has boarded the ship, I stand on the shore weeping alone.

sentence: In fūnere vīcīnī nostrī multī simulant, ego autem vērē fleō.
translation: At our neighbour's funeral plenty of people put on a show of grief, but I really weep.

sentence: Mē nōn pudet: cum Vergilium legō, dē Dīdōne semper fleō.
translation: I am not ashamed of it: whenever I read Vergil, I always weep over Dido.

sentence: Quotiēns avus meus fābulam dē asinō nārrat, per tōtam cēnam rīdeō.
translation: Every time my grandfather tells that story about the donkey, I laugh right through dinner.

sentence: In theātrō, dum servus callidus dominum fallit, cum tōtā turbā rīdeō.
translation: At the theatre, while the clever slave tricks his master, I laugh along with the whole crowd.

sentence: Amīcum in rēbus adversīs numquam rīdeō, quia ipse saepe errāvī.
translation: I never laugh at a friend when things go badly for him, because I have often gone wrong myself.

sentence: Dum pater dē lēgibus disputat, ego in angulō ātriī taceō.
translation: While my father argues about the laws, I keep quiet in the corner of the atrium.

sentence: In cūriā senātōrēs dē bellō clāmant; ego, quid dīcam nescius, taceō.
translation: In the senate house the senators are shouting about the war; not knowing what to say, I stay silent.

sentence: Etsī dominus servum iniūstē accūsat, timōre victus, miserē taceō.
translation: Even though the master is accusing the slave unjustly, fear gets the better of me and I shamefully say nothing.

sentence: Lucerna sum: dum domina epistulās longās scrībit, in cubiculō lūceō.
translation: I am a lamp: while my mistress writes her long letters, I shine in her bedroom.

sentence: Ante tabernāculum lēgātī excubō et hāc taedā tōtam noctem lūceō.
translation: I keep watch in front of the legate's tent and shine with this torch the whole night through.

sentence: Lūna sum: nautīs errantibus in tenebrīs clārē lūceō, sed nēmō mē laudat.
translation: I am the moon: I shine brightly in the dark for sailors who have lost their way, and not one of them praises me.

sentence: Cum uxor mea aegrōtet, iter Rōmam in aliud tempus differre cōnstituō.
translation: Since my wife is ill, I have decided to put the journey to Rome off to another time.

sentence: Ubi collis altus campum spectat, ibi castra hīberna cōnstituō.
translation: Where a high hill looks out over the plain, that is where I establish the winter camp.

sentence: Post tot iniūriās amīcō illī numquam iterum crēdere cōnstituō.
translation: After so many wrongs, I have made up my mind never to trust that friend again.

sentence: In ātriō nostrō novam āram Laribus manū meā statuō.
translation: In our atrium I am setting up a new altar to the household gods with my own hands.

sentence: In forō, priusquam dē contrōversiā vīcīnōrum statuō, utrumque testem audiō.
translation: In the forum, before I give a ruling on a quarrel between neighbours, I hear each witness out.

sentence: Statuō posthāc apud cēnam nihil dē amīcīs absentibus dīcere.
translation: I have resolved from now on to say nothing at dinner about friends who are not there.

sentence: Cum lupī dē montibus dēscendant, ovīle vallō altō mūniō.
translation: Now that wolves are coming down from the mountains, I am fortifying the sheepfold with a high palisade.

sentence: Ubi prīmum in fīnēs hostium veniō, castra fossā et vallō mūniō.
translation: The moment I reach enemy territory, I fortify the camp with a ditch and a rampart.

sentence: Animum meum contrā fortūnae impetūs philosophiā, nōn armīs, mūniō.
translation: I fortify my mind against the assaults of fortune with philosophy, not with weapons.

sentence: Fīlium meum, quī tabulam cērātam frēgit, hodiē sine īrā pūniō.
translation: Today I punish my son, who smashed his wax tablet, but I do it without anger.

sentence: In lūdō meō discipulum mendācem nōn ferulā sed silentiō pūniō.
translation: In my school I punish a lying pupil not with the cane but with silence.

sentence: Nēminem īrātus pūniō; prius enim īram meam, deinde culpam aliēnam exāminō.
translation: I never punish anyone while I am angry: I weigh my own temper first, and only then the other man's fault.

sentence: Cum sōl occidit, opus in agrō fīniō et domum lentē redeō.
translation: When the sun goes down I finish my work in the field and walk slowly home.

sentence: In forō ōrātiōnem meam brevī sententiā fīniō, nē iūdicēs fatīgem.
translation: In the forum I end my speech with one short maxim, so as not to wear the judges out.

sentence: Cupiditātēs meās ratiōne fīniō, nam nūlla dīvitiārum cōpia satis est.
translation: I set limits on my desires by reason, for no amount of riches is ever enough.

sentence: Māne per scālās angustās īnsulae nostrae ad tabernam pānis dēscendō.
translation: In the morning I go down the narrow stairs of our apartment block to the baker's shop.

sentence: Prīmā lūce dē Palātiō in forum ad amīcōs salūtandōs dēscendō.
translation: At first light I go down from the Palatine into the forum to pay my morning calls.

sentence: Quamquam adversārius mē fortior est, in certāmen tamen intrepidus dēscendō.
translation: Even though my opponent is stronger than I am, I still go down into the contest undaunted.

sentence: Ager noster, saxīs plēnus, frūmentō serendō minimē idōneus est.
translation: Our field is so full of stones that it is no good at all for sowing grain.

sentence: Centuriō dīxit hunc tīrōnem nōndum idōneum esse quī signum ferat.
translation: The centurion said this recruit was not yet fit to carry the standard.

sentence: Inter cēnam nūllum tempus idōneum ad rem gravem nūntiandam invēnī.
translation: All through dinner I never found the right moment to break the serious news.

sentence: Hieme ligna in casā necessāria sunt, nam ventus per rīmās intrat.
translation: In winter firewood is essential in the cottage, because the wind gets in through the cracks.

sentence: Ad iter per Alpēs faciendum dux plūrēs mūlōs necessāriōs esse cēnsuit.
translation: For the crossing of the Alps the general decided that more mules were needed.

sentence: Nōn opēs, sed amīcum fidēlem in adversīs rēbus necessārium esse crēdō.
translation: I believe that what you need when things go badly is a loyal friend, not money.

sentence: Vetus falx avī meī adhūc ūtilis est ad herbam in hortō secandam.
translation: My grandfather's old sickle still comes in handy for cutting the grass in the garden.

sentence: Servus quī Graecē loquitur dominō mercātōrī in portū ūtilis est.
translation: A slave who speaks Greek is useful to a merchant master down at the harbour.

sentence: Multa didicī in lūdō quae mihi posteā nūllō modō ūtilia fuērunt.
translation: I learned a great deal at school that afterwards turned out to be of no use to me at all.

sentence: Coquus noster tantam cēnam parāvit ut omnī laude dignus sit.
translation: Our cook put on such a dinner that he deserves every bit of praise.

sentence: Senātus eum virum honōre dignum iūdicāvit quod agrōs suōs pauperibus dedit.
translation: The senate judged the man worthy of honour because he gave his land to the poor.

sentence: Nihil in tōtō librō inveniō quod dignum sit tam longā vigiliā.
translation: In the whole book I can find nothing worth staying up this late for.

sentence: Frāter meus, quī cotīdiē mentītur, fidē nostrā indignus mihi vidētur.
translation: My brother lies every single day, and to my mind he no longer deserves our trust.

sentence: Mīlitēs in castrīs clāmāvērunt ducem timidum imperiō indignum esse.
translation: In camp the soldiers shouted that their cowardly commander did not deserve his command.

sentence: Indignum est cīvēs Rōmānōs in forō sine causā catēnīs vincīrī.
translation: It is an outrage for Roman citizens to be put in chains in the forum with no charge against them.

sentence: Taurus ferōx per viās oppidī cucurrit et omnēs mercātōrēs fūgērunt.
translation: A wild bull ran through the streets of the town and every trader took to his heels.

sentence: Ferōcēs Germānōrum equitēs prīmā lūce vallum nostrum in silvā oppugnāvērunt.
translation: At first light fierce German horsemen attacked our rampart in the forest.

sentence: Puer, quamquam corpore parvus, animō tam ferōx erat ut nēminem timēret.
translation: Small as the boy was, he had such nerve that he was afraid of nobody.

sentence: Cultrum ācrem in mēnsā relīquī, et coquus sibi digitum secuit.
translation: I left the sharp knife lying on the table, and the cook cut his finger on it.

sentence: Iūdex ācrī ingeniō statim intellēxit testem in forō falsa dīcere.
translation: The judge was quick-witted enough to see at once that the witness was lying in court.

sentence: Ācer dolor in genū mē tōtā nocte dormīre nōn sinēbat.
translation: A sharp pain in my knee kept me from sleeping the whole night through.

sentence: Dominus crūdēlis servō aegrō nūllum cibum per trēs diēs dedit.
translation: The cruel master gave the sick slave nothing to eat for three days.

sentence: Tyrannus lēgēs tam crūdēlēs tulit ut multī cīvēs ex urbe fugerent.
translation: The tyrant passed such cruel laws that many citizens fled the city.

sentence: Crūdēle mihi vidētur avem in caveā parvā per tōtam vītam tenēre.
translation: Keeping a bird in a tiny cage for its whole life strikes me as cruel.

sentence: Hōc annō hiems tam mītis fuit ut rosae mēnse Iānuāriō flōrērent.
translation: This year the winter was so mild that the roses were in bloom in January.

sentence: Dominus noster in servōs mītis est, quamquam vīlicus saevē imperat.
translation: Our master is gentle with the slaves, even though the overseer gives his orders harshly.

sentence: Post longum iter vīnum mīte et umbra platanī mē recreāvērunt.
translation: After the long journey a mellow wine and the shade of a plane tree brought me back to life.

sentence: In summā arbore nīdus est, quem puerī tangere nōn possunt.
translation: There is a nest at the very top of the tree, where the boys cannot reach it.

sentence: Summā cum cūrā scrība tabulās dominī ante lūcem cōnfēcit.
translation: The clerk finished his master's accounts before dawn with the greatest care.

sentence: Summus mihi timor erat nē pater epistulam meam legeret.
translation: My greatest fear was that my father would read my letter.

sentence: Avia mea ad focum sedēns dē fātō familiae nostrae saepe nārrābat.
translation: My grandmother would sit by the hearth and tell us about our family's fate.

sentence: Nauta in tempestāte fātum suum Neptūnō commendāvit et fūnem tenuit.
translation: In the storm the sailor commended his fate to Neptune and held on to the rope.

sentence: Fātum meum nōn queror, quia nēmō diem mortis suae mūtāre potest.
translation: I don't complain about my fate, since nobody can change the day of his own death.

sentence: Māter dōnum sub lectō cēlat, nē fīlia ante diem nātālem inveniat.
translation: Mother is hiding the present under the bed so her daughter won't find it before her birthday.

sentence: Ad nūptiās amīca mea dōnum argenteum attulit, quod omnēs mīrātī sunt.
translation: My friend brought a silver gift to the wedding, and everyone admired it.

sentence: Puer dōnum aviae rīsit, sed māter eum statim tacēre iussit.
translation: The boy laughed at his grandmother's gift, but his mother told him at once to be quiet.

sentence: Magister puerō praemium dedit, quod versūs Vergiliī sine errōre recitāvit.
translation: The teacher gave the boy a prize because he recited Vergil's lines without a single mistake.

sentence: Dux mīlitibus praemia magna prōmīsit, sī hostium castra prīmī cēpissent.
translation: The general promised the soldiers large rewards if they were the first to take the enemy camp.

sentence: Nūllum praemium petō; satis est mihi amīcōs meōs incolumēs vidēre.
translation: I'm not after any reward; it's enough for me to see my friends come home safe.

sentence: Prō amphorā frāctā poena mea fuit tōtum hortum sōlus purgāre.
translation: For the jar I broke, my punishment was weeding the whole garden by myself.

sentence: Iūdex fūrī poenam gravem cōnstituit, quamquam multī cīvēs veniam petēbant.
translation: The judge set a heavy penalty for the thief, even though many citizens were begging for mercy.

sentence: Frātrem meum prōdidī, et adhūc poenās in animō meō dō.
translation: I betrayed my brother, and I am still paying the penalty in my own mind.

sentence: Māne vīcīnī clāmāvērunt scelus nocte in Subūrā commissum esse.
translation: In the morning the neighbours were shouting that a crime had been committed in the Subura overnight.

sentence: Cicerō in senātū tōtum coniūrātōrum scelus patefēcit et cīvitātem servāvit.
translation: In the senate Cicero laid bare the conspirators' whole crime and saved the state.

sentence: Tantī sceleris numquam oblīvīscar, etiamsī cēterī iam ignōvērunt.
translation: I will never forget a crime that great, even if everyone else has already forgiven it.

sentence: Nōn est culpa canis, sī iānuam apertam tōtam noctem relīquistī.
translation: It's not the dog's fault if you left the door open all night.

sentence: Vīlicus culpam in servōs contulit, quamquam ipse vīnum neglēxerat.
translation: The farm manager shifted the blame onto the slaves, though he was the one who had neglected the wine.

sentence: Meā culpā amīcitiam veterem perdidī, et nunc nēmō mihi crēdit.
translation: Through my own fault I lost an old friendship, and now nobody trusts me.

sentence: Vīcīna mea crīmen fūrtī mihi obiēcit, quia gallīnae meae hortum eius vāstant.
translation: My neighbour has charged me with theft, because my hens keep wrecking her garden.

sentence: Reus in forō stetit, dum accūsātor crīmina gravissima recitat.
translation: The defendant stood there in the forum while the prosecutor read out the gravest charges.

sentence: Nūllum crīmen probāre potuērunt, sed fāma mea iam periit.
translation: They could not prove a single charge, but my good name is already gone.

sentence: Vīcīnus aquam nostram āvertit, et haec iniūria tōtum vīcum offendit.
translation: Our neighbour has diverted our water, and this injustice has upset the whole street.

sentence: Mercātor iniūriam sibi ā pūblicānīs illātam apud praetōrem questus est.
translation: The merchant complained before the praetor about the wrong the tax collectors had done him.

sentence: Iniūriae tuae ignōscere possum, sed silentium tuum adhūc mē vulnerat.
translation: I can forgive the wrong you did me, but your silence still hurts.

sentence: Cum aegrōtārem, vīcīna nōbīs pānem cotīdiē ferēbat; beneficium magnum fuit.
translation: While I was ill the woman next door brought us bread every day; it was a great kindness.

sentence: Beneficiō patrōnī meī locum in cohorte urbānā tandem accēpī.
translation: Thanks to my patron's good offices I finally got a place in the city cohort.

sentence: Beneficia accipere facile est; reddere autem multō difficilius mihi vidētur.
translation: Accepting favours is easy; paying them back seems to me much harder.

sentence: Hospitī prō cēnā grātiās ēgimus et in viam ante lūcem exiimus.
translation: We thanked our host for dinner and set out on the road before daybreak.

sentence: Senātor grātiam populī quaerēbat, et ideō lūdōs magnificōs dedit.
translation: The senator was courting the people's favour, and so he put on magnificent games.

sentence: Medicō, quī fīliam meam sānāvit, grātiam parem referre numquam poterō.
translation: I will never be able to thank the doctor who cured my daughter as he deserves.

sentence: Scālārum gradus īnfimus semper ūmidus est, itaque cautē dēscendimus.
translation: The bottom step of the stairs is always damp, so we go down carefully.

sentence: Mercātor mihi olīvās īnfimī pretiī vēndidit, sed eās optimās esse iūrābat.
translation: The trader sold me the cheapest olives, but swore they were the finest.

sentence: Quamquam īnfimō locō nātus erat, nēmō in cūriā eum contempsit.
translation: Although he had been born in the lowest station, nobody in the senate house looked down on him.

sentence: In mediā nocte canis lātrāvit, et tōta domus perterrita surrēxit.
translation: In the middle of the night the dog barked, and the whole household got up in fright.

sentence: Ōrātor in mediō forō stetit et tōtam turbam tacēre iussit.
translation: The speaker stood in the middle of the forum and ordered the whole crowd to be quiet.

sentence: Media aestās Rōmae intolerābilis est, itaque omnēs ad mare fugiunt.
translation: Midsummer in Rome is unbearable, so everyone escapes to the sea.

sentence: Avia in extrēmā parte hortī sedet, ubi fīcus umbram praebet.
translation: Grandmother sits at the far end of the garden, where the fig tree gives shade.

sentence: Extrēmō diē mēnsis mercēdem accēpimus, sed dominus nummōs paucōs dedit.
translation: On the last day of the month we were paid, but the master handed over only a few coins.

sentence: Nāvis nostra ad extrēmam ōram Britanniae pervēnit, ubi omnēs mīlitēs timēbant.
translation: Our ship reached the outermost coast of Britain, where every soldier was afraid.

sentence: Vīcīnus proximus noctū canēs solvit, ideō dormīre numquam possumus.
translation: The neighbour next door lets his dogs loose at night, so we can never sleep.

sentence: Frūmentum in proximum oppidum vehēmus, quod hīc nūllum forum est.
translation: We will cart the grain to the nearest town, because there is no market here.

sentence: Proximā aestāte ad vīllam avunculī ībimus, sī pater pecūniam habēbit.
translation: Next summer we will go out to my uncle's villa, if father has the money.

sentence: Tabulātum superius nostrae īnsulae semper aestāte calidum est, itaque in tēctō dormīmus.
translation: The upper floor of our apartment block is always hot in summer, so we sleep on the roof.

sentence: Hostēs locum superiōrem occupāvērunt, itaque dux noster signum receptuī dedit.
translation: The enemy seized the higher ground, so our commander gave the signal to retreat.

sentence: Superiōre annō frūmentum vīlius erat, sed nunc omnia in macellō cāriōra sunt.
translation: Last year grain was cheaper, but now everything in the market costs more.

sentence: Cella īnferior post imbrem plēna aquae erat, itaque vīnum sūrsum tulimus.
translation: The lower cellar was full of water after the downpour, so we carried the wine upstairs.

sentence: Nautae per īnferiōrem flūminis partem nāvigant, ubi aqua altior est.
translation: The boatmen sail along the lower stretch of the river, where the water runs deeper.

sentence: Frāter meus in ōrdine īnferiōre mīlitat, sed plūs stīpendiī quam ego accipit.
translation: My brother serves in a lower rank, and yet he draws more pay than I do.

sentence: Ūniversa familia ad vīllam avī migrāvit, cum pestilentia in urbe esset.
translation: The entire household moved out to grandfather's villa when plague was in the city.

sentence: Mercātor ūniversam mercem ūnō diē vēndidit et domum laetus rediit.
translation: The trader sold his whole stock in a single day and went home delighted.

sentence: Ūniversī cīvēs lēgem novam laudāvērunt, sed singulī domī querēbantur.
translation: All the citizens together praised the new law, but individually they grumbled at home.

sentence: Avia mea crēdit nūmen in hōc antīquō fonte habitāre.
translation: My grandmother believes that a divine power lives in this old spring.

sentence: Nautae ante lūcem nūmen maris precantur, deinde nāvēs solvunt.
translation: Before dawn the sailors pray to the power of the sea, and then they cast off.

sentence: Post proelium mīlitēs victōriam nūminī, nōn ducī suō, tribuēbant.
translation: After the battle the soldiers credited the victory to a god's power rather than to their own commander.

sentence: Ante iter pater noster sacrificium parvum Laribus in ātriō fēcit.
translation: Before the journey our father made a small sacrifice to the household gods in the atrium.

sentence: Pontifex sacrificium parābat, cum taurus subitō ē manibus servōrum fūgit.
translation: The priest was getting the sacrifice ready when the bull suddenly broke loose from the slaves' hands.

sentence: Sacrificium nostrum deae nōn placuisse putō, quod pluvia adhūc nōn vēnit.
translation: I think our sacrifice did not please the goddess, since the rain still has not come.

sentence: Māter nostra cotīdiē flōrēs et lac in ārā domesticā pōnit.
translation: Every day our mother lays flowers and milk on the household altar.

sentence: Ante ārām Vestae virginēs ignem sacrum tōtā nocte custōdiunt.
translation: Before the altar of Vesta the virgins guard the sacred fire all night long.

sentence: Ārae in agrīs relictae iam frīgidae sunt, quia nēmō sacra cūrat.
translation: The altars left standing in the fields are cold now, because nobody tends the rites any more.

sentence: Nūtrīx vetus tōtī familiae nostrae cāra est, quamquam iam nihil labōrat.
translation: The old nurse is dear to our whole household, even though she no longer does any work.

sentence: In macellō piscēs hodiē tam cārī erant ut nihil emerēmus.
translation: At the market the fish were so expensive today that we bought nothing at all.

sentence: Nūllum dōnum mātrī cārius fuit quam epistula fīliī ē castrīs missa.
translation: No gift was dearer to my mother than the letter her son sent from camp.

sentence: Post longum iter umbra platanī et aqua frīgida nōbīs grātae erant.
translation: After the long journey the shade of the plane tree and the cold water were very welcome to us.

sentence: Lībertus patrōnō suō grātus erat, et eum cotīdiē māne salūtābat.
translation: The freedman was grateful to his patron, and greeted him at his door every morning.

sentence: Nūllus mihi sonus grātior est quam clāmor puerōrum in viā lūdentium.
translation: No sound pleases me more than the shouting of boys playing out in the street.

sentence: Pecūniam sub lectō cēlāvimus, quod nūllus locus in īnsulā tūtus est.
translation: We hid the money under the bed, because no spot in the tenement is safe.

sentence: Mercātōrēs hieme nāvigāre nōlunt, quia mare tunc minimē tūtum est.
translation: Merchants refuse to sail in winter, because at that season the sea is anything but safe.

sentence: Tūtius est domī manēre quam nocte per Subūram sōlum ambulāre.
translation: It is safer to stay at home than to walk alone through the Subura at night.

sentence: Servum certum quaerimus, cui clāvēs et omnem pecūniam committāmus.
translation: We are looking for a reliable slave, someone we can hand the keys and all the money to.

sentence: Magister discipulīs certam hōram dīxit, sed nēmō ad tempus vēnit.
translation: The teacher set the pupils a fixed hour, but nobody turned up on time.

sentence: Nihil certī dē fīliō scīmus, quia nūlla epistula ex Britanniā vēnit.
translation: We know nothing definite about our son, because not one letter has come from Britain.

sentence: Coquus incertus stābat, quod dominus numquam dīxerat quot convīvae venīrent.
translation: The cook stood there at a loss, because the master had never said how many guests were coming.

sentence: Nautae incertō caelō ē portū exīre nōlēbant, quamquam mercēs iam impositae erant.
translation: With the sky so unsettled the sailors would not leave harbour, even though the cargo was already loaded.

sentence: Iuvenis incertus erat utrum philosophiam an rem mīlitārem sequerētur.
translation: The young man could not make up his mind whether to follow philosophy or a military career.

sentence: Avī nostrī valētūdō tam dubia est ut medicum cotīdiē vocēmus.
translation: Our grandfather's health is so precarious that we send for the doctor every day.

sentence: Proelium diū dubium fuit, dōnec equitēs nostrī ā dextrā vēnērunt.
translation: The battle hung in the balance for a long time, until our cavalry came up on the right.

sentence: Puella dubiō vultū dōnum accēpit, quod ā iuvene ignōtō missum erat.
translation: The girl took the gift with a doubtful look, because it had been sent by a young man she did not know.

sentence: Hī calceī puerō nōn sunt aptī, quod nimis lātī et gravēs sunt.
translation: These shoes are not right for the boy, because they are too wide and too heavy.

sentence: Dux locum castrīs aptum prope flūmen invēnit et mīlitēs fossam fodere iussit.
translation: The general found a place suitable for a camp near the river and ordered the soldiers to dig a ditch.

sentence: Nēmō mihi vidētur ad hoc negōtium aptior quam frāter tuus.
translation: Nobody strikes me as better suited to this job than your brother.
